These wheels, moreover, have not only fleshes, or a body, or members, but also necks, hands and wings, so that in each of these we may perceive the workings of things, not images of members.

Wherefore those who are over others are to be admonished, that through earnestness of circumspection they have eyes watchful within and round about, and strive to become living creatures of heaven. For the living creatures of heaven are described as full of eyes round about and within. And so it is meet that those who are over others should have eyes within and round about, so as both in themselves to study to please the inward judge, and also, affording outwardly examples of life, to detect the things that should be corrected in others.

Subjects are to be admonished that they judge not rashly the lives of their superiors, if perchance they see them act blamably in anything, lest whence they rightly find fault with evil they thence be sunk by the impulse of elation to lower depths. […]

10:13.t: The 'wheels' themselves, too, are called in the Hebrew tongue 'gelgel', which Symmachus translated 'whirling' and Aquila 'wheel'.

Do you want to know how the ends of the earth see God? We read in Ezekiel: 'And those wheels,' he says, 'which are turned, were called gelgel,' which means 'revelation, revelation.' For GEL means 'revelation,' GELGEL 'revelation, revelation.' Those wheels then hear 'revelation, revelation': because the wheel touches the earth as it were only at some small point, and the whole of it hastens toward heaven. Therefore it is said also in another place: 'Holy stones are rolled upon the earth.' And what is said in Ezekiel? 'Wherever,' he says, 'the spirit went, thither the wheels also followed.' Let us too follow the Holy Spirit, and let us be called wheels. And what is said there? 'And they went not,' he says, 'backward, but always went forward.' And at the same time consider what he says. 'They did not turn back,' he says, 'but always went forward.' For they forgot the things that were past, and reached out toward the things before them. 'And they were full,' he says, 'of eyes.' […]
Further, what follows: In my hearing, up to the place where it is written: The Cherubim were lifted up, is not found in the Seventy but has been added from the Hebrew.

10:14.t: In this it must be observed that it is by no means as is said above: The face of a man, and the face of a lion four, and the face of a calf on the left four, and the face of an eagle four on the right, so that, of course, some might be believed to be on the left and others on the right; rather, an equal order of them all is described, as Scripture says: Now one had four faces: the one face the face of a Cherub, and the second face the face of a man, and in the third the face of a lion, and in the fourth the face of an eagle, so that the first and second and third and fourth face is described not by a difference of place, right and left, but in a single order, by degrees. Now the one face, that is, the first, he called Cherub, where above he had said the face of a calf; from which it is understood that the face of a Cherub is the face of a calf. The sense of all these things is contained in the explanation of the former vision.

10:15.t: But as for what is said: This is the living creature that I had seen beside the river Chebar, Scripture shows that in the exposition of the living creature we ought to understand the same things that we understood above.

10:17.t: This is the living creature that I had seen beside the river Chebar. And when the Cherubim went, the wheels also went alongside them; and when the Cherubim lifted their wings to be raised up from the earth, the wheels did not hold back, but they too were beside them. When those stood, these stood, and when those were lifted up, these were lifted up, for the spirit of life was in them. All things live to God and perceive their own Creator: He is not, you see, the God of the dead, but of the living. Hence also all the bodies of the wheels are full of eyes. And in the psalm it is said: The heavens tell the works of God, and the firmament proclaims the works of his hands. Day to day pours forth a word, and night to night shows knowledge; […]

10:18.t: I linger long in the land of the midday sun, for it was there and then that the spouse found her bridegroom at rest and Joseph drank wine with his brothers once more. I will return to Jerusalem and, passing through Tekoa the home of Amos, I will look on the glistening cross of Mount Olive from which the Savior made his ascension to the Father. Here year by year a red heifer was burned as an offering to the Lord, and its ashes were used to purify the children of Israel. Here also according to Ezekiel the cherubim after leaving the temple founded the church of the Lord.

And the glory of the Lord went out from the threshold of the temple, and stood above the Cherubim; and the Cherubim, lifting their wings, were raised up from the earth before me, and as they went out the wheels also followed; and it stood at the entrance of the eastern gate of the house of the Lord, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them. This is the living creature that I saw beneath the God of Israel beside the river Chebar, and I understood that they were Cherubim. Four by four faces to one, and four wings to one, and the likeness of a man's hand under their wings; and the likeness of their faces, the very faces that I had seen beside the river Chebar, and their gaze, and the onrush of each to go forward before its face. […]

10:20.t: When the prophet had seen this: This is, he says, the living creature that I saw beneath the God of Israel beside the river Chebar, and I understood that they were Cherubim. For what new thing did he see, that he should understand that they were Cherubim, which he had not understood before? 'Cherubim' in our language is 'multitude of knowledge', the knowledge of the mysteries of God, and his throne and resting place; hence also in the psalm it is said: You who sit upon the Cherubim, be made manifest; for the glory of the Lord always sits in the multitude of knowledge, and it is made manifest then: when all things are shown to be ruled by providence, and nothing to happen by chance, and no one to say: The Lord has forsaken the earth, and the Lord does not see; hence also the gaze of the Cherubim and their desire is to forget the things that are past and to stretch themselves forward to the things to come.

11:1.t: And the spirit lifted me up, and brought me in to the eastern gate of the house of the Lord, which looks toward the rising of the sun. Since the glory of the Lord had gone forth from the threshold of the temple and stood above the Cherubim, and afterward, as the Cherubim flew away, the glory itself stood at the entrance of the eastern gate of the house of the Lord, the prophet too — he could not go to it by himself — was lifted up by the spirit and led to the same eastern gate of the house of the Lord, which looks toward the sun of righteousness, of whom it is written: Behold a man, the Orient is his name, so that he should by no means remain in the temple, which was confounded by the cloud of ignorance, but, standing in the gate of the house of the Lord on the east, might come to know the mysteries that follow.

And behold, at the entrance of the gate twenty-five men, and I saw in their midst Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people. And he said to me: Son of man, these are the men who devise iniquity, and handle a most wicked counsel in this city, saying: Were not the houses built long ago? This is the cauldron, and we are the flesh. Therefore prophesy concerning them; prophesy, son of man. And the spirit of the Lord rushed upon me and said to me: Speak. Thus says the Lord: So have you spoken, house of Israel, and the thoughts of your heart I know. You have killed very many in this city, and you have filled its streets with the slain. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Your slain, whom you have laid in its midst, they are the flesh, and this is the cauldron; and I will bring you out of its midst. You have feared the sword, and the sword I will bring upon you, says the Lord God. […]

And since what is said is plain according to the letter, setting aside for a little while the names of Jaazaniah and Azur, Pelatiah and Benaiah, which we reserve for another time, this must be said: that to this day in the Church, which is the house of God, both before the eastern gate and at the entrance, or in the way, of the gate, which signifies the Savior, through whom we enter to the Father, there are twenty-five men, referring all things to the senses — and, so far as it does not escape my memory, I have never been able to find this number in a good sense, although in Leviticus men are chosen for the priestly ministry from twenty-five years of age; for in the Hebrew it does not have this number which is given in the Seventy, but the number thirty, which is contained in the opening of this prophet and in the age of the Lord when he came to the streams of the Jordan and was baptized by John; […]

11:2.t: These, then, who were at the entrance of the eastern gate of the house of the Lord, despairing of salvation and, from the consciousness of their crimes, ready for destruction, and unwilling to correct their sins through repentance, say: 'Although the houses which had earlier collapsed have lately, after the first captivity, been built, yet we know that this city is like a cauldron and we are for flesh, so that in it we may be consumed and burned up together, according to what is written in Isaiah: The tempest, if it passes through, will not take us'.

There are many at the entrance of this gate, before the eastern house of the Lord, who by their vices are compared to the nations, and from the consciousness of their sins despair of salvation, and say: 'The city in which we dwell is a cauldron, and we are all flesh, and we shall be consumed by the Babylonian burning, whose darts are fiery', unwilling to do penance and despairing of salvation; therefore they hear that they themselves are not the flesh of the past and lost city, but those whom they have scandalized, whom they have killed; and for that reason the sword is brought upon them: so that, after they have been judged in the borders of Israel, by no means among the nations but among Christians, then they may know that he himself is the Lord, according to what is read in the Psalms: When he slew them, they sought him, so that him whom they had not perceived through benefits, they may come to know through torments.

11:4.t: As they say these things, the spirit of the Lord rushed upon the prophet, and commanded him a second time to prophesy and to say: 'Since you have said these things, and the secrets of your hearts do not escape me, I will interpret to you how the city is to be reckoned a cauldron and you flesh, not according to the sense in which you spoke, but according to another which you do not fear: the city is indeed in the likeness of a cauldron, but it will not be filled with your flesh, but with that of those whom you have killed; you, however, who think that you will die in this city, I will bring out of the midst of the city and hand over into the hands of enemies, and I will execute judgments upon you, so that, when you have fallen by the sword, by no means in the city nor outside the bounds of Israel but in the borders of your own province, then too you may know that I am the Lord'.

11:11.t: And a second time it is said: 'In the borders of Israel I will judge you, and you shall know that I am the Lord; and all these things you will suffer, because you have not walked in my precepts and have not done my judgments, but have wrought the crimes of the other nations round about'.

11:13.t: And it came to pass, while I was prophesying, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died; and I fell on my face, crying out with a loud voice, and I said: Alas, alas, alas, Lord God, you are making a consummation of the remnant of Israel. As the prophet prophesies, one of the two princes, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, dies, whose name means 'a fall turning aside', and he is the son of a 'builder' or 'mason' — for οἰκοδόμος cannot be rendered into our language otherwise —; the other of the princes, Jaazaniah, is kept safe — Jaazaniah signifies 'his ear', by which 'of the soul' is understood; Azur, however, 'support' or 'help' —. He, then, who by falling had turned aside from the Lord and was of a most wicked building, rightly falls while he whom God strengthened is prophesying; […]

11:14.t: The word of the Lord, therefore, came to Ezekiel, who had said: Alas, alas, alas, Lord God, you are making a consummation of the remnant of Israel, namely in the death of Pelatiah and of those who were killed with him: that by no means were those the remnant which the prophet supposed in Jerusalem, but those who were seen to be captives in Babylon; and the sense is: 'O son of man, your brothers, begotten of the same stock with you, your brothers, I say, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said: You have gone away from the Lord, because you are captives and have handed yourselves over with Jeconiah, but to us the land of Israel has been given for an everlasting possession — say, therefore, to them that I have indeed made them far off from the land of Israel and dispersed them into the nations and ordered them to be in foreign lands, but, because they have obeyed my command, I shall be among them, even in strange and hostile places, for a little sanctification, while very many are found among them who by no means […]

11:15.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, your brothers, your brothers, the men your kinsmen and the whole house of Israel, all to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said: Go far away from the Lord; to us the land has been given for a possession. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because I have made them far off among the nations, and because I have scattered them into the land, I will be to them for a small sanctification in the lands to which they have come. (LXX: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, your brothers, your brothers and the men of your captivity and the whole house of Israel is consummated, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said: You have gone far away from the Lord; to us the land has been given for an inheritance. Therefore say: Adonai the Lord says: Because I will drive them away into the nations, and I will sow them abroad into every land, and I will be to them for a little sanctification in the regions into which they shall have entered there.") […]

11:16.t:
[Passage quoted, Ezek. xi. 16.]

And here he has called the same men by another name, meaning by "a little sanctuary," those of them who shall be saved and survive.
11:16.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

11:17.t: Therefore speak: Thus says the Lord God: I will gather you from the peoples, and I will assemble you from the lands in which you have been scattered, and I will give you the soil of Israel. And they shall enter there, and shall take away all the offenses, and all the abominations from it; and I will give them one heart (or another), and a new spirit I will bestow, in their inward parts; and I will take away the stony heart from their flesh, and I will give them a heart of flesh, that they may walk in my precepts, and keep my judgments and do them, and be to me for a people and I be to them for God. But those whose heart walks after their stumbling blocks and their abominations, their way I will set upon their own head, says the Lord God. The divine word speaks to those who were captives in the land of Babylon, and to the brothers of Ezekiel the prophet and to his kinsmen, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said: You have gone far away from the Lord; to us the land has been given for a possession; […]

11:19.t: Behold, therefore, we have been refashioned, as again He says in another prophet, "Behold, saith the Lord, I will take away from these, that is, from those whom the Spirit of the Lord foresaw, their stony hearts, and I will put hearts of flesh within them," because He was to be manifested in flesh, and to sojourn among us.
11:19.s: The Epistle of Barnabas, Chapter VI

11:19.t: Otherwise, as it is written: "And I will take away from them the heart of stone, and I will give them a heart of flesh," that is, a soft one, with which they may be able to receive the law of God. For unless someone turns from his hardness, and becomes soft, he cannot receive food, and the bread which came down from heaven, so that he may be able to say: "Give us this day our supersubstantial bread," that is, the bread which is of your substance. In the Hebrew Gospel according to Matthew it has thus: "Give us this day our bread for tomorrow," that is, the bread which you are going to give us in your kingdom, give us today.

Now if faith is simply of free will, and is not given by God, why do we pray for those who will not believe, that they may believe? This it would be absolutely useless to do, unless we believe, with perfect propriety, that Almighty God is able to turn to belief wills that are perverse and opposed to faith. Man's free will is addressed when it is said, "Today, if ye will hear His voice, harden not your hearts." But if God were not able to remove from the human heart even its obstinacy and hardness, He would not say, through the prophet, "I will take from them their heart of stone, and will give them a heart of flesh." That all this was foretold in reference to the New Testament is shown clearly enough by the apostle when he says, "Ye are our epistle, . . . written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshly tables of the heart." We must not, of course, suppose that such a phrase as this is used as if those might live in a fleshly way who ought to live spiritually; […]
11:19.s: On Grace and Free Will, Chapter 29

11:22.t:
And this Mount of Olives is said to be over against Jerusalem, because it was established by God after the fall of Jerusalem, instead of the old earthly Jerusalem and its worship. For as Scripture said above with reference to Jerusalem: "The city shall be taken, and the nations that are her enemies and foes shall be gathered together against her, and her spoils shall be divided," it could not say that the feet of the Lord should stand upon Jerusalem. How could that be, once it were destroyed? But it says that they will stand with them that depart from it to the mount opposite the city called the Mount of Olives. And this, too, the prophet Ezekiel anticipates by the Holy Spirit and foretells. For he says:

"22. And the Cherubim lifted their wings, and the wheels beside them, 23. and the glory of the God of Israel was on them above them, and he stood on the mount which was opposite to the city." […]
11:22.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 6, Chapter 18

11:22.t: And the Cherubim lifted up their wings, and the wheels with them, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them; the glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain which is to the east of the city. Little by little the glory of the Lord withdraws from Jerusalem: first, deserting the temple, it stands in the court or at the threshold of the house, and afterward at the entrance of the eastern gate; lastly, its wings lifted and the wheels following, it stands upon the mountain which is to the east of the city — no doubt it signifies the Mount of Olives, from which the Savior ascended to the Father; and the glory of the Lord, which had departed from the city of Jerusalem, stood upon the Mount of Olives as a sign of resurrection and of light, so that from there it might behold Jerusalem about to perish and about to burn —.

11:23.t: And as for his saying: The glory went up from the midst of the city, in other words the Lord speaks to the disciples: Arise, let us go hence, and to the Jews: Your house will be left to you desolate; Josephus also relates that there was heard in the temple a voice of the angels and of the heavenly strength, which had previously been the city's defense: Let us go away from these seats. And, in a wondrous manner, to the present day the glory of the Lord, which deserted the temple, stands upon the Mount of Olives and, gleaming in the sign of the cross, looks upon the once Jewish temple, dissolved into embers and ashes.

11:24.t: And the spirit lifted me up, and brought me into Chaldea, to the exile, in a vision, in the spirit of God; and the vision which I had seen was taken away from me. And I spoke to the exile all the words of the Lord which he had shown me. Where we translated from the Hebrew truth: And the vision which I had seen was taken away from me, the Seventy translated: And I went up from the vision which I had seen; and both signify that the prophet was carried over to Jerusalem from Babylon not in the body but in the spirit, and, when the vision had been taken away which had led him in the spirit to Jerusalem and had shown him all the things which the preceding discourse narrated, he returned from himself, and spoke to the exile all the things which had been shown to him, namely to those of whom it is written above: I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting beside me, and the hand of the Lord God fell upon me there, and I saw. […]

12:2.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a provoking house, who have eyes to see and do not see, and ears to hear and do not hear, for it is a provoking house. (Where we have rendered: You dwell in the midst of a provoking house, the Seventy put: You dwell in the midst of their iniquities; but from what follows: For it is a provoking house, we understand that the former clause too fits this little verse.) We have often shown, too, that 'bitterness' is said in place of 'provocation', so that the sense is: 'You dwell in the midst of a house that turns God to bitterness, which, by the bitterness of its vices, makes God, who is by nature sweet and merciful, bitter and cruel'; otherwise we read of God: Taste and see that gracious (or sweet) is the Lord. The prophet, then, dwells in the midst of a people provoking God to bitterness, which has eyes and does not see, ears and does not hear, not through a defect of the senses but through the obstinacy of depravity; […]

12:3.t: You therefore, son of man, make yourself vessels of exile, and you shall migrate by day before them; and you shall migrate from your place to another place in their sight, if perhaps they may look, for it is a provoking house. (LXX: "And you, son of man, make yourself vessels of captivity, and be taken captive by day before them; and be taken captive from your place to another place in their sight, that they may see, for it is a provoking house.") No one doubts that the whole content of this passage points to the future captivity of King Zedekiah of the tribe of Judah, who was taken together with Jerusalem. But since some would have the captivity of Zedekiah, which means 'righteous Lord', go before as a type of the Savior, who, descending from heavenly things to earthly, took on a human body, and would have these be the vessels of captivity, I therefore think the prudent and cautious reader must be forewarned: that we set these things down, lest we seem to pass over anything, but do not approve them; […]

12:4.t: And you shall carry out your vessels like the vessels of one going into exile by day in their sight, and you shall go out in the evening before them, as one migrating goes out. Before their eyes dig through the wall for yourself, and you shall go out through it; in their sight you shall carry on your shoulders, in the darkness you shall flee: you shall veil your face, and you shall not see the land, for I have given you as a portent to the house of Israel. (LXX: "And you shall bring forth your vessels, vessels of captivity, by day in their eyes, and you shall go out in the evening in their sight, as a captive goes out. Dig for yourself in the wall, and you shall pass through it; in their sight you shall be carried on shoulders, and you shall go out hidden: you shall cover your face, and you shall not see the land, for I have given you as a portent to the house of Israel.") […]

12:7.t: So I did as he had commanded me: I brought out my vessels like the vessels of one migrating by day, and in the evening I dug through the wall for myself with my hand; in the darkness I went out, and I carried on my shoulders in their sight. (LXX: "And I did so according to all that he had commanded me: and I brought out vessels like vessels of captivity by day, and toward evening I dug through the wall for myself with my hand, and I went out hidden, I was taken up upon shoulders in their sight.") What he was commanded above to do, he testifies that he accomplished in deed, and it needs no interpretation, according to either sense, since it was expounded above. […]

12:9.t: And the word of the Lord came to me in the morning, saying: Son of man, have not the house of Israel, the provoking house, said to you: What are you doing? Say to them: Thus says the Lord God. 'If the provoking house asks you: Why are you doing these things? — or, according to the Seventy, even if they do not ask, you thrust it upon them, so that they may know why you have done these things —, say to them: Thus says the Lord God.'

12:10.t: This burden is upon the prince who is in Jerusalem, and upon all the house of Israel which is in their midst. Say: I am your portent; as I have done, so shall it be done to them: into exile and into captivity they shall go; and the prince who is in their midst shall be carried on shoulders, he shall go out in the darkness; they shall dig through the wall to lead him out: his face shall be covered, so that he may not see the land with his eyes. And I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my dragnet; and I will bring him to Babylon, into the land of the Chaldeans, and he shall not see it; there he shall die. And all who are around him, his guard and his troops, I will scatter to every wind; and I will draw the sword after them. And they shall know that I am the Lord, when I have scattered them among the nations and sown them in the lands. And I will leave of them a few men from the sword and famine and pestilence, that they may tell all their crimes among the nations to which they shall enter; […]

12:18.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Eat your bread in disturbance, and drink your water in haste and grief. And say to the people of the land: Thus says the Lord God to those who dwell in Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread in anxiety, and drink their water in desolation, so that the land may be made desolate of its multitude because of the iniquity of all who dwell in it; and the cities that are now inhabited shall be desolate, and the land deserted, and you shall know that I am the Lord. (LXX: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, you shall eat your bread with pain, and you shall drink your water with torment and distress. And you shall say to the people of the land: Thus says Adonai the Lord to the inhabitants of Jerusalem upon the land of Israel: They shall eat their loaves with want, and drink their water with devastation, so that the land and its fullness may be devastated; […]

12:22.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, what is this proverb of yours in the land of Israel, of those saying: The days shall be put off far, and every vision shall perish? Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God: I will make this proverb cease, nor shall it be commonly said any longer in Israel; and speak to them that the days have drawn near, and the word of every vision. For no longer shall any vision be empty, nor divination ambiguous, in the midst of the sons of Israel; for I the Lord will speak, whatever word I speak, and it shall be done; it shall not be prolonged any more: but in your days, provoking house, I will speak the word and do it, says the Lord God. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, behold the house of Israel, of those saying: The vision that this man sees is for many days, and for distant times he prophesies; therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God: None of my words shall be prolonged any longer; […]

12:27.t: It was not as though it were unknown that He had promised in their behalf that things should be thus, and then the years were diminished and also were increased, but as known; for He knew the measure of that which was to come, and on account of His mercies He gave a time for repentance that men might be without excuse; and men despised the longsuffering of God, and when they heard that there was much time until the wrath which was promised should come, becoming bold they sinned before Him and said: "That which the prophets say is prophesied for a remote time." On account of this when there arose a disputing concerning these things in the days of Ezekiel the prophet and they said: "That which hath been prophesied is for a remote time," He said to Ezekiel: "As I live," saith the Lord of dominions, "there shall not again be a delay to My words, for the word which I shall speak I shall shortly accomplish." And He cut off that which He had foretold, to give to men a time for repentance, that perhaps they might repent; […]

13:2.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, prophesy to the prophets of Israel who prophesy; and you shall say to those who prophesy from their own heart: Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God. (This which we have set down: Who prophesy; and you shall say to those who prophesy from their own heart, the Seventy omitted, and in its place they added what is not found in the Hebrew: And you shall prophesy, and you shall say to them.) Now this speech is against the false prophets, who were deceiving the people and prophesying something else, contrary to the commandments of God. Nor should it trouble anyone that they are called prophets, for holy Scripture has this custom, that it names each one the prophet of his own prophesying and speech, just as there are called prophets of Baal and prophets of idols and prophets of confusion; […]

13:3.t: Woe to the senseless prophets, who follow their own spirit and see nothing. (LXX: "Woe to those who prophesy from their own heart and do not see at all", leaving out that which has been set down by us: Who follow their own spirit). Since the name of prophets, according to the rule of the Scriptures, is common to the good and the bad, they differ in this, that the good prophets are said to be wise, but the bad stupid and senseless; of these the one is referred to the men of the Church, the other to all the heretics, who, abandoning the Spirit of God, follow their own spirit, because they prophesy not at all by divine inspiration but from their own heart: whence also they see nothing. But he who is wise follows not the thoughts of his own heart but the Spirit of God, according to that passage in which, earlier on, the living creatures and the wheels followed the Spirit of God; […]

13:4.t: Moreover, according to the Seventy the sense here is this: all the heretics, because of their deceitfulness and wickedness, are like foxes, of whom the Savior speaks: Foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky nests; and of Herod it is written: Tell this fox; and of these same foxes, which deceive the little and simple ones and lay waste the vineyard of Christ, Solomon speaks: Catch us the little foxes that destroy the vineyards; and in the psalm it is sung concerning those who are tripped up by their deceitfulness: They will go into the lower parts of the earth, they will be handed over into the hands of the sword, they will be the portions of foxes.

Like foxes in the deserts were your prophets, Israel. You do not go up from the opposite side, nor did you set up a wall for the house of Israel, that you might stand in battle on the day of the Lord. They see vain things and divine a lie, saying: Says the Lord, when the Lord has not sent them; and they persisted in confirming the word. Have you not seen an empty vision, and spoken a lying divination, and do you say: Says the Lord, when I have not spoken? (LXX: "As foxes in the deserts are your prophets, Israel. They did not stand on the firmament, and they gathered flocks upon the house of Israel; they did not rise up, those who speak on the day of the Lord, seeing lies, divining vain things, who say: The Lord says, and the Lord did not send them; and they began to raise up the word. […]

13:5.t: These prophets, who are like foxes, did not stand on the firmament; nor did they deserve to hear with Peter: You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church; nor are they like Moses, to whom it was said: But you, stand here with me, nor like him who says: He set my feet upon a rock, but they are tossed about by every wind of doctrine; nor did they stand on the firmament of which we read in Psalm 18 (19): The heavens tell the glory of God, and the firmament announces the works of his hands. These gathered all sorts of irrational people, who on account of their excessive innocence are like cattle, against the house of God; hence it is now said: And they gathered flocks upon the house of Israel; nor did they themselves rise up, nor could they raise up others, but whatever they have done and are doing is full of lies.

To such men it is rightly said through the prophet: "You have not gone up against the enemy, nor have you set up a wall for the house of Israel, to stand in battle on the day of the Lord." To go up against the enemy is to oppose with the free voice of reason any powers that act wickedly. And we stand in battle on the day of the Lord for the house of Israel and set up a wall if we defend the faithful and innocent against the injustice of the perverse with the authority of justice. Because the hireling does not do this, when he sees the wolf coming, he flees.

Whence it is well said to Ezekiel, "Take unto thee a tile, and thou shalt lay it before thee, and pourtray upon it the dry Jerusalem." And immediately it is subjoined, "And thou shalt lay siege against it, and build forts, and cast a mount, and set camps against it, and set battering rams against it round about. And do thou take unto thee an iron frying-pan, and thou shalt set it for a wall of iron between thee and the city."

But although the ruler may nicely insinuate all these things, he procures not for himself lasting absolution, unless he glow with a spirit of jealousy against the delinquencies of all and each. For by the frying-pan is denoted a frying of the mind, and by iron the hardness of reproof.

13:6.t: Since, therefore, they behold vain things and divine a lie and say that they have been sent by the Lord, when they have not been sent by him, and persist in their errors and desire to make their own word firm, they are convicted that all the things they preach are empty, since they say that their own lie is the word of the Lord.

And what follows: And they began to raise up the word, signifies this: that they wish indeed to rise up and to lift themselves to the heights, but cannot fulfill what they desire; and it is said to them: Have you not seen a false vision, and spoken vain divinations? — and what follows: And you were saying: The Lord says, and I have not spoken, is not found in the Seventy —.

13:8.t: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have spoken vain things and seen a lie, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord God; and my hand shall be upon the prophets who see vain things and divine a lie: in the council of my people they shall not be, and in the writing of the house of Israel they shall not be written, nor shall they enter into the land of Israel, and you shall know that I am the Lord God. (LXX: "Therefore say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Since your words are lies and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am over you, says the Lord God; and I will stretch out my hand upon the prophets who see a lie and who speak vain things: in the discipline of my people they shall not be, nor shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, and into the land of Israel they shall not enter, and they shall know that I am Adonai the Lord.") […]

13:9.t: Finally, when the Lord would for their speedy fall turn away His merciful countenance from the people, whom He had chosen out of all nations, the giver of the law interposes on their behalf and cries out: "I beseech Thee, O Lord, this people have sinned a great sin; they have made for themselves gods of gold; and now if Thou forgivest their sin, forgive it; but if not, blot me out of Thy book which Thou hast written. To whom the Lord answered: If any man hath sinned before Me, I will blot him out of My book." David also, when complaining in prophetic spirit of Judas and the Lord's persecutors, says: "Let them be blotted out of the book of the living;" and because they did not deserve to come to saving penitence because of the guilt of their great sin, he subjoins: "And let them not be written among the righteous." […]
13:9.s: The Second Conference of Abbot Joseph, Chapter 25

13:10.t: But I must proceed to my former statement that Christ is called the Stone in the Prophets. For in ancient times David said concerning Him:—The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the building. And how did the builders reject this Stone which is Christ? How else than that they so rejected Him before Pilate and said—This man shall not be King over us. And again in that parable that our Lord spake that a certain nobleman went to receive kingly power and to return and rule over them; and they sent after Him envoys saying:—This man shall not be King over us. By these things they rejected the Stone which is Christ. And how did it become the head of the building? How else than that it was set up over the building of the Gentiles and upon it is reared up all their building. And who are the builders? […]

For there is a peace that does not have an offense, and there is one that has it: which is from love, it does not have an offense; which is from deceit, it has. Therefore, the Prophet also says: Peace, peace; but where is peace (Ezekiel 12:10)? Therefore, let us seek the refuge of peace for sinners; for they conspire against the innocent, they gather together to oppress the righteous, to destroy the widow, or to assault her modesty.

How is the cause helped by the people who dance attendance on these people with itching ears who know neither how to hear nor how to speak? They confound old mire with new cement and, as Ezekiel says, daub a wall with untempered mortar; so that, when the truth comes in a shower, they are brought to nothing.

Because they have deceived my people, saying: Peace, peace, and there is no peace; and he himself was building a wall, but they were daubing it with mud without straw. Say to those who daub without tempering that it will fall; for there will be a flooding shower, and I will give very great stones rushing down from above, and a wind of tempest scattering it. For behold, the wall has fallen; will it not be said to you: Where is the daubing with which you daubed? Therefore thus says the Lord God: And I will make the spirit of tempests burst forth in my indignation, and there will be a flooding shower in my fury, and great stones of wrath in consummation; and I will destroy the wall which you daubed without due mixture, and I will level it with the earth, and its foundation will be uncovered, and it will fall and be consumed in its midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord. […]
Also that which we read above: He himself was building (or builds) a wall, many refer to the people of Israel, which was promising itself vain help, either from the Egyptians or from peace.

13:11.t: That which the Seventy translated: And upon their joints, is not found in the Hebrew; and it signifies the joints of the stones in a wall, or the supports of timber by which walls are strengthened.

'Say,' he says, 'to those who promise them vain things and pledge empty help, that this wall, this enclosure, will fall, and I will send a most violent shower, that is, most savage enemies — and he means the Babylonians and Chaldeans —, and these same enemies as stones of hail rushing down from above', all by μεταφορὰν [metaphor], so that a sudden whirlwind may overturn and undermine the unstable enclosure; and that afterward it may be said to them — that is, to the false prophets —: 'Where is the daubing with which you daubed? and where is the help you promised?'.

13:13.t: The words that follow describe and condemn some sin that has been committed. The judgment contained in these words is just, for it is as if he were giving notice in the words of the prophet that, if you had not sinned, he would not have made these threats.… The inspired Word exists because of both obedience and disobedience: that we may be saved by obeying it and educated because we have disobeyed.

But whatever we have said of the false prophets can be referred also to the heretics: that all their fabrications are dissolved by the wrath of God, and the building of the worst dogmas, which does not have the seasoning of the Holy Spirit, collapses and slides down to its foundations and to dust, and the enclosure itself is leveled with the earth and falls, and both the prophets who were promising and the people to whom it was promised are consumed in its midst, so that, after he has fulfilled his indignation and has said to them: There is no such wall — that is, 'you have no defense' — and there are none who daub it, but all things are vain and come to nothing, then you will know by deed that I am the Lord.

13:14.t: He threatens that He will consume both the wall and them that daubed it, that is, those who sin and those who throw a cloak over them; as the evil rulers and priests have done, who caused the house of Israel to err according to their own hearts which are estranged in their lusts.

13:16.t: And so that we may know who those are who daub the wall, there follows: The prophets of Israel — that is, the false prophets — who prophesy to Jerusalem, and see for her a vision of peace; these are the cause of sin and ruin and foolish security: For there will be no peace, says the Lord, because the Lord did not send them nor did he speak to them.

13:17.t: The prophet, then, is ordered to set, or to make firm, his face against the daughters of his people. And first we must say what the face 'set' or 'directed' and 'made firm' means: namely that which is written of the Lord: The face of the Lord is upon those who do evil, to destroy their memory from the earth. As indeed wax melts before the face of the fire, so let sinners perish before the face of God; according to which sense it is said in this same prophet: Son of man, make your face firm upon Theman and Darom and Nageb, and again: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, make your face firm upon Jerusalem, and a little after: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, make your face firm upon the Ammonites, and again: Make your countenance firm upon Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and again: Son of man, make your face firm upon Gog and Magog, and in another place: I will make my face firm upon that man, and I will put him into the desert and into dissipation, and I will take him away from the midst […]

And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own heart, and prophesy over them, and say: Thus says the Lord God: Woe to those who sew cushions under every elbow of the hand, and make pillows under the head of every age to catch souls; and when they caught the souls of my people, they made their souls alive. And they profaned me before my people for a handful of barley and a fragment of bread, to kill souls which do not die, and to make alive souls which do not live, lying to my people who believe lies. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against your cushions, with which you catch flying souls, and I will tear them from your arms, and I will let go the souls which you catch, souls to fly, and I will tear your pillows, and I will free my people from your hand, and they shall no longer be in your hands for plunder; and you shall know that I am the Lord. […]

13:18.t: The Holy Spirit poured out upon the prophet lamenting the misfortune of our frailty, which neither had rest in this life nor retained anything in the sudden encounter with death, that humanity would not rise again until the one came who did not patch the new onto the old nor put a new piece of cloth on an old garment; but rather made all things new, as he himself said: Behold, I make all things new. For he is the resurrection, he is the firstborn from the dead, in whom we have indeed received a foretaste of the future resurrection, yet he alone has already risen with eternal resurrection.

Woe, then, to these heresies and to these doctrines, which, promising rest, deceive every age and sex, to catch the souls of the wretched and to defile me before my people, while I am believed to love pleasure; and this not for a corus and a hemicorus of barley, as we read in Hosea, but for a handful of barley, on which brute animals feed, and a fragment of bread: not a whole loaf, nor the solid testimonies of the Scriptures, but those which have been broken and cut short and diminished by heretical depravity, so as to deceive all the holy and drag them to death, while they strive to make sinners alive with vain promises.

For from love of himself the ruler's mind is inclined to softness, because, when he observes those that are under him sinning, he does not presume to reprove them, lest their affection for himself should grow dull; nay sometimes he smooths down with flatteries the offence of his subordinates which he ought to have rebuked. Hence it is well said through the prophet, "Woe unto them that sew cushions under every elbow, and make pillows under the head of every stature to catch souls"; inasmuch as to put cushions under every elbow is to cherish with bland flatteries souls that are falling from their uprightness and reclining themselves in this world's enjoyment. For it is as though the elbow of a recumbent person rested on a cushion and his head on pillows, when the hardness of reproof is withdrawn from one who sins, and when the softness of favour is offered to him, that he may lie softly in error, while no roughness of contradiction troubles him.

13:19.t: There were, it is likely, in the time of our forefathers also, some who "weakened the hands of the people," and brought into practice that which is mentioned by Ezekiel,—or rather who did the works of the false prophets, who "profaned God among His people for handfuls of barley"; a thing, by the way, done methinks by some even at this day. When, for example, we say that he who calleth his brother a fool shall depart into hell-fire, others say, "What? Is he that calls his brother a fool to depart into hell-fire? Impossible," say they. And again, when we say that "the covetous man is an idolater," in this too again they make abatements, and say the expression is hyperbolical. And in this manner they underrate and explain away all the commandments.

It often happens that a Pastor is moved by hatred or favor toward any neighbor; but those who follow their own hatreds or favor in the cases of their subjects cannot judge worthily concerning their subjects. Whence it is rightly said through the prophet: They were putting to death souls that do not die, and giving life to souls that do not live. For he puts to death one who is not dying who condemns the just. And he strives to give life to one who will not live who attempts to absolve the guilty from punishment.

Therefore the causes must be weighed, and then the power of binding and loosing must be exercised. It must be seen what fault preceded, or what repentance followed after the fault, so that those whom almighty God visits through the grace of compunction, the sentence of the pastor may absolve. For then the absolution of the one presiding is true, when it follows the judgment of the internal Judge.

13:20.t: Therefore the clement and merciful God does not slay the prophetesses themselves, but will tear their cushions, which like nets catch flying souls, so that, after these have been torn, the souls may have free power of flying; and he will rend the veils, or pillows, on which the ruling part of the soul was reclining and with which the heads of the deceived were covered; since the apostle teaches that the heads of men are not to be veiled, but that the glory of the Lord is to be contemplated with unveiled face: 'For you,' he says, 'were breaking the spirits of those who serve God with false terrors, and were keeping the wicked shut in with fraudulent promises, lest by doing penance they should recover the life which they had lost; […]

14:1.t: And men, elders of Israel, came to me and sat before me. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, these men have set uncleannesses in their hearts, and have set up the stumbling block of their iniquity against their face; shall I, being asked, answer them? Therefore speak to them, and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: A man, a man of the house of Israel who sets his uncleannesses in his heart, and sets up the stumbling block of his iniquity against his face, and comes to the prophet inquiring of me through him, I the Lord will answer him according to the multitude of his uncleannesses, that the house of Israel may be caught in their heart, in which they have withdrawn from me in all their idols. Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Turn and withdraw from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your defilements. […]

14:4.t: Now the meaning of the whole passage, to comprehend a broad explanation in a brief discourse, is this: 'A man, a man not of the other nations — whose error can have pardon —, but of the house of Israel, who comes to the prophet to inquire with his former vices — of which we have spoken above —, I will answer him according to his heart and his uncleannesses, so that he may hear according to what he wishes and believes: for he who asks not in a spirit of learning but of testing does not deserve correction. For they have withdrawn from me and have followed idols; and this is a brief threat, so that they may withdraw from idols and perverse thoughts and turn to me, abandoning their former crimes'; for he who asks deceitfully does not deserve to hear the truth, but is to be caught by his own heart, just as the scribes and Pharisees, questioning the Lord, or rather testing him, hear: Why do you test me?, and again: Neither will I tell you by what power I do these things; […]

14:7.t: And what is said a second time: A man, a man of the sons of Israel and of the strangers who are joined to them, shows, according to the Apostle, a twofold man in us: the outer and the inner — for many, having the bodily face of a man, take on the images of various beasts, whose destruction the prophet desires when he prays: Lord, in your city you will destroy their image; those of whom it is written: Man, when he was in honor, did not understand; he was compared to senseless beasts of burden, and became like them, are not men who are men, but men who are beasts of burden; again, those who hear in the Gospel: Serpents, brood of vipers, who showed you to flee from the wrath to come?, are not men who are men, but men who are serpents as well; and those of whom it is written: Foxes have holes, and the birds of heaven nests, and of Herod: Tell this fox, are not men who are men, but men who are foxes —; […]

Those dissatisfied with any facet of your creation are unsound in mind, as I was when many things that you made displeased me. Because my soul did not dare to be dissatisfied with my God, it would not identify as yours whatever dissatisfied it. In this way it had strayed into a belief in two substances, and it got no rest but recounted the opinions of others. Recoiling from that error, it had made for itself a god inhabiting the boundless area of all space, and it had considered that god to be you, and had "set it in its heart" and had become again the shrine of its idol, deserving of your loathing. But after you stroked my ignorant head and closed my eyes so that they should not see vanity, I retired from myself a little, and my madness was lulled to sleep. I awoke in you and saw you infinite in a different way, and that vision was not with the eyes of the flesh.

14:9.t: And what follows also seems to raise a question: The prophet, when he errs and speaks a word, I the Lord have deceived that prophet; let us not think that this is said of a true prophet, but of a false prophet, who is called a prophet συνωνυμῶς [by a shared name]. And it can be resolved from that passage of the Scriptures where Ahab king of Israel, going to battle, will not listen to Micaiah the prophet, but acquiesces in the counsels of the false prophets, and Micaiah says that he saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and that a spirit of error offered itself of its own accord to deceive the king; the devil too, in the book of Job, going around the earth, is said to stand in the sight of God and to receive power from the Lord, first over Job's substance, then over his body; and Balaam the soothsayer also is sent by the Lord to deceive Balak the son of Beor. […]

Then he stretches out his hand upon him — the prophet is understood — and he is blotted out from the midst of his people, so that he may bear his iniquity, because for like error the punishment too is alike, so that both he who asks and he who is asked may bear their iniquity, and the house of Israel, that of those who wish to hear the words of God, may by no means be mocked by perverse prophesyings, but may be the people of God, and may itself deserve to have the Lord as God. With what he said: I the Lord have deceived him, the words of Solomon agree, who, discoursing of God, says: And he will mock the mockers, and that testimony: If they walk perversely toward me, I too will walk against them in perverse fury.

When, therefore, you hear the Lord say, "I the Lord have deceived that prophet," and likewise what the apostle says: "He hath mercy on whom He will have mercy, and whom He will He hardeneth," believe that, in the case of him whom He permits to be deceived and hardened, his evil deeds have deserved the judgment; whilst in the case of him to whom He shows mercy, you should loyally and unhesitatingly recognise the grace of the God who "rendereth not evil for evil; but contrariwise blessing."
14:9.s: On Grace and Free Will, Chapter 45

14:13.t: It is not easy for God to pardon idolaters.… Ezekiel also denounces this wrath of God on those who sin against God. He says, "And the word of the Lord came to me saying, 'son of man, when a land shall sin against me so as to transgress grievously, I will stretch forth my hand on it, and I will break the staff of the bread thereof; and I will send famine on it and destroy man and beast out of it. And if these three men, Noah, Daniel and Job, shall be in it, they will not deliver sons or daughters; themselves alone shall be saved.' "

And the hand is stretched out over the transgressing land so that the staff, or strength, of bread may be broken; and that hand, stretched out, threatens plagues, since he who stretches it out and lifts it up does not wish to strike sinners, but by its stretching out to terrify them and to preserve them once terrified.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, when a land sins against me so as to transgress, transgressing, I will stretch out my hand upon it, and I will break the staff of its bread, and I will send famine into it and kill from it man and beasts; and if these three men are in its midst, Noah and Daniel and Job, they by their righteousness shall deliver their own souls, says the Lord of hosts. But if I also bring most evil beasts upon the land to lay it waste, and it becomes impassable because there is no one passing through on account of the beasts, if these three men are in it, as I live, says the Lord, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they alone shall be delivered, and the land shall be made desolate. Or if I bring a sword upon that land, and say to the sword: Pass through the land, and I kill from it man and beast, and these three men are in its midst, as I live, says the Lord God, they shall not deliver sons or daughters, but they alone shall be delivered. […]

But upon our land too, to which it is said: You are earth, and into earth you shall go, and upon our Jerusalem, each and every one of the believers, if they despise the commandments of God and deserve to be called transgressors, famine will be brought: Not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of God; the sword too will be brought, of which we read: They shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes, and to Mary: A sword shall pierce through your own soul also; beasts too will be brought, to which the righteous man asks not to be handed over: Do not hand over to beasts the soul that confesses to you; and pestilence will be brought — for which the Seventy translated 'death' —, of which it is written: The death of sinners is very evil, and: The soul that sins, it shall die, and: So bitter is death. […]

14:14.t: Who was more righteous than Noah, who, when the earth was replete with sins, was alone found righteous on the earth? Who more glorious than Daniel? Who stronger in firmness of faith for enduring martyrdom, happier in God's favors, who when he fought so often conquered and when he conquered survived? Who was more diligent in good works than Job, stronger in temptations, more patient in suffering, more submissive in fear, more true in faith? And yet God said that, if they should ask, he would not grant. When the prophet Ezekiel interceded for the sins of the people, God said, "Whatever land shall sin against me, so as to transgress grievously, I will stretch forth my hand on it, and will break the staff of bread thereof, and will send famine upon it and will destroy people and beast out of it. And if these three men, Noah, Daniel and Job, shall be in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they only shall be delivered." […]

That no one may despair of himself, though hitherto he have been careless, that he may set his hopes on nothing else, after God's mercy, but on his own virtue. For if these were nothing the better for such a kindred, though they were of the same house and lineage with Christ, until they gave proof of virtue; what favor can we possibly receive, when we plead righteous kinsmen and brethren, unless we be exceeding dutiful, and have lived in virtue? As the prophet too said, intimating the selfsame thing, "A brother redeemeth not, shall a man redeem?"… Yea, if it be Ezekiel who entreats, he will be told, "Though Noah stand forth, and Job, and Daniel, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters." Though the patriarch Abraham be supplicating for them that are most incurably diseased, and change not, God will leave him and go His way, that he may not receive his cry in their behalf.… For it is true, the prayers of the saints have the greatest power; on condition however of our repentance and amendment.
14:14.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 5:7

14:14.t: Considering then all these things, let us betake ourselves unto the preparation for our departure hence. For even if the common day of the consummation never overtake us, the end of each one is at the doors, whether he be old or young; and it is not possible for men after they have gone hence, either to buy oil any more, or to obtain pardon by prayers, though he that entreats be Abraham, or Noah, or Job, or Daniel. While then we have opportunity, let us store up for ourselves beforehand much confidence, let us gather oil in abundance, let us remove all into Heaven, that in the fitting time, and when we most need them, we may enjoy all: by the grace and love towards man of our Lord Jesus Christ.
14:14.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 20:6

14:14.t: — It is asked, since Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, Moses too and the other patriarchs and prophets, were righteous, why mention is made of these alone; which is easily resolved: for Noah could not put off the flood impending over the world, because all the earth had polluted the ways of the Lord, but he had his sons preserved, who perhaps were of the same virtue, and also for the sake of a seedbed of the human race; Daniel too softened by no weeping the captivity impending over the people of the Jews; and Job as well, not on account of sins but for the sake of testing, delivered neither his house nor his sons. Others, however, say that because these three men alone beheld both prosperity and adversity and prosperity again, they are for that reason named together, and that this is secretly signified: that, just as they saw both good things and evil and again joyful things, so also the people of Israel, which had first enjoyed good things and afterward bore the yoke of captivity, if it does penance, returns to its […]

But if Noah and Daniel and Job, gathered together and placed in one place, cannot withdraw the sinning land, that is, those who dwell in the land, from the wrath of God, what is to be said of those who think that sinful sons can be delivered from the fires of Gehenna by the merit and virtues of their parents? Hence neither will a martyr father be able to deliver a transgressing son, nor will a mother of holy life give the rewards of chastity to an unchaste daughter; and on the contrary the vices of parents will not harm their children, but: The soul that sins, it shall die. Lot, dwelling in Sodom but a stranger both in spirit and in flesh, did not deliver his wife, who had looked back behind her, but only his daughters, who perhaps had not sinned; and Josiah, a holy man, not only did not save a sinful people by his virtues, but he himself also died in its sins. […]

Nay, can we be better men than Daniel himself, concerning whom God, speaking to the prince of Tyre, says by the prophet Ezekiel, "Art thou wiser than Daniel?" who also is placed among the three righteous men to whom alone God saith that He would grant deliverance,—pointing, doubtless, in them to three representative righteous men,—declaring that he would deliver only Noah, Daniel, and Job, and that they should save along with themselves neither son nor daughter, but only their own souls.

Now, I suppose it is not easy to find in God's Scripture so weighty a testimony of holiness given of any man as that which is written of His three servants, Noah, Daniel, and Job, whom the Prophet Ezekiel describes as the only men able to be delivered from God's impending wrath. In these three men he no doubt prefigures three classes of mankind to be delivered: in Noah, as I suppose, are represented righteous leaders of nations, by reason of his government of the ark as a type of the Church; in Daniel, men who are righteous in continence; in Job, those who are righteous in wedlock;—to say nothing of any other view of the passage, which it is unnecessary now to consider. It is, at any rate, clear from this testimony of the prophet, and from other inspired statements, how eminent were these worthies in righteousness.
14:14.s: ON THE MERITS AND FORGIVENESS OF SINS AND ON INFANT BAPTISM 2:12.10

14:14.t:
The conversion of one man does not atone for the sins of the many, nor is it enough to appease God that one man should leave off sinning, while the whole human race offends him. Consider too that he who is converted for the sake of escaping eternal death certainly gains a great reward for his conversion in this escape. By no means could he succeed in turning away the punishment of damnation from others. It is a mark of intolerable presumption, and an enormous wickedness, for a man to think himself so holy that he even supposes wicked men can find salvation through him. God spoke thus of a certain land and a sinful people: "Though these three men, Noah, Daniel and Job, were in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters, they only shall be delivered."

No one, I think, will be so shameless as to dare compare himself with such men as these. However much a man may now try to please God, yet to assert one's own morality is an example of the greatest unrighteousness. […]
14:14.s: On the Government of God, Book 3, Chapter 11

14:14.t: Ezekiel the prophet mystically distinguishes them from one another when he foretells that there are only three men who will be delivered when the time of plagues comes, namely: Noah, Daniel and Job. For surely in Noah, who steered the ark over the waves, he shows those who are set over the church; in Daniel, who was zealous to live continently in the royal court, he shows the continent or virgins; in Job, who while married exhibited a wonderful example of patience to all, he shows the life of the virtuous married people.

14:20.t: And you deceive yourselves while you fancy that, because you are the seed of Abraham after the flesh, therefore you shall fully inherit the good things announced to be bestowed by God through Christ. For no one, not even of them, has anything to look for, but only those who in mind are assimilated to the faith of Abraham, and who have recognised all the mysteries: for I say, that some injunctions were laid on you in reference to the worship of God and practice of righteousness; but some injunctions and acts were likewise mentioned in reference to the mystery of Christ, on account of the hardness of your people's hearts. And that this is so, God makes known in Ezekiel, [when] He said concerning it: 'If Noah and Jacob and Daniel should beg either sons or daughters, the request would not be granted them.' And in Isaiah, of the very same matter He spake thus: 'The Lord God said, they shall both go forth and look on the members [of the bodies] of the men that have transgressed. […]

And besides, they beguile themselves and you, supposing that the everlasting kingdom will be assuredly given to those of the dispersion who are of Abraham after the flesh, although they be sinners, and faithless, and disobedient towards God, which the Scriptures have proved is not the case. For if so, Isaiah would never have said this: 'And unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we would have been like Sodom and Gomorrah.' And Ezekiel: 'Even if Noah, and Jacob, and Daniel were to pray for sons or daughters, their request should not be granted.' But neither shall the father perish for the son, nor the son for the father; but every one for his own sin, and each shall be saved for his own righteousness.

14:21.t: 'Since,' he says, 'these things are so, and the prayer of such great men does not save a sinning land from single plagues, thus says the Lord: Because Jerusalem has sinned abominably, I will bring four plagues upon it at once: the sword by which it is slaughtered by its enemies, and famine which it endures under siege, and beasts by which those who flee are devoured in deserts and forests, and pestilence, which always follows famine and want — for which the common edition translated 'death' —. And these things,' he says, 'I will bring upon it, so that neither men remain in it nor beasts; and yet, in my clemency, while the four plagues impend at once and lay everything waste, I will leave in it some who bring out their sons and daughters, and let them come here as captives — that is, to Babylon and to Chaldea —; […]

15:2.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, what will become of the wood of the vine, out of all the woods of the groves that are among the trees of the forests? Is wood taken from it to make a work, or will a peg be fashioned from it, so that any vessel may hang from it? Behold, it has been given to the fire for food; the fire has consumed both its parts, and its middle has been reduced to ashes; will it be useful for a work? Even when it was whole it was not fit for a work; how much more, when the fire has devoured it and burnt it up, will no work be made of it! Therefore thus says the Lord God: As the wood of the vine among the trees of the forests, which I have given to the fire to devour, so will I give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem; […]

According to the spiritual understanding, we can understand the vineyard and Jerusalem as the multitude of believers, which, if it has been negligent and has lost the cultivation of its former religion, and has not borne the fruits of the virtues nor made wine that gladdens the heart of man, will be given up to everlasting flames and reckoned as nothing: for the servant who knows the will of his master, and does not do it, will be beaten with many blows. The Lord too says something of the kind in the Gospel according to John: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Every branch that abides in me and does not bear fruit, the Father will take it away; and every one that bears fruit he will cleanse, that it may bear more fruit; but if the Savior is the vine and we the branches and God the Father the husbandman, as long as we keep God's commandments we are continually cultivated, and our cultivation is a cleansing: for it is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy; […]

15:4.t: For the heavenly Watchers departed from the fence of the vineyard; and the mighty tower on which they relied was torn down. The winepress, the cleansing away of their offences, was overthrown. When the vine was without blemish, it did not prove of service. Now that the fire has devoured it and that it is laid waste, how shall it prove of service? The fire has devoured its two branches and its inward parts are wasted. For its two branches are the two kingdoms, and its inward part which is laid waste is Jerusalem.

Now the ambiguity of the Hebrew word 'sene', which is written with three letters, 'sin' and 'nun' and 'iod', is this: if it is read 'sene' it means 'two', if 'sane', 'years'; hence it came about that for its two extremities, which we translated 'both its parts', the Seventy translated 'its yearly cleansing', whereas Aquila said 'its two last parts', Symmachus and Theodotion 'its two extremities'; and the sequence is this: 'As a fruitless vine is given to the fire to no use, so Jerusalem too, or rather its inhabitants, will be given up to the flames, so that they go out from the fire and the fire consumes them, that is: even if they escape from the city, outside they will be consumed by the enemy's sword, and those who remain, crushed by the very weight of their miseries, will recognize that I am the Lord, when I have set, or set firm, my face against them and have given them up to everlasting desolation: for they proved not sinners like the other nations, but transgressors' — for it is one thing to neglect what you […]

16:1.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations, and you shall say: Thus says the Lord God to Jerusalem. (LXX: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, bear witness to Jerusalem of her iniquities, and you shall say to her: Thus says Adonai the Lord.") Where the compass of the individual prophecies was brief, we set down whole passages, adding at once beneath them what seemed right to us; here, however, because a long discourse is directed to Jerusalem by one who bears witness to her and teaches her the sins she has committed, and the prophecy extends to nearly two hundred lines, namely up to that place in which it is written: When I have been appeased toward you in all that you have done, says the Lord God, we must set out the whole prophecy in parts, and fit the due explanations to the parts we have set out. […]

16:2.t: And again, Ezekiel makes this an accusation against them, that they did not grieve for the afflicted. What sayest thou, O Prophet? God punisheth, and shall I grieve for those that He is punishing? Yea verily: for God Himself that punisheth wisheth this: since neither does He Himself wish to punish, nay, even Himself grieves when punishing. Then be not thou glad at it. You will say, "If they are justly punished, we ought not to grieve." Why, the thing we ought to grieve for is this—that they were found worthy of punishment. Say, when thou seest thy son undergoing cautery or the knife, dost thou not grieve? and sayest thou not to thyself, "What is this? It is for health this cutting, to quicken his recovery; it is for his deliverance, this burning?" but for all that, when thou hearest him crying out, and not able to [bear it], the hope of health being restored is not enough to carry off the shock to nature. […]
16:2.s: HOMILIES ON THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES 43

16:3.t: Your root and your generation from the land of Canaan, your father an Amorite and your mother a Hittite. Great is the faith, great the boldness of the prophets, that one man should charge a whole city with ignoble birth; admirable is Daniel who, to an elder who was sinning and joining murder to adultery, dared as a boy to say: Seed of Canaan and not of Judah, beauty has deceived you; great too is Isaiah, who cries out to the princes and to the people of the Jews: Hear the word of the Lord, princes of Sodom; give ear to the words of the Lord, people of Gomorrah; but no less is Ezekiel, who speaks confidently to the whole city: Your root and your generation from the land of Canaan, your father an Amorite and your mother a Hittite. […]

How, then, were the Jews the children of the devil? By imitation, not by birth. Listen to the usual language of the Holy Scriptures. The prophet says to those very Jews, "Thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother a Hittite." The Amorites were not a nation that gave origin to the Jews. The Hittites also were themselves of a nation altogether different from the race of the Jews. But because the Amorites and Hittites were impious, and the Jews imitated their impieties, they found parents for themselves, not of whom they were born, but in whose damnation they should share, because following their customs.

16:4.t: And when you were born, on the day of your birth, your navel was not cut, and you were not washed in water for salvation, nor salted with salt, nor wrapped in swaddling cloths. No eye spared you, to do for you one of these things, having pity on you, but you were cast out upon the face of the earth in the abjection of your soul on the day on which you were born. (LXX: "And your generation: on the day on which you were born, they did not bind your breasts, and you were not washed in water for salvation, nor salted with salt, and you were not wrapped in swaddling cloths. Nor did your eye spare you, that I should do for you one of all these things, and that it should suffer anything over you, and you were cast out upon the face of the field for the depravity of your soul on the day on which you were born.") Let us discuss each point in the order of the reading. […]

16:5.t: But why she deserved none of these things, the following Scripture testifies: No eye spared you, to do for you one of these things, having pity on you, for which the Seventy put: Your eye did not spare you, that I should do for you one of all these things, and the twofold edition must have a twofold understanding; the former signifies this: No eye spared you, to do for you one of these things, having pity on you, and the sense is: 'No one had pity on you, since God was offended; no one's heart was moved over you, so as to do for you at least one of the four things above, since you did not deserve to receive them all together'; in the other it is said: Your eye did not spare you, that I should do for you one of all these things, and it has this sense: 'You acted so, and were so born in sins, and in sins your mother conceived you, that not even you yourself had pity on yourself. […]

16:6.t: But passing by you I saw you trampled in your blood, and I said to you, when you were in your blood: Live. I said, I say, to you: In your blood live. I made you multiplied like the sprout of the field, and you went in and came to womanly finery, your breasts swelled and your hair sprouted; and you were naked and full of confusion. (LXX: "And I passed by you and saw you mixed in your blood, and I said to you: From your blood, life; be multiplied. Like the growth of the field I made you, and you were multiplied and were magnified; and you entered into the cities of cities, your breasts were raised and your hair sprang up; but you were naked, full of disgrace.") 'After you were cast out on the face of the field, or upon the face of the earth, because of the depravity of your soul, you no longer deserved my help. […]

16:7.t: And so great was the abundance of all things in you, that you had the likeness of a most fertile field — and the blessing of Jacob with which his father blessed him, saying: Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a full field which the Lord has blessed —, and that you entered the inner chambers of the Lord — and said with the bride: The king has brought me into his chamber —, and came to womanly finery'; for which the Seventy translated: And you entered into the cities of cities, so that, just as one speaks of the Song of 'Songs' and of an age of 'ages', so cities are called cities of 'cities', of which it is said in the Gospel: 'Have authority over ten (or over five) cities, so that you are called not only a city but a metropolis city', according to what is written in Isaiah: Faithful Zion, mother of cities; […]

16:8.t: But from hence infer not thy punishment only, but also the boundless longsuffering of God. How often at least have we put our hands to the same evil deeds, and yet He suffers long! But let us not be sanguine, but fear; since Pharaoh too, had he been taught by the first plague, would not have experienced the later ones; he would not afterwards have been drowned, his host and all together.
16:8.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 43:5

16:8.t: And I passed by you and saw you; and behold, your time, the time of lovers. And I spread my cloak over you, and covered your disgrace. (LXX: "And I passed by you and saw you; and behold, your time, the time of those turning aside. And I spread my wings over you, and covered your disgrace.") What great clemency! It had not been enough to have seen her once trampled in blood and to have called her to repentance, but when she sins again he visits her and, because she was naked and full of confusion, he comes again and visits; and behold, her time, the time 'of lovers' — or according to the Seventy 'of those turning aside', and according to the second translation of Aquila, συναλλαγῆς, namely 'of betrothal' and 'of the time of the nuptials', but according to the first edition of the same and Theodotion μαστῶν, which means 'of breasts', for which Symmachus rendered ἀγαπῆς, which signifies 'love' —; that, then, was the time when women can be joined and sustain marital intercourse. […]

And I swore to you, and entered into a pact with you, says the Lord God. (LXX: "And I swore to you, and entered into a covenant with you, says Adonai the Lord.")
