You shall be food for the fire, your blood shall be in the midst of the land; you shall be given over to oblivion, because I the Lord have spoken. […]

21:31.t: And because he was once speaking under the person of the sword about the king, or rather the kingdom, of Babylon, he keeps the μεταφορὰν [metaphor]. 'In the fire', he says, 'of my fury I will blow upon you, so as to have you consumed by fire; and I will hand you over to the hands of foolish and unskilled men, who have not the art of forging and sharpening swords, so that you may by no means be sharpened any more, be filed and flash to kill, but may be food for the fire, and your blood, which you shed with all looking on, may rather flow back upon you; and you shall be handed over to eternal oblivion; and may you perish forever, because I the Lord have spoken these things, for whom to have said is to have done'.

22:2.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, will you not judge the city of bloods? And you shall show her all her abominations, and you shall say: Thus says the Lord God: A city shedding blood in her midst, so that her time may come; and which made idols against herself, so as to be polluted. By your blood, which has been shed by you, you have sinned; and in your idols which you made you are polluted; and you have made your days draw near, and you have brought on the time of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all lands. Those that are near and those that are far from you will triumph over you (or will mock you), filthy one, noble one, great in ruin. Behold, the princes of Israel, each in his own arm, have been in you to shed blood. Father and mother they have treated with insults in you (or they have cursed father and mother), the stranger they have falsely accused in your midst, the orphan and the widow they have grieved (or have oppressed) in you. […]

22:4.t: First of all crimes, in place of God you have worshiped idols, and you have adored the works of your hands, and you have made the time of your years draw near, which for a long time was being announced and postponed, so that you might do penance. But according to your impenitent heart you treasure up wrath for yourself against the day of wrath. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all lands that are round about you, both near and far, which will triumph over you, or mock you, filthy, noble, great in ruin: filthy, because you have ceased to be clean; noble in evil, you who once surpassed all cities in nobility in good; great in ruin, so that the more lofty you were, the more heavily you should fall.

22:6.t: And meanwhile, to pass over the rest, I will enumerate a few things that took place in you: your princes, judging not by righteousness but by the strength of their might and of their arm, shed innocent blood in you; others treated father and mother with insults, or cursed their parents, though Scripture says: Whoever curses father and mother shall die the death; the stranger and the sojourner they oppressed in your midst, as though sojourning and exile from their homeland were not enough for them in place of every distress; the orphan and the widow they grieved, or oppressed, in you, so that those whose whole protection lies in the justice of the laws were not only grieved but oppressed by you; my sanctuaries, or holy things, you despised, and my sabbaths you polluted, so that you did not distinguish between holy and polluted, between the day decreed for religion and the rest of the sabbath for the worship of God, and the other days on which it is permitted by the law to work and to serve the needs of the flesh; […]

22:13.t: Hence I have taken on the bearing of the Lord in anger and have clapped my hands against your avarice and against the blood that has been shed in your midst, so that you may understand and recognize in your mind whether you can endure my wrath either in spirit or with your hands; for I the Lord have spoken and I will do it, so that, after you have been captured, Jerusalem, I will scatter you among the nations and winnow you into the air like useless chaff to be swept this way and that.

22:15.t: And I am of such great clemency that my severity is turned into mercy; for I will do everything so that your uncleanness may fail from you and you may recover your former purity; and when you have recovered it, I will possess you in the sight of all the nations, so that, when you have been possessed by me, you may then understand that I myself am the Lord'. If, however, we follow the interpretation of Symmachus and Theodotion, of whom the one says: And I will wound you (or I will pierce you through), the other: I will defile you in the sight of the nations, everything must be referred to the bad sense, although what is said above is contrary to this sense: And I will make your uncleanness fail from you; for the failing of uncleanness is the restoration of purity. I have discussed both editions together, so as to avoid enlarging the books.

22:18.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, the house of Israel has been turned into dross for me; all these are bronze and tin and iron and lead in the midst of the furnace; they have become the dross of silver. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have all been turned into dross, therefore behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem, with a gathering of silver and bronze and iron and tin and lead into the midst of the furnace, so that I may kindle a fire in it for smelting: so will I gather in my fury and in my anger, and I will rest, and I will smelt you, and I will kindle you in the fire of my fury, and you shall be smelted in the midst of it. As silver is smelted in the midst of the furnace, so shall you be in the midst of it; and you shall know that I am the Lord; that I have poured out my indignation upon you. […]

What we have understood of Jerusalem, let us understand of the state of souls, which were created pure by God and received gold in understanding and wisdom, and silver in speech and eloquence, so that what they have conceived in the mind they may unfold in words. Of silver we read: The utterances of the Lord are chaste utterances, silver tried by fire, proved for the earth, purged sevenfold. Of gold and silver alike Psalm 67 (68) speaks, in which it is written: If you sleep in the midst of the lots, the wings of a dove covered with silver, and the hinder parts (or the inner parts) of her back in the greenness (or paleness) of gold. All indeed the glory of the king's daughter is within, she who speaks in the Song of Songs: The king has brought me into his chamber. Whoever has slept and rested between the two testaments at once takes up the silvered wings of the dove, and will shine with the brightness of gold in the treasury of the heart. […]

Indeed, aside from a very few servants of God, what was the whole territory of Africa but one house of vice, like that bronze vessel of which the prophet said: "Woe to the bloody city! to the bronze vessel whose scum is therein, and whose scum hath not gone out from it, because the blood shall not go out from it!" He compared the city, as we see, to a bronze vessel and its iniquity to blood, that we might know that the iniquity of the people in a city is like blood seething in a brazen pot. And again, not unlike this is another saying of the Sacred Word: "The houses of Israel have all been made a mixture before me of brass and iron and tin and lead, in the midst is silver mixed with the mass. Therefore say this; thus saith the Lord God: 'Inasmuch as ye are all made one mass I shall blow upon you and melt you in the fires of my wrath.' "

How are the very dissimilar metals that the Scriptures have named melted together in one furnace? Surely in the diversity of metals the unlike qualities of men are figured. […]
22:18.s: On the Government of God, Book 7, Chapter 14

22:19.t: Just as, then, silver, which the metals mentioned above have corrupted, is put into the furnace so that, once the filth and the counterfeit substances have been removed, it may remain pure: 'so', he says, 'I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem and surround you with the Babylonian siege, so that I may kindle a fire in you for smelting; and what the immense heat of the flames does there, famine and pestilence do here, so that, after I have gathered you and kindled you in the fire of my fury, I may then rest and quell the pain of being despised by the vengeance of your punishments; and all this I will do so that, after I have poured out my indignation upon you, the end of your torment may be the knowledge of me, and you shall know that I am the Lord, the judge and requiter of all'. […]

22:24.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, say to her: You are a land unclean, and not rained upon in the day of fury. A conspiracy of prophets in her midst, like a lion roaring and seizing prey; they have devoured souls, they have taken wealth and price, they have multiplied her widows in her midst. Her priests have despised my law and have polluted my sanctuaries; between holy and profane they made no distinction, and between polluted and clean they did not discern, and from my sabbaths they turned away their eyes, and I was defiled in their midst. Her princes in her midst like wolves seizing prey, to shed blood and to destroy souls and greedily to pursue gains. And her prophets daubed them without tempering, seeing vain things and divining her falsehood, saying: Thus says the Lord God, when the Lord has not spoken. The people of the land they wronged with false accusation and plundered violently; […]

22:25.t: We wish to know what the dross of the city is, what the squalor of a land most hard and full of brambles and thorns. A conspiracy, he says, of prophets (or, according to the Seventy, of leaders) in her midst, who bear the likeness of a lion, of which Peter too writes: Our adversary the devil goes about like a roaring lion; and this lion and all his companions seek to devour not bodies but souls, and they take rewards and decide everything by money. That this happened to the people of the Jews at that time indeed, no one doubts; for because of the priests and the princes and the prophets the Lord brought evil upon them.

But in our Jerusalem too we often see this: those who, according to the Seventy, devour souls in power and take a price, so as to make many widows who have lost the Lord, their bridegroom; and these prophets form a faction and a conspiracy, so as to be one another's supporters and to do everything for the sake of shameful gain; the priests, who ought to be the guardians of the temple and from whose mouth the knowledge of the law is sought, violate the sanctuaries and make no distinction between holy and profane except that of money; they turn their eyes away from the sabbaths and do not ponder the rest of God, which lies in the knowledge of the Scriptures, nor do they say with the prophet: Unveil my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law, nor that word of the Apostle: But we all with unveiled face behold the glory of the Lord. Among such prophets and priests the Lord, standing in their midst, is defiled, of whom it is written: In the midst of you stands one whom you do not know.

22:27.t: The prophets, then, or leaders, are compared to lions; but the princes, whom we understand as men of a lower rank, imitate the rapine of wolves, so as to shed the blood not of bodies but of souls, and greedily pursue gains, by no means content with this: Those who serve the altar live by the altar, but, once they have come to the ministry of God, they amass the riches of Croesus.

22:28.t: Her prophets also, who foretell things to come, daubed them without tempering — which we also discussed above, that of the soothsaying prophets who, without an admixture of chaff, plastered a wall that is broken down by the rains; men of this kind see vain things, and do not so much prophesy as divine falsehood, saying to the wretched land: 'Thus says the Lord, this he promises', when the Lord has not spoken to them; and the people of the land, being an imitator not of God at all but of the earthly works of the princes and priests, did everything through false accusation and power, oppressing not the rich but the poor, of whom it is written: But the poor man does not bear threatening, and: The ransom of a man's soul is his own riches; […]

22:30.t: 'Amid such great', he says, 'vices and a multitude of crimes, I sought among them a man who could resist my anger and, after the pattern of Moses and Aaron and Samuel, set himself against my fire and my burning, and I could not find one — whence he said to Moses: Let me alone, and I will destroy this people —; and because I could not find one to resist me and hold me back, therefore I poured out all my indignation upon them and consumed them, not without measure and judgment, but so as to render their ways upon their own heads', either assigning to their authors the very sins they had committed, or surely upon the heads of the leader of the people, the prince and the prophets, of whom there was none who dared to resist the Lord in his anger, and on whose account the land, squalid and deserted, did not deserve to receive the rain of the Lord.

23:2.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother, and they committed fornication in Egypt; in their youth they committed fornication: there their breasts were subdued, and the teats of their puberty were broken (or, as is contained in the Seventy, there their breasts fell, and there they were deflowered). Their names were Oholah the greater (or the elder) and Oholibah her sister; and I had them (or they became mine) and they bore sons and daughters: and their names were Samaria Oholah and Jerusalem Oholibah. Oholah therefore committed fornication over me; and she went mad (or went off) after her lovers, after the Assyrians, who drew near to her, clothed in hyacinth, princes and magistrates, young men of desire (or chosen), all horsemen, riders of horses. And she bestowed her fornications upon them, the chosen sons of the Assyrians, all of them; and in the uncleannesses (or inventions) of all those over whom she went mad she was polluted. […]

23:4.t: According to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], we have discussed more fully in the prophet Hosea what Joseph, Ephraim, Samaria, Jezreel and Israel signify, and how they are opposed to the house of David and to Jerusalem, which signifies the Church — of whom Psalm 77 (78) also sounds: The sons of Ephraim, bending and shooting the bow, turned back in the day of battle, and again: He rejected the tabernacle of Joseph and chose the tribe of Judah; for the Lord chose the house of confession, the Church, and rejected the tabernacle of 'Joseph', which means 'increase'; and they, setting aside the law of God, added golden calves of their own worship —; and she is called 'Oolla', that is, 'tabernacle', not of God but of error and of demons; […]

23:5.t: And first Oholah, that is, Samaria, committed fornication over God, when she went mad after the Assyrians, who were clothed in hyacinth, and not just anyone of the people but leaders and magistrates, not men worn out with age but all young men, chosen horsemen, whose idols she followed and from whom, against the command of God, she requested help; and they came and polluted her, so that she did not abandon whatever she had done in her youth in Egypt —for the Egyptians too had lain with her in her youth, whose images she venerated, and there she was deflowered and her breasts were broken; and so great was the abundance of fornication that they are said not to have committed fornication with her but to have poured out their fornication —.

23:9.t: Therefore she was handed over to her lovers themselves, Pul and Tiglath-pileser and Shalmaneser, after whose lust she went mad; and they themselves uncovered her shame — τροπολογικῶς [tropologically], as of a harlot woman; but the uncovering of a city is captivity — ; and they led their sons and daughters captive and slaughtered her herself with the sword, so that she was butchered as an example to all women —and is celebrated, in the bad sense, in the talk of all of them — ; and they executed judgments and vengeances upon her —so as to leave nothing of safety in her, but the ten tribes are held in captivity to this day in the mountains and cities of the Medes to which they were transported —.

23:11.t: And when her sister Oholibah had seen this, she went mad with lust more than she, and shamelessly offered her fornication, beyond the fornication of her sister, to the sons of the Assyrians: to leaders and magistrates coming to her, clothed in varied garments (or costly), to horsemen who rode upon horses, and to youths all of outstanding form. And I saw that she was polluted: one way for both; and she increased her fornications. And when she had seen men painted on the wall, images of the Chaldeans expressed in colors, with their loins girded with belts, and dyed tiaras on their heads, with the appearance of all leaders (or of all the tristatae), in the likeness of the sons of Babylon and of the land of the Chaldeans in which they were born, she went mad over them with the lust of her eyes, and sent messengers to them in Chaldea. And when the sons of Babylon had come to her, to the bed of breasts (or of those turning aside), they polluted her with their debaucheries; […]

Moreover, according to tropology the understanding is difficult: how the Church can surpass heretical lust; unless perhaps we can say this, that the servant who knows the will of his master and does not do it will be beaten with many blows, and that heretics commit abominations outside and perish by shipwreck outside the ark of Noah, while churchmen, if, though following the true faith, they imitate Assyrian and Chaldean vices and follow the many-colored images of sins, deserve greater torments — or do we not send messengers to the 'Chaldeans', which means 'as it were demons', when we lay open and offer them the breasts to be broken in the bosom, where the lodging of the mind is, and, sated with pleasures, pass from some women to others; and desire not so much fornication as a number of harlots; and come to such madness that, after long years of the Lord's service, we return to Egypt and do the things we did in the world before we received the name of the faith? —.

23:14.t: But Jerusalem increased her fornications in this, that, seeing on the walls images of the Chaldeans, she went mad with lust and, deceived by their form and dress, sent messengers to them requesting help, and they came and polluted her.

23:17.t: And because pleasure is not perpetual but quickly brings satiety, polluted and sated with them, she withdrew from their covenant.

23:18.t: 'Therefore I too, seeing her foul deeds and fornications made public to all, withdrew from her, so that she who had outdone her sister's crimes might also surpass her sister in the magnitude of her punishments'.

23:19.t: She was of such wantonness that she committed all the errors of her youth at an age already more mature, and pursued the Egyptian vices in her lust for the Chaldeans too; for she once went mad in her bedding with the Egyptians, whose flesh is in the likeness of asses, with so copious an issue of seed, or private parts so huge, that they surpass the deformity of horses.

23:21.t: 'Nor did the wickedness of her youth cease; rather, she went back to it after she became mine, so that both in the wilderness and in the land of promise she sighed for the old lust in which she was deflowered and her breasts were broken and all her virginal beauty perished'.

23:22.t: Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will stir up all your lovers against you, with whom your soul was sated; and I will gather them against you round about, the sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, nobles and tyrants and princes, all the sons of the Assyrians, youths of outstanding form, all the leaders and magistrates, princes of princes, and renowned riders of horses; and they will come upon you equipped with chariot and wheel, a multitude of peoples: with breastplate and shield and helmet they will be armed against you on every side, and I will set judgment before them, and they will judge you with their judgments. And I will set my jealousy in you, which they exercise with you in fury: they will cut off your nose and your ears, and what remains they will cut down with the sword; they themselves will take your sons and your daughters, and your last will be devoured by fire. And they will strip you of your garments, and take away the vessels of your glory; […]

All of this is said under the metaphor of an adulteress, disfigured because of her adultery, so that she may no longer glory in her comeliness but blush in the hideousness which she has merited by the magnitude of her pleasures. Whatever is said τροπικῶς [figuratively] of Jerusalem can also be referred to the soul, which, joined by its virtues to the embrace of God, afterwards turned adulteress to vices and withdrew from him, and, all her crimes being laid open, was stripped and disfigured and shown to all, so that she may at some time desist from her wickedness; and may not glory in the dignity of her name, but, from her consciousness of evil and her remembrance of Egypt, may not dare any longer to lift her eyes to heaven; whence too her nose is cut off and her ears are amputated, because she had turned the odor of good fragrance into stench and had heard the judgment of blood; […]

23:23.t: The sons, I say, of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, nobles, tyrants and princes — in place of which the Hebrew has 'facud' and 'sue' and 'cue', which many understand as nations of the east, since we find names of this kind neither in the volume of Kings nor in Chronicles, nor even in Jeremiah, which describe the captivity of Jerusalem, nor in any other place of holy scripture; nor is it surprising if the Seventy set down the Hebrew names themselves, since Symmachus too and Theodotion agree in the same words — ; all', he says, 'the Assyrians, horsemen and youths of outstanding form, leaders and magistrates — or τριστάτας, which we have translated 'princes of princes', of whom we also read in Exodus: Chosen riders, τριστάτας, in place of which Latin simplicity translated 'ternos stratores' [grooms by threes]; and 'tristatae' is the name among the Hebrews for the second rank after the royal dignity, of whom it is written: Yet he did not attain to the first three; […]

23:28.t: For thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hated, into the hands with which your soul was sated, and they will deal with you in hatred, and take away all your labors, and leave you naked and full of disgrace. Your wickedness and your fornications have done these things to you, because you committed fornication after the nations, among whom you were polluted in their idols. You walked in the way of your sister, and I will give her cup into your hand. Thus says the Lord God: You will drink the cup of your sister, deep and wide — you will be for derision and for scorn: you who are most capacious, you will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow! —, and the cup of grief and sadness, the cup of your sister Samaria; and you will drink it and drain it to the dregs; and you will devour its fragments, and you will tear your breasts (or, as the Seventy translated, I will take away her feasts and new moons), for I have spoken, says the Lord. […]

23:31.t: 'In the ways', he says, 'of your sister Samaria you walked; therefore you must drink the cup of her whose sins you followed — and that a cup is often taken for punishments and torments, there are many examples, among which is this: A cup in the hand of the Lord, full of pure wine, mixed. And he has tilted it from this; yet its dregs are not emptied: all the sinners of the earth shall drink; and in Isaiah it is called 'the cup of ruin' and 'the draught of fury'; and God speaks to Jeremiah, saying: Take the cup of pure wine from my hand, and you shall give drink to all the nations to which I shall send you; and they shall drink and vomit, and go mad; for just as certain cathartics are given so that the noxious humor that is in bodies may be purged out, so the Lord too gives a most undiluted cup of torments, to take away from sinners whatever there is of gall and bitterness and restore them to their former health — ; […]

23:34.t: This that is said: And you will drink to the dregs; and you will devour its fragments, can be understood meaningfully of Jerusalem, which drank the cup of her sister Samaria last, and drained, as it were, the dregs of her torments to the bottom.

23:35.t: Since, therefore, you have done these things and forgotten me and cast me behind your body —or backward, because of the vices of the body, or behind the genitals, by which the foulness of turpitude is indicated —, therefore bear your wickedness and your impiety — that is, the punishments which you have merited by your impiety and crimes —'.

23:36.t: And the Lord spoke to me, saying: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah, and declare to them their crimes (or iniquities)? For they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands, and they have committed fornication with their idols (or inventions); moreover their sons too, whom they had borne to me, they offered to them to be devoured (or they led through the fire). But this too they did to me: they polluted my sanctuary on that day, and profaned my sabbaths. And when they sacrificed their sons to their idols, and entered my sanctuary on that day to pollute it, these things too they did in the midst of my house. They sent to men coming from afar, to whom they had sent a messenger; and so, behold, they came. For them you washed yourself (or when they had come, at once you bathed), and painted round your eyes with stibium, and adorned yourself with womanly finery; you sat on a beautiful couch, and a table was adorned before you; my incense and my ointment (or oil) you set upon it. […]

All these things were said τροπικῶς [figuratively] and under the type of adulteresses against Samaria and Jerusalem: that, delivered to the Assyrians and Chaldeans, they were led into captivity and their cities were burned up in fire, and the peoples were killed who had venerated the images of demons in place of God. These things can also be understood of the time after the coming of Christ: that righteous men from the peoples of the Gentiles, they themselves, judge the Samaritans and the Jews by comparison with themselves and deliver them to be devoured, those to whom the Lord had said: Your house will be left to you desolate, and: When you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, know that its desolation draws near; for to this day they are adulteresses and are crushed by the stones of the whole world, because they sent messengers to those who were far off and could not say: I am the Lord who draws near, and not from afar, says the Lord; […]

23:40.t: But neither were they content only with present adulteries, nor did it suffice them that, after sacrificing my sons, they made them their idols' or the demons', but, wanton also in foreign pleasures, they venerated the images of the Assyrians and Chaldeans. And when these had come, Oholibah, Jerusalem, you fulfilled for them the whole bearing of an adulteress: you washed your body, smeared your eyes with stibium, put on womanly adornment, sat on a couch prepared for lust, set out feasts with which to restore the strength of your lovers, broken by lust; my incense and ointment — which I had ordered to be made specially for me, and that soul to be exterminated from the people which wished to make it for private uses — you offered to idols, so as to gather a throng of peoples, or sang with every kind of musician, so as to please your lovers not only by sight but by hearing and smell and all the senses; […]

23:43.t: Wherefore I said to her, whether to Jerusalem or to Samaria or to both: So have you worn down your brow that you are by no means polluted in secret, nor do you heed the gaze either of a husband or of men, but like harlots you are prostituted publicly; they went in to you as to harlots, vying with one another in their desire to pollute you.

23:45.t: Remember that the Apostle also said, We shall judge angels. And our Lord said to His disciples, Ye shall sit on twelve thrones, and judge twelve tribes of the house of Israel. And Ezekiel said concerning righteous men, that they shall judge Ahola and Aholibah. Since, then, the righteous are to judge the wicked, He has made clear concerning them that they shall not come into judgment.
23:45.s: Demonstration 22 (Of Death and the Latter Times), Section 16

23:45.t: I will therefore deliver you for punishment to those to whom you delivered yourselves of your own accord for defilement; for they are righteous men in this, that at my command they torment the adulteress and parricide.

23:46.t: For thus says the Lord God: By the warning of your voice, O prophet, gather against them a multitude of peoples, and first let all their substance be plundered; then let them be stoned and pierced with swords; and let their sons and daughters be slaughtered, and their houses burn.

23:48.t: And all these things will be done so that impiety may be removed from the land, and all women and all provinces may learn from their punishments to avoid the like, so that, after you have received what you deserve and have borne the crimes of your idols, you may then know that I am the Lord'.

24:1.t: And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying: Son of man, write down for yourself the name of this day, on which the king of Babylon has been made strong against Jerusalem today. And you shall speak by a proverb a parable to the provoking house, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Set on the pot; set it on, I say, and put water into it. Heap its pieces into it, every good part, the thigh and the shoulder, choice pieces and full of bones; take the fattest of the flock, and arrange also piles of bones under it. Its cooking has boiled up, and its bones have been boiled through in the midst of it. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of bloods, to the pot whose rust is in it, and its rust has not gone out of it. Piece by piece, and by its pieces, cast it out; the lot has not fallen upon it, for its blood is in the midst of it; upon a most clear rock she poured it out; […]

It must also be noted how, from the beginning of the prophecy up to the present day when Jerusalem began to be besieged, the captivity comes in order. First the sword is called forth; then two ways are set out, Ammon and Jerusalem, and of these the lot falls for Nebuchadnezzar on the right-hand one; silver, bronze, tin, lead and iron are melted together in the city; the land too is not rained upon, but is overgrown with briers; afterwards, under the name of the two sisters Oholah and Oholibah, the sins of Samaria and Jerusalem are narrated, how the one has been captured and the other is to be captured; finally, in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, it is shown to Ezekiel, placed in captivity, and to those who were with him and had surrendered themselves with King Jeconiah, on what day the city began to be besieged, and the likeness of the cauldron is set forth so that, just as the flesh and the bones, heaped into the cauldron, are burned up by the fire, so the whole city is to perish […]

24:4.t: It is said also in Jeremiah: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" "A boiling pot," he says. See, then, that into this pot flesh is cast. This is written in Ezekiel. "And I cast," he says, "flesh into the pot": that it may become soft, and the hard may be converted to the Lord, and from a heart of stone may become a heart of flesh, so that where before it could not be written upon because of hardness, afterward it may be written upon because of softness. "I will kindle," he says, "this pot, and I will boil down the flesh and the bones, until they lose all moisture and filth." And see what is said afterward. "And let them learn," he says, "that I am the Lord." Great mercy, great sacrament. The flesh is cast into the pot, that it may be boiled down and may learn that he is the Lord.

24:6.t: But do you wish, prophet, to know what this cauldron is, or what the flesh or the bones are? Speak these things, says the Lord: Woe to the city of bloods, that is, Jerusalem, to the cauldron whose rust, that is, malice, is excessive, and although fire has been put beneath it, yet its rust has not gone out of it; for even when captured and tortured they persevered in their former crime. Consume it part by part and one by one, so that no one remains to be saved. The lot has not fallen upon it, so that some should perish and others be saved, but a common destruction has come upon all; for its blood, that is, its murders and the slaughter of sons, is in the midst of it. […]

Indeed, aside from a very few servants of God, what was the whole territory of Africa but one house of vice, like that bronze vessel of which the prophet said: "Woe to the bloody city! to the bronze vessel whose scum is therein, and whose scum hath not gone out from it, because the blood shall not go out from it!" He compared the city, as we see, to a bronze vessel and its iniquity to blood, that we might know that the iniquity of the people in a city is like blood seething in a brazen pot.
24:6.s: On the Government of God, Book 7, Chapter 14

24:9.t: Therefore say to the city of blood — of bloods not of one but of many —: Behold, I will make a great pyre in you, or I will bring a firebrand, which the common people call a titio [the everyday word for a firebrand], and I will set alight in you not only the soft and tender flesh but the hardest bones as well, and nothing shall remain in you that is not burned up by the fire.

24:11.t: And when both the flesh and the bones have been consumed and burned, set the empty cauldron itself upon the live coals, so that its bronze too may melt and be consumed and, the bronze being consumed, its rust too may perish; that is, when the city has been burned up by the fire, its malice may perish utterly with the city.

And the prophet seeing that all the remedies of this life will have been applied in vain for their healing, and already as it were despairing of their life, declares: "The bellows have failed in the fire, the founder hath melted in vain: for their wicked deeds are not consumed. Call them reprobate silver, for the Lord hath rejected them." And the Lord thus laments that to no purpose has He applied this salutary cleansing by fire to those who are hardened in their sins, in the person of Jerusalem crusted all over with the rust of her sins, when He says: "set it empty upon burning coals, that it may be hot, and the brass thereof may be melted; and let the filth of it be melted in the midst thereof. Great pains have been taken, and the great rust thereof is not gone out, no not even by fire. Thy uncleanness is execrable: because I desired to cleanse thee, and thou art not cleansed from thy filthiness." […]

24:12.t: But what does it profit to have done what was commanded? Not even by fire could the rust and malice of the cauldron and of the city be taken away, and there remains in it a wicked and execrable uncleanness — for this is what 'zemma' signifies. And he makes an apostrophe to the cauldron itself, that is, to the city itself — : I wished to cleanse you, and you were not cleansed of your filth, nor will you be able to be cleansed any more until I fulfil my indignation upon you.

24:14.t: I the Lord have spoken, and my sentence cannot pass away. The siege of the city has already come; I will do what I have threatened, and I will not pass over — as I have often done — your crimes, and I will spare no longer, nor will I be appeased toward you even if you multiply your prayers, but I will repay you your ways and your devices; indeed, I will judge you according to your works and your thoughts, so that in this too I may show my clemency' — like a physician who does not spare rotten flesh, so that the healthy limbs may be saved: he does not spare in order to spare, he is cruel in order to have mercy, and he considers not the pain of the patient but the healing of the wound, according to that saying of the Gospel, preferring that one member should perish rather than that the whole body be killed —.

24:16.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, behold, I am taking from you the desirable thing of your eyes with a stroke, and you shall not mourn nor weep, nor shall your tears flow. Groan in silence; you shall not make the mourning for the dead; let your crown be bound about you, and your shoes shall be on your feet, and you shall not veil your face with a mantle, nor eat the food of mourners. So I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening; and in the morning I did as he had commanded me. And the people said to me: Why do you not show us what these things mean that you are doing? And I said to them: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Speak to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your dominion and the desirable thing of your eyes, and that over which your soul trembles. And your sons and daughters, whom you have left behind, shall fall by the sword. […]

Let us come to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], if only it does not seem forced to the prudence of a cautious reader. No one doubts that the son of man is said to be the Lord Savior, who at the last hour, that is, at the evening of this world, lost his former wife, and did not weep for her nor veil his face with a mantle nor receive any consolation from men, and who foretold in the morning the things to come which were fulfilled in the evening, and again in the morning, at his second coming, proved accomplished what he had foretold was to come: that the sanctuary of the Jews, and what they had held desirable in their eyes and that over which their souls trembled, had been profaned, and that their sons too and their daughters had fallen by the Roman sword. […]

24:17.t: You shall not make the mourning for the dead (or, as the Seventy rendered: The groaning of the blood of the reins is mourning): by this he shows that his wife is going to die; for there follows immediately: And my wife died in the evening, which properly pertains to the union of the reins: nothing is more lovable to a man than a good wife, who is provided for a man by God, and to whom he is joined by the law of the Lord, and with whom he becomes one body. And what follows: Let your crown be bound about you, and your shoes shall be on your feet, signifies this: 'You shall have the hair which is shorn in mourning, and on your feet the shoes which mourners are accustomed to cast off' — whence David too, fleeing from his son Absalom and repenting over the murder of Uriah, walks with bare feet —. […]

24:18.t: 'I spoke,' he says, 'to the people the things the Lord had commanded me, and in the evening my wife died, the desirable thing of my eyes and the mourning of the loins and of the blood. And immediately, on the next day, in the morning, I did all the things that had been commanded me; and the people asked me why I had acted against the custom of all; and to those seeking the reasons for such great endurance I replied: The word of the Lord which came to me, that I should speak to the people of Israel, commanded these things: Behold, I (that is: now already) will profane my sanctuary, so that the temple may be burned and lie open to all foreigners and profane persons, the temple in which you had your pride, that is, your confidence and hope and the desire of your salvation, and at whose siege your souls were in dread; your sons too and your daughters, whom famine and pestilence had left remaining to you, I will consume with the sword, so that whatever I have done, you too may do'.

24:22.t: When custom is observed in mourning, the grief is moderate; but when so great a necessity of evils presses upon men that it is greater than all lamentation, each one, anxious about his own death, does not groan over the miseries of others, even though they are his nearest. 'You shall do nothing,' he says, 'of what is customarily done in mourning, but, when the city and the temple have been set on fire, you will be stunned at the magnitude of the evils; you will not cut your hair nor walk with bare feet, you will not mourn nor veil your faces with a mantle nor receive food from those who console you, but you will waste away, and you will be consumed in your iniquities, and you will scarcely have free groaning, lest you offend the pride of the victors if you are seen to weep publicly; so that Ezekiel the prophet may be a portent to you, and all that he did not do at the death of his wife, you may not do at the overthrow of the city and the temple'.

24:25.t: And yet more plainly: 'O son of man,' he says, 'at the time when I take away from them their strength — the confidence of the temple, as we have said —, and the joy of dignity and that in which they had their only hope, and the desire in which their souls rested, and besides their sons and their daughters — understood from the above: — I take away, at that time,' he says, 'when one fleeing from Jerusalem, or one who has escaped, comes to you, saying that the city has been overthrown, then you, who before had been silent and had no free groaning, and were of such great endurance that at the death of your wife and in the pain of your loins you did not shed a tear, will open your mouth and speak, not to him who has come but with him, so that whatever you had foretold was to come, he may announce as now accomplished; […]

25:1.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set (or make firm) your face against the Ammonites and you shall prophesy concerning them, and you shall say to the Ammonites: Hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God: Because you said: Well done, well done, over my sanctuary (or because you rejoiced over my sanctuary) because it was profaned, and over the land of Israel because it was made desolate, and over the house of Judah because they were led into captivity, therefore I will hand you over to the sons of the east (or Cedem) as an inheritance; they shall set up their sheepfolds in you, and they shall pitch their tents in you; they themselves shall eat your fruits, and they themselves shall drink milk (or your richness). And I will make Rabbath a dwelling for camels (or the city of Ammon pastures for camels), and the Ammonites a lair for cattle, and you shall know that I am the Lord. […]

25:2.t: According to tropology we can understand the Ammonites — who were begotten of the seed of Lot in a cave, and begotten in drunkenness and incest — as all the heretics, of whom the apostle John also says: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us; these have sprung from 'inclination' — for this is what 'Lot' is rendered in our language —, because: All have turned aside, together they have become useless; there is none who does good, there is not even one. Against these the prophet's face is set, or made firm, so that it may crush them by its severity, and it says to them: 'Because you mocked my Church in the time of persecution, and because my sanctuary had been profaned through various vices, whether by the vice of those who served me or by the cruelty of the enemies who persecuted my own, and because the land of Israel too, the senses that see God, was desolate of the choir of virtues, and because the sons of the house of Judah — the house […]

25:6.t: Nor was it enough for the Ammonites to mock and say 'Well done, well done' over the temple and sanctuary of the Lord, which had been profaned by the entry of various nations; but so great was the wantonness of their mocking that the whole people together clattered with hands and feet and shouted with all the passion of the heart, because the land of Israel was desolate. Therefore not through angels nor through other ministries, but the Lord himself, stretching out his hand to strike, will hand it over for plunder — not at all to camels and flocks of sheep but, more plainly, to the nations — so that it may be utterly uprooted from the number of the peoples, and perish, and be brought to nothing; and after it has been crushed, then it may understand that he himself is the Lord, who judges all things and has power over all lands.

And again he reproaches them for having mocked with excessive passion of heart at the ruins of the people of God, and for having thought the land of Israel utterly deserted, for which they deserve the hand of the avenging God, so that those who had exceeded the measure of exultation and joy over the ruin of the house of Judah are not handed over to the sons of the east at all, but become a plunder for all the nations, and are slain from among the peoples, and perish, and are crushed, and are to be believed to belong not at all to the stock of Abraham but to all the nations; and then, by the greatness of their misfortunes and by their own crushing and the slaughter of their people, they may know that he himself is the Lord. […]

25:8.t: Thus says the Lord God: Because Moab and Seir said: Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations, therefore behold, I will open the shoulder of Moab, from its cities, I say, and from its borders, the glorious places of the land, Bethiesimoth and Beelmeon and Cariathaim, to the sons of the east together with the Ammonites; and I will give it as an inheritance, so that there may be no more remembrance of the Ammonites among the nations. And upon Moab I will execute judgments, and they shall know that I am the Lord. (LXX: "Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because Moab ※ and Seir ⁚ said: Behold, the house of Judah is like all the nations, therefore behold, I will loosen the shoulder of Moab from the cities of its promontories, the chosen land, the house of Bethiesimuth above the spring of the maritime city, the sons of the east over the Ammonites; I have given it to him as an inheritance, so that there may be no remembrance of the Ammonites among the nations. […]

But to this day 'Moab', which means 'from the father', and 'Seir', which is rendered 'hairy' and 'shaggy', looks down on and despises the house of Judah, in which is the true confession, and thinks that it can be overthrown as easily as the fortifications of the other cities are overthrown.

25:9.t: Therefore, not a long time afterward but at the present moment, the Lord threatens that he will loosen, or open, the shoulder of Moab — that is, its strength and might — from its cities, so that the Babylonian conqueror may enter in to them too, and the cities in Moab may cease to be, and in its borders and boundaries the glorious cities may be destroyed whose names he sets down: 'Bethiesimoth and Beelmeon and Cariathaim', for which the Seventy, intending I know not what, translated 'the house of Bethiesimuth', although this word signifies 'a deserted village', while 'Beelmeon' too is to this day a very large village in Moab, which they rendered 'above the spring', and 'Cariathaim' 'a maritime city'; and it too is handed over, together with the Ammonites, to the sons of the east, namely the Babylonians, according to the sense which we have expounded against the Ammonites. […]

Hence the Lord threatens that he will open, or loosen, all the strength of the Moabites, so that they may cease to have cities and may no longer trust in the dialectical art, but that all its boundaries, which he calls promontories because of the dashing of the waves, may be destroyed, and that the glorious and chosen lands — 'Bethiesimoth', which means 'house of solitude' and 'deserted', and 'Beelmeon', which is likewise rendered 'having a spring' or 'above the spring', and 'Cariathaim', which the Seventy translated 'a maritime city' — may perish; for although they have the strength of fighters, and the glorious go forth to battle with the art of fighting, and advance hedged about and fortified on every side, yet their glorious land is not a house of habitation but a house of solitude; […]

25:12.t: Thus says the Lord God: Because Idumaea took vengeance, to avenge itself on the sons of Judah, and sinned in transgressing and sought vengeance on them, therefore thus says the Lord God: I will stretch out my hand over the Idumaeans, and I will take away from it man and beast, and I will make it desert from the south, and those who are in Dedan shall fall by the sword. And I will lay my vengeance on Idumaea by the hand of my people Israel, and they shall do in Edom according to my anger and my fury, and they shall know my indignation, says the Lord God. (LXX: "Thus says the Lord Adonai: Because Idumaea acted so that they avenged a vengeance on the house of Judah, and they kept the memory of evil and avenged themselves with vengeance, therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: I will stretch out my hand over Idumaea, and I will slay from it man and beast, and I will make it desert, and those fleeing from Theman shall fall by the sword. […]

According to tropology, this seems to me the sense: Idumaea is called 'earthly' and 'fleshly', which rises up against the spirit so that we do not do the things that are of the spirit, and hastens to draw to itself the soul placed in the middle, and wishes to repay vengeance on the sons of Judah, to whom it had formerly been subject, and remembers the old pain, that it was not in its own power, and therefore seeks vengeance on those who, withdrawing from the flesh, followed the spirit; therefore this Lord, being the avenger of the sons of Judah, stretches out his hand over Idumaea and takes away from it man and beast — whatever it seems to have either of reason or of simple faith — so as to reduce it to solitude, and of 'Theman', which means 'failing', and 'Dedan', which itself signifies 'kinship', he slew all with the sword which he placed in the hand of his people Israel, so that Edom may be overthrown, and feel the anger and fury of the Lord, and understand that his vengeance has served to this end: that it […]

25:13.t: Therefore not through angels nor through anyone else, but the Lord himself, stretching out his hand over Idumaea, took away from it man and beast, and reduced its cities to desert, that is, 'Theman', which we rendered 'south', from which, and from the other city, Dedan, the slain will fall by the sword; 'and when they have avenged themselves on Judah, I will lay vengeance on the Idumaeans by the hand, or in the hand, of my people Israel, so that they may be crushed by those on whom they exercised vengeance, who will do in Edom, or Idumaea, according to my anger and fury, so as to fulfil my indignation, and so that, through the hands of my people Israel, my anger may rage against the hostile nation, and they may understand that, against the unjust vengeance of Idumaea, my vengeance was just,' says Adonai the Lord.

25:15.t: Thus says the Lord God: Because the Philistines acted in vengeance, and avenged themselves with their whole soul, slaying, and fulfilling old enmities, therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will stretch out my hand over the Philistines, and I will slay the slayers, and destroy the remnants of the maritime region; and I will execute great vengeances on them, rebuking in fury, and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I have laid my vengeance on them. (LXX: "Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Because the foreigners acted in vengeance, and stirred up retribution, mocking from the soul, so as to destroy for ever, therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I will stretch out my hand over the foreigners, and I will destroy (or slay) the Cretans, and destroy the remnants of the shore; and I will execute great vengeances on them in the retribution of fury, and they shall know that I am Adonai the Lord, when I have laid my vengeance on them.") […]

26:2.t: And it came to pass in the eleventh year, on the first (or one) of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, because Tyre (or Sor) has said of Jerusalem: Aha, the gates of the peoples (or nations) are broken, she is turned to me, I shall be filled, she is laid waste (or she who was full is laid waste); therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, O Tyre, and I will make many nations come up to you, as the surging sea comes up; and they shall break down the walls of Tyre and destroy her towers, and I will scrape (or winnow) her dust from her, and I will make her a most clear (or most gleaming) rock. There shall be a drying of dragnets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord God; and she shall be for plunder to the nations. Her daughters also who are in the field (or in the plain) shall be slain by the sword, and they shall know that I am the Lord. The order of the prophecy is woven together in sequence. […]

26:7.t: But it is doubtful to no one that, according to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who comes from the north, is understood as the devil, who, though he is a most harsh wind and a left-hand one, is called by the name 'right-hand', claiming for himself the dignity of the name; and he is the king of kings and of all the kingdoms which he showed to the Lord, when he said to him: All these have been handed over to me, and I will give them to you if you fall down and worship me. He has horses and chariots, of which it is written: A horse is deceitful for safety, and: All who mount horses have fallen asleep, and in another place: Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea.

For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring to Tyre (or to you, Sor) Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north, king of kings, with horses and chariots and horsemen and a company and a great people. Your daughters who are in the field he shall slay with the sword, and he shall surround you with siegeworks, and heap up a mound round about, and raise the shield against you, and he shall direct mantlets and rams (or lances) against your walls, and destroy your towers with his weaponry. By the flood of his horses their dust shall cover you; at the sound of horsemen and wheels and chariots your walls shall be shaken, when he has entered your gates as through the entry of a city laid waste (or as one entering a city from the plain). With the hoofs of his horses he shall trample all your streets, your people he shall cut down with the sword, and your noble statues shall fall to the ground (or he shall bring down the substance of your strength to the ground). […]

26:8.t: He slays the daughters of Tyre, souls placed in distress and in a kind of prison of sins, in the field and the widest plain, and surrounds Tyre with his siegeworks, so as to hold her shut in, so that no one from her can escape the dominion of the Babylonian king; he destroys her walls and overthrows her towers, and whatever she may have had in the way of doctrines trembles violently at the flood of his horses and the sound of his horsemen and the clatter of wheels and chariots; and he will enter her gates with no one preventing him, and the hoofs of his horses will trample the streets of the city — for wide and spacious is the way that leads to death —, and he will cast down to the ground all her substance — or the noble statues, by which they had fashioned for themselves images of falsehood, of which it is written: Lord, in your city you will scatter their image —; and, the walls destroyed, the noble houses too will be overthrown which she had prepared for herself and in which she exulted; […]

26:11.t: Is this the case in Aquitania alone? Let us pass under review other parts of the world also, and not speak exclusively of the Gauls. Have not the same crimes or greater ones destroyed the provinces of Spain? Even if the divine wrath had handed these lands over to any other barbarians you might name, the enemies of chastity in them would have suffered tortures worthy of their vices. But as an added evidence of the condemnation of their shamelessness they were delivered into the hands of the Vandals, the most shamefast of barbarians. In the captivity of Spain God wished to give a twofold evidence of his hatred of carnal lust and love of chastity, when he put the Vandals in command solely on account of their preeminent chastity and subjected the Spaniards to them solely on account of their surpassing lewdness. What do I mean by this? Were there not anywhere in the world stronger barbarians to whom the Spanish lands might be surrendered? Many, without doubt, nay, all of them were stronger, if I am not mistaken. […]
26:11.s: On the Government of God, Book 7, Chapter 7

26:14.t: But what follows: Nor shall you be built any more, seems to raise a question: how has she not been built, when today we see her as the most noble and most beautiful city of Phoenicia? — whence some will have it that Tyre is to suffer these things in the last time, and is not to be built afterwards —; but how will they be able to keep to the person of Nebuchadnezzar — especially since we read in what follows that Nebuchadnezzar besieged Tyre and did not receive the wages of his labor, and that Egypt was therefore handed over to him, because he had served the sentence of God in the siege of Tyre —? Those who contradict this history say that they have read the Greek histories and those of the Phoenicians, and especially of Nicolaus of Damascus, and others of the barbarians, and have found nothing about a siege of the city of Tyre by the Chaldeans; […]

26:15.t: Thus says the Lord God to Tyre: Shall not the isles be shaken at the sound of your fall and the groaning of your slain, when they have been killed in your midst? And all the princes of the sea shall come down from their seats, and shall take off their spoils, and cast away their varied garments; and they shall be clothed with astonishment, they shall sit on the ground, and, dumbfounded at your sudden fall, they shall marvel. And taking up a lamentation over you, they shall say to you: How you have perished, you who dwell in the sea, renowned city, who were strong in the sea with your inhabitants, whom all shall dread! Now the ships shall be astonished in the day of your terror, and the isles in the sea shall be troubled, because no one goes out from you. (LXX: "For thus says the Lord God to Sor: Shall not the isles be shaken at the voice of your fall, when your wounded groan, when the sword has been drawn in your midst? […]

26:19.t: For thus says the Lord God: When I make you a desolate city like the cities that are not inhabited, and bring up the deep upon you, and many waters cover you, and I drag you down with those who go down into the pit (or to those who go down into the ditch) to the everlasting people, and set you in the uttermost land (or in the depth of the lands) like the ancient wastes, with those who are led down into the pit (or go down into the ditch), so that you are not inhabited, and I give glory in the land of the living (or so that you do not rise again in the land of the living), I will reduce you to nothing (or I will give you to destruction), and you shall not be, and when sought you shall not be found any more forever, says the Lord God. Join what has been said with what preceded. […]

This we have said briefly about Tyre μεταφραστικῶς [by way of paraphrase]; it can also be referred to those who, set in the distress of this world, are led down to the underworld and are covered by the deeps and waves of punishments, and are dragged to the lower parts of the earth, and are joined to those who are in the ancient wilderness, and are led down into the pit or the everlasting ditch, so that they are no longer inhabited by the Holy Spirit; of whom it is written: The ungodly, when he has fallen into the depth of evils, despises; and henceforth they will not be in the land of the living, but will perish, and be reduced to nothing, and cease to be to God. These testimonies are made use of by those who say that the punishments of the ungodly, and not of sinners, are perpetual: of the ungodly who, sought by God, were not found, and have ceased to be forever, because by their own fault they lost him who says: I am the life.

26:21.t: And this is to be noted: that Tyre is sought by him who came to seek and to save what had perished, and who, leaving the ninety-nine sheep on the mountains, seeks the one straying sheep — the woman too who had lost one drachma seeks and finds it, and calls together her neighbors to share her joy —; but if Tyre, when sought, is not found, the fault is not the seeker's but his who has fled the hand of the good shepherd. 'And no more', he says, 'shall you be forever' — or, as is written in the Hebrew 'lolam' and in the Greek αἰών [age], it signifies 'one age', according to that passage of Isaiah, who says that after seventy years Tyre is to be restored to her whole state; and they say that 'one age', that is, the span of a human lifetime, is reckoned at the number of seventy years, as the psalmist says: The days of our years in them are seventy years; but if in the strong, eighty years; whatever is beyond is toil and pain —.

27:2.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: You therefore, son of man, take up a lamentation over Tyre, and you shall say to Tyre, which dwells at the entrance of the sea, the trade of the peoples to many islands (or from many islands): Thus says the Lord God. If I should wish to comprehend the whole prophecy against Tyre, or over the lamentation of Tyre, in a single discourse, I shall both make it long and obscure the reader's understanding, since he cannot hold everything in mind at once, especially the places in which the edition of the Seventy differs from the Hebrew in this passage, that is, what they have added or what they have taken away. Therefore we shall be content with our own translation, and wherever they disagree we shall attach theirs alongside, leaving the perfect knowledge of all things to God, and we shall briefly point out what seems right to us in each point. He who is lamented is still a concern to the one by whom he is lamented; […]

27:3.t: Tyre, then, or Sor, according to the letter, dwells at the entrance of the sea, either because it was formerly an island or because it receives ships coming from the deep into a most safe harbor, and it is the trade of the peoples to many islands, or from many islands, which indeed continues to this day, so that the commerce of almost all nations is carried on in it. But following the interpretation we have begun, let us refer whatever is said of Tyre to the συνοχὴν, that is, the 'straits', of this world, which is set in the evil one and is hemmed in and battered by various disturbances as if by waves — of traders of this sort it is told also in the Psalms in mystical language: Those who go down to the sea in ships, doing business in many waters, these have seen the works of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep —.

O Tyre, you have said: I am of perfect beauty (or you have said: I have surrounded myself with beauty), and set in the heart of the sea. The first charge against Tyre is that, if she seems to have anything good, she thinks it not God's but her own, and reckons all the beauty that came to her from various regions to be the work of her own diligence and strength; for she said: I am of perfect beauty, or: I have surrounded myself with beauty, although she is set in the heart, that is, in the middle, of the sea, and is tossed about like an island, and is shattered by the surge and the dashing of the waves. That the heart of the sea signifies its middle, that prophetic saying also shows: Therefore we will not fear when the earth is troubled, and the mountains are carried into the heart of the sea. Their waters roared and were troubled; and our Lord too is said to have descended into the heart of the earth, that is, into its middle, and to the underworld. […]

27:4.t: Your neighbors, who built you, have filled up your beauty; with firs from Sanir they constructed you, with all the planking of the sea; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you. (In place of which, intending I know not what, the Seventy translated thus: Beelim your sons surrounded you with beauty; cedar from Sanir was built for you; they took thin boards of cypress from Lebanon to make masts of fir for you; for the word 'Beelim' is not found at all in this place among the Hebrews, but in place of 'Beelim' is written 'gebulaich', which means 'your borders'; in what they said, 'your sons', too, they were deceived by the ambiguity of the word and the similarity of the writing, since the same letters, with a different pronunciation, are read as 'of masons' and 'of sons', 'bonaich' and 'benaich'.) […]

27:5.t: And he speaks as if to a ship, τροπικῶς [figuratively] signifying the beauty of the city and its abundance of all things, so that, after he has described all its equipment — mast, yards, oars, sails, prow, keel, ropes, coverings, hides, and the other things which the use of the best-fitted ships requires — he may then announce that a storm and the south wind, by which the greatest waves will be stirred up, will come upon it, and that it will be subjected to shipwreck — by which he signifies the overthrow of the Tyrian city by king Nebuchadnezzar, or, as many think, by Alexander king of the Macedonians, who is related to have besieged and taken that very city in six months, after he had defeated Darius in Lycia —. […]

27:6.t: Oaks from Bashan they hewed into your oars, your benches they made for you of Indian ivory, and cabins from the islands of Italy. (LXX: "From Bashan they made your oars, your temples they made for you of ivory, forest houses from the islands of Chetthiim.") How great the beauty of the ship and of its equipment, that it should have oars of cedar — not from just anywhere but from Bashan —, and benches of ivory, and cabins — or storerooms in which the most precious merchandise is laid up — from the islands of 'Chetthiim' — which we have rendered as 'Italy' —, from that region which is nearer to Greece, understanding by it all the parts of the western islands! Let us say, then, according to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], that the oars of the Tyrian ship are made from Bashan — of which it is also written in the Psalms: The Lord said: From Bashan I will turn back, I will turn back from the depth of the sea; Basan in our language means 'ignominy' —; […]

27:7.t: Embroidered byssus from Egypt was woven for you into a sail, to be set on the mast; hyacinth and purple from the islands of Elishah became your covering. (LXX: "Byssus with embroidery from Egypt was made for you into a spread to surround you with glory, and to cover you with hyacinth and purple from the islands of Elisee, and they became your coverings.") Because Tyre had said: I am of perfect beauty (or: I myself have surrounded myself with beauty), she is convicted as to what she has received from each region, according to that word of Scripture: What do you have that you have not received? But if you have received it, why do you glory as if you had not received it? So it is described what each province sends, according to that line of Vergil: India sends ivory, the soft Sabaeans their incense, But the hardy Chalybes iron, and Pontus the rank castoreum, and the rest. Byssus grows most of all in Egypt, and from it was woven the sail of the Tyrian ship, which is hung on the mast; […]

27:8.t: The inhabitants of Sidon and the Aradians were your rowers; your wise men, O Tyre, became your pilots. The elders of Byblus and its prudent men provided sailors for the service of your varied equipment. All the ships of the sea and their sailors were among the people of your trade. (LXX: "Your princes who dwelt in Sidon and the Aradians were your rowers; your wise men, Sor, who were in you, these were your pilots. The elders of Byblus and its wise men were in you: these strengthened your counsel. And all the ships of the sea and their rowers became yours toward the west of the west.") He had said above: Your neighbors, who built you, have filled up your beauty; before he comes to those who dwell far off, he describes the help of the nearest provinces: 'Your inhabitants,' he says, 'or the princes of Sidon and of Aradus, which is a neighboring island, are your rowers; […]

So much meanwhile according to the letter; but according to the mystical understandings, since 'Sidonians' means 'hunters', and 'Aradians' 'those who put down', we say that Tyre, the glorious and most proud city, which is afterwards to be shattered when the wind blows, has citizens or princes who are hunters — of whom it is written: Our soul has been snatched like a sparrow from the snare of the hunters; for where we read 'of the hunters', in the Hebrew is written 'of the Sidonians' —; these hunt: they draw unwary souls, set on high, down to earthly things, and they become rowers to lead them to shipwreck; but the wise men of Tyre, who are taken in the bad sense, in which the sons of darkness are wiser than the sons of light, they themselves steer what has been made ready for Tyre for shipwreck; […]

27:9.t: 'The old men or elders of Byblus and its prudent men provided sailors for the service, or strengthened the counsel of Tyre, and provided varied equipment; and all the ships of the sea and their sailors were among the people of the Tyrian trade, or toward the west of the west'.

27:10.t: Persians and Lydians and Libyans were in your army; your men of war hung up shield and helmet in you for your adornment (or hung up targes and helmets in you, they gave you your glory). That the Persians were most brave, whose king Cyrus, as is foretold by the prophecy of Isaiah, having overthrown Astyages king of the Medes, captured Babylon, both sacred and secular history relate; that the Lydians too were reckoned at that time among the most robust nations, whose king Croesus was captured by the same Cyrus, Xenophon writes most fully; and that Libyans came against Jerusalem with the Troglodytes and Ethiopians, we read in the volume of Chronicles; because in those times they were most flourishing and fighters famous in battle, they are recorded to have been defenders of the Tyrian city, and to have hung up shields and helmets on the battlements of the walls to terrify enemies. […]

27:11.t: The sons of the Aradians with your army were upon your walls round about; but the Pygmies too, who were in your towers, hung their quivers on your walls all around; they completed your beauty. (LXX: "The sons of the Aradians and your strength were upon your walls round about; guards were in your towers; they hung their quivers upon your battlements all around; they perfected your beauty.") The word 'gamadim' the first edition of Aquila translated 'Pygmies', Symmachus 'Medes', the Seventy 'guards', Theodotion 'gomadim', the Hebrew word itself; we see to this day the island of Aradus, which is entirely a city, and has opposite it the town of Antaradus, and is near to Tyre, and lies out off the Phoenician shore of the mainland. These are in the army of the Tyrian city and are the guards of its towers, and they hang their quivers all around and complete its beauty, so as to show that they are archers; […]

27:12.t: The Carthaginians were your traders, by reason of the multitude of all riches; with silver, iron, tin and lead they filled your fairs. Not only in the present place, but also in Isaiah, where it is written: Howl, ships of Carthage, the other translators rendered the Hebrew word as 'Tharsis'; and that these are a colony of the Tyrians no one doubts; they themselves, from the regions of the west, filled the fairs of Tyre with silver, iron, tin and lead. 'Tharsis' in our language sounds 'exploration of joy'; but we ought not to understand the explorers here in a good sense, such as Moses had sent to explore the land of promise, but in the contrary sense, such as the Apostle too says that he avoids: Because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who came in to explore our liberty which we have in Christ, and of whom Joseph speaks: You are explorers; […]

27:13.t: Greece, Tubal and Meshech, they were your dealers; they brought slaves and vessels of bronze to your people. From the house of Togarmah they brought horses and horsemen and mules to your market. (LXX: "All Greece and the parts adjacent to it, they were your traders in the souls of men, and they gave vessels of bronze as your merchandise. From the house of Togarmah they gave horses and horsemen and mules as your fairs.") 'The Ionians,' he says, '— who in Hebrew are called Iauan —, and Tubal — that is, the eastern Iberians, or the Spaniards from the regions of the west, who are called by this name from the river Iberus —, and Meshech — whom we understand as the Cappadocians, whose metropolis, which was later called Caesarea by Augustus Caesar, is to this day called Mazaca in their own language —, these made the precious commerce of Tyre, bringing slaves and bronze vessels from Corinth to Tyre, and from the house of Togarmah, that is, from Phrygia, horses and horsemen and mules, of which that province once had the […]

27:15.t: The sons of Dadan were your traders. In place of which, intending I know not what, the Seventy translated 'the sons of the Rhodians', unless perhaps by the deceptive similarity of the first letter, so that instead of 'Dadan' they read 'Radan', which itself is also the largest of the Cyclades, and was once a most powerful city in the Ionian Sea and glorious in naval combat, and, because of its very safe harbor, the resort of all merchants. And since 'Rhodians' is rendered in our language 'seeing judgment', it is now said tropologically of those who discern the truth of judgment and do not themselves do it, as the Apostle says: Therefore you are inexcusable, O man, every one who judges; for in that in which you judge another, you condemn yourself, for you do the same things which you judge. But it is better to take 'Dadan' as the name of another place, as it is found in the Hebrew and among the other translators.

Therefore, according to the Seventy, the sons of the Rhodians, traders of Tyre, multiplied its trade from very many islands; according to the Hebrew, after the sons of Dadan, its traders, islands too of various nations increased its merchandise, bringing teeth of ivory from India and ebony wood — which, being of a black color, are most precious —, and exchanged them for other wares of Tyre.

Many islands were the trade of your hand: they exchanged teeth of ivory and of ebony at your price. The Syrian was your trader because of the multitude of your works: drop, purple and checkered cloths and byssus and silk and chodchod they set out in your market. (LXX: "From the islands they multiplied your trade: elephants' teeth, and to those who were brought in you paid your wages. Men were your trade from the multitude of your market: in aphec, stacte, and many-threaded cloths from Tharsis, and ramoth and chodchod they gave as your fairs.") The edition of the Seventy differs much from the Hebrew in the present place; therefore a few things must be said according to each, lest, occupied with the wares of Tyre, we pass too slowly to the remaining prophecies. The sons of Dadan, the traders of Tyre, multiplied its trade from many islands, so that they gave elephants' teeth to those who came to its commerce, and had men in the fairs because of the multitude of the trade. […]

But from many islands, to pass to the ἀναγωγὴν, which are beaten by the salty and bitter waves of this age, the traders of Dadan bring teeth of ivory, promising the whiteness of eloquence, of which it is written: From the ivory houses, from which the daughters of kings delighted you in your honor; but they are not white, nor do they imitate the bride of whom it is said: Who is this who comes up made white, leaning upon her kinsman?, but are of ebony, of a black color, who cannot change their blackness, as Jeremiah says: If the Ethiopian will change his skin and the leopard his mottling. 'The Syrian' too, that is, 'aram', who means 'lofty' and swells with pride, is a trader of Tyre, and in the multitude of the Tyrian works he brings in the knowledge falsely so called, promising many varieties and 'stacte' of the best odor, and purple of royal dignity, and checkered cloths from the dialectical art, and byssus, for which the Seventy translated 'Tharsis', given over to the works of the earth, and silk, for which in the […]

27:16.t: 'The Syrian' too was a trader of Tyre, for which in the Hebrew is set down 'aram', in whose place the Seventy translated 'men', reading 'adam' for 'aram', deceived, as above, by the similarity of the letters 'res' and 'daleth' [r and d]. And to this day there remains in the Syrians an inborn ardor for trade: they run about through the whole world out of desire for gain, and they have such a madness for trading that, now that the Roman world has been seized, they seek riches amid swords and the slaughter of the wretched, and flee poverty through dangers; men of this kind are the traders of Tyre who deal in many-threaded cloths, purple and checkered cloths, and who set out byssus too, and silk and chodchod, in the market for her. For 'purple', which all translated, the Seventy rendered 'stacte', that is, 'drop'; […]

27:17.t: Judah and the land of Israel, they were your dealers in first wheat; balsam and honey and oil and resin they set out in your fairs. (LXX: "Judah and the sons of Israel, these were your traders in the commerce of grain and in ointments; first honey and oil and resin they gave in your fairs.") The Hebrew word 'phanag' Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion translated just as it is set down among the Hebrews; for it the Seventy rendered 'ointments', we 'balsam'. It is told, moreover, with what supplies the land of Judea, which is now called Palestine, abounds: grain, balsam, honey and oil and resin, which are brought by Judah and Israel to the fairs of Tyre. And since the letter is plain, according to the spiritual sense we say: the land of confession and the understanding of one who sees God, which refers to the Church, ought not to bring to Tyre the first wheat, which, falling into the earth, is multiplied and is taken for the word of God: for not by bread alone does man live, but by every word of God; […]

27:18.t: The Damascene was your trader in the multitude of your works, in the abundance of various riches, in rich wine, in wool of the best color. (LXX: "Damascus was your trader in the multitude of your works, out of the multitude of all your strength: wine from Chelbon and wool from Miletus.") For 'rich wine', which Symmachus translated, both in Aquila and Theodotion and in the Hebrew itself it has 'wine from Chelbon'; and again, where we have put 'wool of the best color' or 'shining', Aquila and Theodotion translated 'in wool of Soor'. It signifies, moreover, that among the other trades of Tyre, very rich wine and choice wool were brought to its fairs from Damascus, which we see to this day. […]
