35:2.t: Set, he says, (or turn) your face against Mount Seir; and he says 'turn' significantly: from one prophecy to another prophecy; and 'face': not of the body but of the mind — of which the Apostle also speaks: But we all, with unveiled face beholding the glory of the Lord —; and Mount 'Seir', which means 'shaggy' and 'hairy', is to be taken as the opposing power that presided over the nation of the sons of Esau and had raised itself up against the people of 'Iuda' [Judah], that is, of 'confession' and of the true faith — but if a prudent reader objects, how in this place 'Seir', that is, 'shaggy' and 'hairy', is understood in a bad sense when Elijah too was called a hairy man, I shall answer briefly: it is written of Esau that he was red and shaggy like a hide, but of Elijah only that he was a hairy man; in Esau, who, bloodthirsty and bloodstained, is compared to a shaggy hide, it is a sign of mortal works and of death itself; […]

Now the whole prophecy of this chapter is against Mount Seir — namely of the sons of Esau and Edom, who in Greek and in our language are called Idumaeans [Edomites], because, in the time of need and distress, when Judah was being captured by the Babylonians, they insulted them, and, the people of the Jews having been cast out, they thought the land had been handed over to them to possess, and not only did they not take in his own sons, namely those of Jacob his brother, but they persecuted them and shut them up into the hands of the sword; whence Symmachus translated it more plainly: You have hated your blood, and blood pursues you —. It is prophesied, moreover, that he too is to be captured and reduced to everlasting wastes, and is to learn by the outcome of events that God is judge, because he said: Two nations and two regions are mine — either of the Edomites and the Jews, or surely of Judah and Israel, that is, of the two and the ten tribes —. […]

35:3.t: Let us see, then, what God commands to be said to the mountain, or against Mount Seir: 'Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir: I will not send angels, nor will I use other ministers, but I myself will come to you; and I will stretch out my hand over you, so as to take on the bearing of one who strikes, and I will make you desolate and deserted, so that you, who were wickedly inhabited and had very many companions in your impiety, to such a degree that you even built cities and claimed for yourself a dominion of your own, now, made desolate with your cities — which Jeremiah too is commanded to destroy and to dig up, so that he may build good cities in their place —, may profit in this, that you may know that I am the Lord, whom before you were laid waste you could not know'.

35:5.t: Now the whole cause of the sin is this: that he was a perpetual enemy; hence the psalm also says: Be angry and do not sin, so that we may quickly be reconciled with our enemies and exchange hatreds for love; but Mount Seir is not such, which, on top of its perpetual enmities, shut up, or besieged, the sons of Israel by guile in the hand of the sword; from which we understand that whoever has seized the sword against the sons of God and has done anything deceitfully and has besieged them has Mount Seir in the hand of the sword in the time of the final iniquity: when the days are most evil, and: The world is set in the evil one, and: Because iniquity is multiplied, the love of many grows cold.

35:6.t: There is, moreover, another sin of Mount Seir, so that, since it hated the blood of the righteous, which it longed to see poured out one by one in persecution after persecution, it suffers persecution from that very blood — whence also under the altar the souls of the saints keep crying out and beg the Lord for vengeance for their blood —.

35:7.t: And those who go and those who return are taken away from Mount Seir, that is, every inhabitant, or the men and beasts that are saved in the Church — of whom it is written: Men and beasts you will save, O Lord —; both of which are destroyed in Mount Seir, so that both those who seem to have some reason and those who are content with simple faith perish at God's command.

35:8.t: And its mountains are filled with the wounded and the slain; and not only the mountains, which have reached the summit of impiety, but the hills too, that is, the lesser disciples of Mount Seir, and the valleys, which are sunk into the depths, or the torrents, which have muddy waters, gathered from here and there and coming from pride, or, according to the Seventy, the plains, which lie midway between hills and valleys: all these, slain, shall fall by the sword of the Lord and of his outstretched and striking hand, so that they may be reduced to everlasting wastes; and if there were any cities, that is, gatherings of an evil habitation, they too are to perish and cease to hold agreement in the bad sense, and their tongues are to be divided, so that they cannot build a tower of blasphemy against God; and, reduced to a waste and a desert, let them know that he is the Lord.

35:10.t: Nor was it enough for Mount Seir to have said so much and done so much, as the preceding discourse has related, but this too it spoke in its pride: 'Two nations and two lands (or regions) are mine: namely, both Edom and Judea, both heretics and churchmen, I shall possess alike'. 'And this', he says, 'you said while the Lord was there, who presided over his people'.

35:11.t: Therefore the Lord swears and says: 'As I live, says the Lord God, according to your anger with which you raged against the people of God, and your zeal with which you persecuted the household of Christ, holding in hatred those whom you longed to possess, when I have struck you and judged you, then I will be made known to you. And you shall know that I learned of your reproaches and blasphemies not through another's report, but that I myself heard what you spoke against the mountains of Israel, saying: Deserted, they have been given to us to devour, the mountains of Israel' — we ought to understand Moses, the prophets, the apostles, whom the heretics and the prince of heretics, the devil, think have been handed over to them to devour, when either rarely anyone or no one is found in the Church who can fight for the mountains of the Lord and ward off their mangling with his voice —.

35:13.t: 'And you rose up', he says, 'against me with your mouth, or you spoke boastfully, not, as you think, against the mountains, but through them against me; and you prayed, or cried out, against me; for all your prayers, O Mount Seir and companions of Mount Seir — of whom it was said above: I will fill its mountains and hills and valleys and plains (or torrents) —, were against me: not at all prayers and petitions, as you think, to God, but a clamor of shouting and blasphemy'.

35:14.t: Hence the Lord also threatens and says: 'As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel when by your persecutions it was laid waste and torn and scattered through the whole world, so will I do to you: for while the whole land of the living and the land of the saints rejoices, and all are turned to the service of God, you shall be laid waste, shaggy mountain, hairy mountain, and all Edom — namely, earthly works given over to gore and blood —, so that then you may know that I am the Lord, who have said elsewhere: I am the Lord your God'.

36:1.t: We, therefore, say that the mountains of Israel are the prophets and apostles, who hear the word of God and whom the devil, the enemy, insulted, saying: 'Aha, the mountains once lofty — of which it is written: Mountains are round about it, and the Lord is round about his people — have been given to me as a possession, when through the straits of persecution they were made desolate and trampled down round about, and made an inheritance for the rest of the nations, and blasphemed by all'.

But you, son of man, prophesy over the mountains of Israel, and you shall say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Because the enemy has said of you: Aha, the everlasting heights (or solitudes) have been given to us as a possession; therefore prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God: Because you have been made desolate and trampled down round about (or Because you have been scattered by those who are round about you), and made an inheritance (or a possession) for the rest of the nations, and you have come up upon the lip of the tongue and become a reproach to the peoples (or nations); therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God: Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and the hills, to the torrents and the valleys and the deserts, to the ruined walls (or the things scattered) and the forsaken cities, which have been depopulated and derided (or trampled down) by the rest of the nations round about. […]

These things we have said παραφραστικῶς [by way of paraphrase], in the Jewish manner: things which they expect in the reign of a thousand years, when they assert that the city of Jerusalem is to be built, and the temple which is described at the end of this volume, and the happiness of all things; and some of them think that these things were fulfilled under Zerubbabel — but how can what is said stand: And I will make you to be inhabited as from the beginning, and I will endow you with greater goods than you had from the beginning? For under Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah few of the people were brought back, and they themselves, obeying the Medes and Persians and thereafter the Macedonians and Egyptians and Romans, served the kings of various nations up to Titus and Vespasian, and serve them to this day, so that what is said at the end of the prophecy cannot stand at all: And the reproach of the peoples thou shalt by no means bear, and thou shalt no more lose thy nation —; […]

36:4.t: Therefore the Lord speaks to the mountains trampled down and made desolate, and not only to the mountains but also to those lower down, set at their several degrees in the land of Judea, that is, on the mountain of the Church — of which it is written: A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden —, and to the hills and torrents, whose faith is increased by the winter of persecutions and the storm of affliction, to the valleys also, those who have been brought low in humility, and to the deserted churches, and to the ruined walls, and to the meeting places of the churches forsaken throughout the whole world — such was the persecution throughout the whole world under Diocletian and Maximian, through which the churches were proscribed and laid waste, when all the nations of the Gentiles and of the heretics round about derided the Church —: that he has spoken in the fire of the zeal of his fury; […]

36:5.t: For hence it is that under the figure of the Idumaeans, who allowed themselves to be vanquished by their own prosperity, those who rejoice in the successes of this world are rebuked, when it is said, "They have given my land to themselves for an inheritance with joy, and with their whole heart and mind." In which words it is to be observed, that they are smitten with severe rebuke, not merely because they rejoice, but because they rejoice with their whole heart and mind.

36:6.t: Therefore speak,' he says, 'O prophet, over the land of Israel, and you shall say to the mountains and hills and ridges — for which the Seventy translated νάπας [glens], which we understand as 'places' that are 'wooded' —, and to the valleys: Thus says the Lord God: In my zeal and in my fury I will stand forth as the avenger of your reproach; and I will lift up my hand, so that the nations which are round about you may bear their ignominy and confusion; but you, O mountains of Israel, shall sprout according to your former state, and put forth shoots and branches — or, according to the Seventy, bear grapes —, with which my people Israel may be filled; and do not think that this will come after a long time: it is near, the time is at hand and will come.

But what did it profit the nations, what did it help the nations of heretics to have insulted the land of the Lord, when the Lord speaks to it, and has spoken in his zeal and in his fury to its mountains and hills and ridges, or wooded places, which were green with the loveliness of paradise, and to the hills, of which we spoke above, and lifts up his hand, on account of the reproach of the nations, against the adversaries who persecuted the Church, so that they bear their confusion and ignominy?: then, when the persecutors have been slain and peace has been restored to the Church, the mountains of Israel, namely the apostles and apostolic men, will make their trees sprout and stretch out their branches, and will bring grapes to be trodden in the winepress of the Lord, from which the new wine flows that inebriates the peoples of believers, and the wine is pressed out that gladdens the heart of man, so that all the fruit of the mountains, from which is made the bread descending from heaven, may be eaten by the people […]

36:8.t: And lest perhaps we despair in persecutions, it is added: It is near — the time — that it should come — for coming indeed he will come and will not delay —; hence he promises his coming to the mountains and to those who have endured in tribulations, and promises that, after the heat of persecution, the land formerly stripped may be worked by the plowshare of Christ, and receive every seed of the virtues, from which men may be born and multiplied, and the whole house of Israel.

36:9.t: And lest this seem difficult to you, I myself will come to you, and I who had withdrawn from you will turn to you, so that you may recover your former cultivation and all things may be filled with seed, so that there may be many men in you, and the cities which had formerly been destroyed may be inhabited. And not only will I multiply men, but the beasts too shall likewise be multiplied and shall increase; and I will make you to be inhabited as from the beginning, when, under the leadership of Moses, two and a half tribes received their possession beyond the Jordan, and, under Joshua the son of Nun, the other nine and a half tribes possessed the land of Judea; and I will endow you with goods much greater than you were from the beginning, before you experienced the various captivities; and when I have done this for you, then you will know that I am the Lord.

36:10.t: And when the cities, that is, the churches of believers, have been inhabited by the returning crowds, then not only the men who will be strong in the knowledge of the Scriptures, but also the beasts, all the simple among the believers, will be multiplied and grow up; and the churches will be inhabited as from the beginning, that is, before there was persecution, and will flourish with greater goods than they had from the beginning, crowned with the victories of the martyrs. And then they will know that he is the Lord who restores his people to its former state, so that it may possess the churches and itself be the inheritance of the churches, and no longer be without the children whom it had lost in persecution.

36:12.t: Since then God blesses this people, and calls them Israel, and declares them to be His inheritance, how is it that you repent not of the deception you practise on yourselves, as if you alone were the Israel, and of execrating the people whom God has blessed? For when He speaks to Jerusalem and its environs, He thus added: 'And I will beget men upon you, even my people Israel; and they shall inherit you, and you shall be a possession for them; and you shall be no longer bereaved of them.'
And you shall be filled,' he says, 'O land of Israel, with my people, who will hold you as an inheritance, and you shall be a possession for them, and you shall not add any more to be without sons.

36:13.t: But when your inhabitant has been multiplied, O mountains of Israel, then your enemies will by no means say against you that you devour men and that your possession is without children; but on the contrary you will multiply men, and your posterity will bring forth a most abundant offspring. Nor will you hear,' he says, 'any more, nor will you bear, the confusion of the nations; nor yet will you lose your nation so as ever to undergo captivity, since the Lord has spoken'.

Hence the prophet is commanded to speak to the land of the meek and the land of the living, or to the mountains of Israel, and to say: 'You shall no longer suffer the reproach of the persecutors, nor will they insult your slaughtered people as sheep for the slaughter; for when peace has been restored, all reproaches will cease, nor will you bear confusion and ignominy among the various nations round about, but you will have your nation and your people, because the truth of the promise has been confirmed, since the Lord has spoken'.

36:16.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, the house of Israel have dwelt (or has dwelt) in their land, and they defiled it in their ways and in their pursuits (or idols); like the uncleanness of a menstruous woman their way has become before me. And I poured out my indignation (or my fury) upon them, for the blood which they shed upon the land; with their idols they defiled it. And I scattered them among the nations, and they were winnowed (or I winnowed them) into the lands (or into the regions); according to their ways and their devices (or sins) I judged them. And they went in to the nations to which they entered, and they defiled my holy name, when it was said of them: This is the people of the Lord, and they have gone out of his land. And I spared my holy name (or I spared them for the sake of my holy name), which the house of Israel had defiled among the nations to which they went in. […]

36:17.t: The house of Israel, that is, the people of the Jews, once dwelt in its own land, that is, in the land of Judea, when it was led out of Egypt; but they defiled it in their ways and in their pursuits, or idols; and they became so polluted that they were compared to the uncleanness of a menstruous woman.

Whoever is of the house of Israel and sees the peace of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, dwells in his own land, the Church, or in the lodging of the flesh which has been handed over to him by God; but if he defiles either land in his most evil ways and is compared to the uncleanness of a menstruous woman, God pours out his indignation upon him, for the blood, whether his own or that of those whom he has scandalized and has shed upon the land, and for the perverse thoughts with which he defiled it.

36:18.t: On which account God pours out his indignation upon them for the blood of the prophets and the righteous which they shed upon the land — as the Savior says in the Gospel: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who have been sent to you, and again: Amen, amen I say to you: the blood which has been shed shall be required of this generation, from the blood of Abel the righteous up to the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah, which they shed between the altar and the temple —; and not only did they shed blood, but they also defiled the land with their crimes; for which reason he scattered them, whether under the Babylonian captivity or under the Roman, when they truly shed the blood of Christ; […]

36:19.t: Then he will be scattered among the nations so as to be made equal to the unbelieving nations, and he will be winnowed on the earth like chaff so as to be separated from the grain of the Church, and he will be judged according to his ways; and if not even so does he perceive his sin, but defiles his holy name, all among whom he dwells will say: 'Behold the people of God, behold one who went out of his land, or rather was cast out'.

36:21.t: 'When I had seen this,' he says, 'not for their sake but for the sake of my holy name — for I am the Creator of all — I spared them; and I sanctified them and restored them to their former glory, so that upon those who believed and were converted from error I poured out the clean water of saving baptism, and cleansed them from their abominations and from all the errors with which they had been taken up; and I gave them a new heart, that they might believe in the Son of God, and a new spirit' — of which David speaks: Create a clean heart in me, O God, and renew a right spirit in my inward parts —.

36:22.t: Nay, He is doing and contriving all things, so that even for little He may crown thee; and He goes about seeking excuses, whereby thou mayest be delivered from hell. For this cause, though thou shouldest work but the eleventh hour of the day, He gives thy wages entire; and though thou afford no ground of salvation, He saith, "I do it for mine own sake, that my name be not profaned:" though thou shouldest sigh only, though thou shouldest only weep, all these things He quickly catches hold of, for an occasion of saving thee. Let us not therefore lift up ourselves, but let us declare ourselves unprofitable, that we may become profitable.
36:22.s: Homily on the Gospel of Matthew 3

36:22.t: In another passage, also, by the same prophet, God, in the clearest language, shows us that it is not owing to any good merits on the part of men, but for His own name's sake, that He does these things. This is His language: "This I do, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went. And I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the heathen, which ye have profaned in the midst of them; and the heathen shall know that I am the Lord, saith the Lord God, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes. For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land. Then will I sprinkle you with clean water, and ye shall be clean: from all your own filthiness, and from all your idols will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you; and the stony heart shall be taken away out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. […]
36:22.s: On Grace and Free Will, Chapter 30

36:23.t: 'But if they repent and I am sanctified in their midst, then the whole crowd of the nations will know that I will take them from the lands into which they had been scattered, and lead them back into the land of the Church; and I will pour out upon them not the waters of saving baptism but the waters of the teaching and the word of God, and I will cleanse them from all their defilements and from all the idols and errors which they have feigned in their heart.

36:25.t: The water ought to be first cleansed and sanctified by the bishop that it may be able to wash away in its baptism the sins of the one who is baptized.

And it must be considered that the new heart and the new spirit are given after the pouring out and sprinkling of the water; and when the new heart and the new spirit have been given, then all the hardness which is compared to stone will be taken away from the Jewish heart, and in place of the heart of stone there comes to be a heart of flesh, soft and tender, which can receive the spirit of God into itself and be inscribed with saving letters; then they will walk in the precepts of the Lord and keep his judgments.

36:26.t: And I will give them,' he says, 'a new heart, which they had lost through sin, and I will renew a right spirit in their hearts, and I will take away the heart of stone, namely the unbelieving heart, and give a heart of flesh, soft and tender, which may receive the precepts of God, so that they walk in my precepts and do the judgments which they had formerly neglected.

Lest, however, it should be thought that men themselves in this matter do nothing by free will, it is said in the Psalm, "Harden not your hearts;" and in Ezekiel himself, "Cast away from you all your transgressions, which ye have impiously committed against me; and make you a new heart and a new spirit; and keep all my commandments. For why will ye die, O house of Israel, saith the Lord? for I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord God: and turn ye, and live." We should remember that it is He who says, "Turn ye and live," to whom it is said in prayer, "Turn us again, O God." We should remember that He says, "Cast away from you all your transgressions," when it is even He who justifies the ungodly. We should remember that He says, "Make you a new heart and a new spirit," who also promises, "I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit will I put within you." How is it, then, that He who says, "Make you," also says, "I will give you"? Why does He command, if He is to give? […]
36:26.s: On Grace and Free Will, Chapter 31

36:26.t: It is certain that it is we that act when we act; but it is He who makes us act, by applying efficacious powers to our will, who has said, "I will make you to walk in my statutes, and to observe my judgments, and to do them." When he says, "I will make you . . . to do them," what else does He say in fact than, "I will take away from you your heart of stone," from which used to arise your inability to act, "and I will give you a heart of flesh," in order that you may act? And what does this promise amount to but this: I will remove your hard heart, out of which you did not act, and I will give you an obedient heart, out of which you shall act?
36:26.s: On Grace and Free Will, Chapter 32

36:28.t: And they will dwell in the land of confession, which he had given to their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and to all the saints and prophets, and they will be for a people of God and the Lord will be to them for a God, which is borne out at the present time.

And let them dwell in the land which I had given to their fathers, namely the masters and teachers, and let them again be the people of God, and let the Lord, whom they had formerly offended, become God to them.

36:29.t: And when they have been saved, the Lord will call the grain and multiply it — for unless indeed a grain of wheat falling into the earth has died, it remains alone —, and they will by no means suffer famine — not a famine of bread and a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of God — the famine which he suffered who, setting out from his father, squandered all the substance he had received, when, compelled by the necessity of hunger, he fed on the pods of the swine.
Then they will be saved from all their defilements, and the grain from which the heavenly bread is made will be multiplied for them, and they will no longer suffer the famine of the word of God.

36:30.t: Then the fruit of the tree will be multiplied — that is, of wisdom, of which it is written: She is a tree of life to all who seek her — and the produce of the field — in the likeness of Jacob, whose smell was: Like the smell of a full field which the Lord has blessed —, and they will no longer bear the reproach of famine among the nations, which the unbelief of the Jews suffers even today; but, after they have attained blessedness, they will imitate the Apostle, who says: I am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God.
And the tree of wisdom will be multiplied in them, and the produce will be brought to fullness in their breast, nor will they any longer be a reproach among the nations.

36:31.t: That penitents may have their due it is enough for them to feel shame instead of all other punishment.

And they will remember their most evil ways and their pursuits that were not good, by which they had offended God, and their iniquities and their crimes, by which they had formerly gone astray, will displease them.

But, after God has had mercy on them, they will remember their most evil ways, and they will know where they have been, and they will be displeasing to themselves in their iniquities'; which the Lord says he does, not for their sake, but for the sake of his own clemency.

36:32.t: Now the Lord will bestow all these things, not for the sake of those who perished by their own error, but for the sake of his holy name; hence he challenges the house of Israel to be confounded and to blush for its former vices, and to understand its Creator.

Hence he also exhorts those who stray to be confounded and to blush for their ways, and to be restored to the cities of the Church, so that these may again be inhabited by them, and everything that had collapsed in them may be built up, and they may return to their former ceremonies, and the land once deserted, which had seemed desolate to the neighbors and strangers and to those passing through the conduct of this world, may return to its former state, and all may marvel and say: 'That untilled land, that deserted land in which all the virtues once perished, has now become like a garden of pleasure and the paradise of God'; and the cities once deserted, which did not have God as their guest and were forsaken by the Holy Spirit and undermined by unbelief, will be fortified by the faith of Christ, so that all round about may know that the Lord has built up the scattered souls, and planted in them and sown together the trees of all the virtues, and that he who promised by word has himself made it good in deed.

36:33.t: But after he has cleansed the people of believers from among the Jews from their iniquities, and caused the cities of the Church to be inhabited, and restored the ruined places which had fallen in the synagogues, and the land of confession has been tilled with the ceremonies of God, which once seemed desolate to all the saints who pass by the works of earthly conduct, then all will say: 'How is it that the land of Judea, which had once been untilled, now has the likeness of the paradise of God, and the cities of Judea, which had been deserted and forsaken and undermined by their own unbelief, are now raised up and fortified in the confession and the name of the Lord Savior?'; so that every creature, and the multitudes of angels that encircle the land of Israel, may know that the Lord has built the scattered cities and planted the untilled regions, and has fulfilled in deed what he promised through the prophets.

36:37.t: Nor will he be content with this gift of his liberality toward the people he has saved, but he will bestow far greater things: for he will be found by the house of Israel, he who had been sought for a long time and not found; and, after it has found him, he will multiply them like sheep, not sheep of brute animals but sheep of men — who are full of reason and confession —, like holy sheep and the flock of Jerusalem — in which properly is the worship of God and the vision of peace —, in her solemn feasts — when we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, and feed on the flesh of the Lamb and are given his blood to drink, and in the seven weeks and in the tabernacles of this age, of the Lord, of the Lord, celebrate the feasts —, so that the cities, once deserted, may become full of flocks of men, and by this means they may know that he is the Lord who has bestowed all things. […]

And again the prophetic word exhorts the penitent that, even when they have returned into the churches, they should always seek the Lord and find him, so that the flocks of the Lord may be multiplied by the crowds of those returning, not flocks of beasts and brute animals, but flocks of men who are full of faith and reason, holy flocks, flocks of the city of Jerusalem, in all the solemn feasts which they have received by the clemency of God, so that, after a multitude of such flocks has filled the cities of the Lord, then all may know that he is the Lord.

37:1.t: For even if there is some surpassing glory of the eye, it is chiefly in this, that either it itself be the guide of the body, or it not be forsaken by the offices of the other members. And this too I think we are taught through that vision of the prophet Ezekiel, when he says that "bone must be gathered to bone, and joint to joint and sinews and veins and skin", and each thing be restored to its own place. In short, see what the prophet adds: "these bones", he says (he did not say: they are all men, but he said: "these bones") "are the house of Israel". You will have gladness, then, on departing from this life, if you have been holy. But then there will be full gladness, when no member of the body is lacking to you.… Of these bones, while they were still scattered, before he came who was to "collect and gather them into one", that prophetic word too was spoken: "our bones are scattered beside hell". […]

And also through the Prophet Ezekiel, the Resurrection of the dead was manifestly shown, when God brought him forth to the valley and showed him many bones, and made him pass by them round about them, and said to him:—Son of Man, will these bones live? And Ezekiel said to Him:—Thou knowest, O Lord of lords. And the Lord said to him:—Prophesy, O Son Man, over these bones; prophesy and say to the dry bones, Hear the word of the Lord of lords. And when he had caused them to hear those words, there was a shaking and a noise, and the bones were gathered together, even those that were crushed into pieces and broken. And when the Prophet saw them, he was astonished, for they came together from all sides, and each bone received its fellow, and each joint approached its fellow-joint, and they ordered themselves, one on another. And their dryness was made moist, and the joints were united by the ligatures, and the blood grew warm in the arteries, and skin was stretched over the flesh, and hair grew up according to its nature. […]
37:1.s: Demonstration 8 (Of the Resurrection of the Dead), Sections 12-13

37:1.t: The hope of resurrection is the root of every kind of good work, for the expectation of reward braces the soul to productive toil. And whereas every worker is ready to sustain his toil if he can look forward to being repaid for his labors, where toil has no recompense the soul is soon discouraged and the body flags with it. A soldier who expects his share of the spoils is ready for war. But no one is prepared to die serving a king so undiscerning that he does not provide rewards for labors. In the same way, any soul that believes in resurrection takes care for itself, as is right, but any soul that disbelieves the resurrection abandons itself to destruction. A person who believes that the body survives to rise again is careful of this garment and does not soil it by fornicating. But a person who does not believe in the resurrection gives himself up to fornication, abusing his own body as if it were nothing to him. A mighty message and teaching of the holy Catholic church is belief about the resurrection of the dead; […]

For instance, Ezekiel leaps in the spirit of prophecy over all the intervening time, with its vast duration; he stands, by his powers of foresight, in the actual moment of the Resurrection, and, as if he had really gazed on what is still to come, brings it in his description before our eyes. He saw a mighty plain, unfolded to an endless distance before him, and vast heaps of bones upon it flung at random, some this way, some that; and then under an impulse from God these bones began to move and group themselves with their fellows that they once owned, and adhere to the familiar sockets, and then clothe themselves with muscle, flesh, and skin (which was the process called "decorating" in the poetry of the Psalms); a Spirit in fact was giving life and movement to everything that lay there.
37:1.s: ON THE SOUL AND THE RESURRECTION

37:1.t: The hand of the Lord came upon me, and he led me out in the spirit of the Lord, and set me down in the midst of a plain which was full of bones; and he led me around through them in a circle: and they were very many upon the face of the plain, and exceedingly dry. And he said to me: Son of man, do you think these bones will live? And I said: Lord God, you know. And he said to me: Prophesy concerning these bones, and you shall say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord; thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will send spirit into you and you shall live, and I will put sinews upon you and make flesh grow up upon you, and I will stretch skin over you, and I will give you spirit, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I prophesied as he had commanded me. And there was a sound, as I prophesied, and behold, a commotion; and the bones drew near, bones to bones, each one to its joint. […]

But those who interpret otherwise will put forward the following: it ought not to bring odium upon us that, by expounding this passage otherwise, we seem to deny the resurrection: for we know that we find in the holy Scriptures much stronger testimonies, and ones in which there is no doubt — such as that of Job: You will raise up my skin, which endures these things, and in Daniel: Many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall rise again, these to life eternal, and these to reproach and to eternal confusion, and in the Gospel: Do not fear those who kill the body and cannot kill the soul; but rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in gehenna, and in the apostle Paul: Who will give life to your mortal bodies because of his spirit dwelling in you, and many others —; […]

37:3.t: And when the divine word had asked him whether he thought these bones could live, he replied: 'Lord God, you know, you who have full knowledge of things to come'.

37:4.t: In minute detail the holy prophet Ezekiel teaches and describes how strength will be restored to our dry bones, feeling return and motion added; how, with the return of sinews, the whole structure of the human body will grow strong, and how the driest bones will be clothed with restored flesh and the openings of the veins and the streams of the blood will be concealed by a veil of skin drawn tautly over them. At the very words of the prophet, as we read, the crop of human bodies seems to rise up again to life, and one may see the wide expanses of the fields sprouting with a novel kind of growth.

Note how the prophet shows that there was hearing and movement in the bones before the Spirit of life was poured on them. For, above, both the dry bones are bidden to hear, as if they had the sense of hearing, and that on this each of them came to its own joint is pointed out by the words of the prophet.…Great is the lovingkindness of the Lord, that the prophet is taken as a witness of the future resurrection, that we, too, might see it with his eyes. For all could not be taken as witnesses, but in that one all we are witnesses, for neither does lying come on a holy person or error on so great a prophet.

And the Lord said to him: Prophesy concerning the bones (or over these bones), and you shall say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. In this it is to be wondered at how he spoke to dry bones, which, before the sinews, flesh and skin and the life-giving spirit, could hear the word of God; and first bones are bound to other bones by the bonds of sinews, then they are filled with flesh, and over them, for beauty, skin is stretched to cover the unsightliness of the bare flesh, and then they receive the spirit which makes them live, so that, after they have lived, they may then know that he is the Lord.

37:7.t: For the prophets have proclaimed two advents of His: the one, that which is already past, when He came as a dishonoured and suffering Man; but the second, when, according to prophecy, He shall come from heaven with glory, accompanied by His angelic host, when also He shall raise the bodies of all men who have lived, and shall clothe those of the worthy with immortality, and shall send those of the wicked, endued with eternal sensibility, into everlasting fire with the wicked devils. And that these things also have been foretold as yet to be, we will prove. By Ezekiel the prophet it was said: "Joint shall be joined to joint, and bone to bone, and flesh shall grow again; and every knee shall bow to the Lord, and every tongue shall confess Him." And in what kind of sensation and punishment the wicked are to be, hear from what was said in like manner with reference to this; it is as follows: "Their worm shall not rest, and their fire shall not be quenched;" and then shall they repent, when it profits them not.

After this was seen the sight which had been desired and prayed for by us all; feasts of dedication in the cities and consecrations of the newly built houses of prayer took place, bishops assembled, foreigners came together from abroad, mutual love was exhibited between people and people, the members of Christ's body were united in complete harmony.

Then was fulfilled the prophetic utterance which mystically foretold what was to take place: "Bone to bone and joint to joint," and whatever was truly announced in enigmatic expressions in the inspired passage.

And there was one energy of the Divine Spirit pervading all the members, and one soul in all, and the same eagerness of faith, and one hymn from all in praise of the Deity.

So when the prophet spoke what he had been commanded, at once a commotion arose; and the bones were fitted into their framework, bound with sinews, full of flesh, covered with hide; and there lay human bodies that did not have spirit.

And again, the blessed Ezekiel says: And it was as I prophesied, and behold a shaking and the bones came together, bone to his bone, each to its own joint: and when I beheld, lo, the sinews came up upon them and the flesh grew and rose up on them and the skin covered them above. And later he teaches how the spirits came back when they were bidden.
37:7.s: An Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith, Book 4, Chapter 27

37:9.t: Therefore the prophet prophesies to the spirit, and says: Thus says the Lord God: Come from the four winds, O spirit — namely from the four quarters of the world, so that, just as in the first creation of man: God breathed into his face and he was made into a living soul, so also the second creation, that is, the resurrection of the dead, may be given life by the breathing of the spirit —, and the spirit entered the human bodies, and at once they lived and stood upon their feet — whence also the resurrection of the dead is called a 'congregation', or church, 'large' and, as it is in the Hebrew, 'a great army'; and at that time is fulfilled: Send forth your spirit and they shall be created, and you shall renew the face of the earth —.

37:11.t: But what follows: And he said to me: Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel, seems to raise a question, in that it is said not of the general resurrection but properly of the resurrection of the house of Israel, which says: 'Our bones have dried up and our hope has perished, and we are cut off from our land' or 'we have utterly despaired'; and as they say these things, Ezekiel is compelled to prophesy a third time and to say to the dry bones: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will open your tombs, and here it is asked, if he opens tombs, how he said above: And they were very many upon the face of the plain, and exceedingly dry. And I will lead, he says, you out of your graves, my people — according to what is written in the Gospel: The hour comes when those who are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and those who have done good shall come forth to the resurrection of life, and again: Those who hear shall live —. […]

37:14.t: It is a prerogative of God to raise the dead.

We notice here how the operations of the Spirit of life are again resumed; we know in what way the dead are raised from the opening tombs. And is it in truth a matter of wonder that the sepulchers of the dead are opened at the bidding of the Lord, when the whole earth from its utmost limits is shaken by one thunderclap, the sea overflows its bounds and again checks the course of its waves?

37:15.t: But if the Jews and judaizing Christians wish to refer these things to the reign of a thousand years, they will be compelled by necessity to accept that all who have been saved will dwell in the land of Israel, that Jerusalem is to be built, the temple to be erected, all the ceremonies of the law to be practiced, the sabbath to be observed, the injury of circumcision to be received, that there is to be eating and drinking, and that an abundance of riches is to be esteemed as the highest blessedness and all wealth, when the Apostle says: Food for the belly and the belly for foods: but God will destroy both it and them; […]

37:16.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, take for yourself one stick and write upon it: Of Judah and of the sons of Israel his companions. And take another stick and write upon it: Of Joseph — the stick of Ephraim — and of the house of Israel and of his companions. And join them one to the other for yourself into one stick; and they shall be in union in your hand. And when the sons of your people say to you, speaking: Will you not show us what you mean by these things? you shall speak to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph — which is in the hand of Ephraim — and the tribes of Israel which are joined to him, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah and make them one stick, and they shall be one in his hand. […]

But if we wish, following the prophecy of Hosea, which is almost wholly directed to the ten tribes, that is, to Joseph and Ephraim and Samaria and Israel, to understand the knowledge falsely so called and the various crowds of heretics, we shall say this: that in the last time, when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in and all Israel has been saved, then the hostile peoples also, who fought against the house of Judah and the confession of the Church, will give themselves up to the faith of the Church, and, having abandoned all their errors and the princes of this world who are being destroyed and their own patriarchs who led them down into the abyss of blasphemies, they will rise up, and leave their idols and their abominations which they had fashioned out of their own heart, and from all their dwelling places in which they sinned will pass over to the faith of the Church, and be cleansed, and be the people of Christ, and he will be their God; which I know I have dictated more fully on the prophet Hosea.

And that the Lord rejected the tribe of Ephraim and chose the tribe of Judah, we read also in the Psalms, where it is written: And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph, and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim; but he chose the tribe of Judah, of which it is written: A prince shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes for whom it is laid up; and he shall be the expectation of the nations: for truly at the coming of the Lord Savior the 'two rods' and, as it is set down in the Hebrew, the 'two sticks', were joined into one scepter, and in the baptism of Christ those long separated are united, so that they become one new man and one nation, and are no longer defiled with idols and abominations but, made clean by the washing, are the people of God, and Christ rules over them, and they dwell upon the land of the meek and the land of the living which he had given to his servant Jacob, who supplanted the people of Israel in his mother's womb.

37:21.t: For he says that he takes the sons of Israel from the midst of the nations to which they were led captive, and will lead them back into the land and into the mountains of Israel — of which we read above —, and that they are to be called one nation and ruled by the authority of one king, so that they are no longer defiled with their idols and abominations; but that, when they have been freed from the dwelling places of captivity in which they had sinned, they are to be cleansed of all vices and will be the people of God, so that the Lord is their God.

37:24.t: And my servant, he says, David shall be king over them — of whom the angel also speaks in the Gospel, saying that he will reign over the house of Jacob and of his kingdom there will be no end —; and he will be of such clemency that he is called not only king but also shepherd, so that the name of shepherd may soften the proud name of power; and they, after they have become one nation and have dwelt in the land and on the mountains of Israel, will walk in all the judgments of the Lord and keep his precepts; and they will dwell not in another land but in that which he gave to his servant Jacob, in which their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and the other saints dwelt; and not only will they themselves dwell there, but also their sons and grandsons — according to that line of Vergil: And the sons of sons and those who will be born of them —; and they will dwell there not for a short time, but for ever.

'But do you wish' he says 'to know who this king and shepherd is? He is the one of whom I spoke above: My servant David: Who, though he was in the form of God, did not think it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, and became obedient to the Father unto death, even the death of the cross. And when they are under such a king, I will strike with them a covenant of peace': not, as in the old testament, a covenant of contests and wars, but a pact of peace: Which surpasses all understanding — of which the Savior speaks to the apostles: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you, and the prophet says: His place was made in peace —. And when he has founded and established them in the Church — so that they can say: He set my feet upon a rock —, then they will be multiplied, either in the number of believers or in the multiplication of virtues.

37:26.t: And I will put, he says, my sanctification (or sanctuary) in the midst of them for ever, which the Jews interpret of the temple that was built under Zerubbabel — but how will what is said, 'for ever', be able to stand, when that temple, which was built by Zerubbabel and afterwards restored by many, was burned by Roman fire? —. All these things are to be referred to the Church and to the times of the Savior, when his tabernacle was set in the Church, where he has become our God and we his people. And it is the advancement of all, that they may know that he is the Lord; and that he himself sanctifies Israel, not according to the flesh but according to the spirit, when his sanctification has been set in the midst of believers for ever.

38:1.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face against Gog and the land of Magog, the prince of the head (or Ros) of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy concerning him, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Gog, the prince of the head (or Ros) of Meshech and Tubal, and I will turn you about, and I will put a bridle in your jaws, and I will lead out (or I will gather) both you and all your army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed with breastplates, a great multitude seizing spear and shield and sword (or bucklers and helmets and swords). Persians and Ethiopians and Libyans with them, all with shields and helmets; Gomer and all its troops, the house of Togarmah, the sides of the north (or from the farthest parts of the north) and all its strength, and many peoples (or nations) with you. Prepare and equip yourself and all your multitude that is heaped together to you, and be for them a command (or and you shall be to me for a guard). […]

38:2.t: He it was, then, and none other, Whom the prophecy foretold, in Whose time the kingdom of Gog should be exalted concurrently with the growth of Christ's power. It is said that by this figure the Hebrews disguised the Roman Empire, which grew concurrently with the teaching of Christ. And the Prophet Ezekiel also mentions Gog, naming him Ruler of Ros, Mosoeh, and Thobel, probably disguising the city of Rome under the name of Ros, because empire and power are signified in Hebrew by that word; by Mosoeh, he meant Mysia and the adjacent nations, which are now subject to Rome; and by Thobel Josephus means Iberia, saying that the Thobelian Iberians sprang from Thobel. He says that Gog, the ruler of all of them, will be exalted at the coming of the Christ prophesied, Whom God led out of Egypt, when, as Matthew records, Herod laid a plot against Him when He was a Child, and Joseph informed by God took the young Child and His mother, and afterwards returned into the land of Israel.
38:2.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 3

38:2.t: The eleventh book of the explanations on Ezekiel will contain, in its last part, the prophecy against Gog and Magog, and it will come as far as the beginning of the city set on the mountain, Jerusalem, and of the temple situated in it. If, with the Lord helping and expounding his own mysteries, I am able to bring it all the way to the end, I shall have to hesitate long and much whether I ought to set my hands to the spiritual temple or openly confess my ignorance, especially since, both among the Jews and among us, there is a great silence over its interpretation: some judge that it is to be built in time to come; others, with a good intention indeed but an unskilled one, know that the things said are spiritual, and yet do not know how those spiritual things themselves ought to be expounded. And in the meantime, so that the care of the present work may hold us, know also, O virgin of Christ Eustochium, that you must pray for us. […]

Next it must be observed that the face of the prophet is set, or made firm, against Gog the land, or of the land, of Magog; for there is need of firmness and of much consideration of the countenance, so that we may be able to know the things that are said, according to that apostolic saying: But we all, contemplating the glory of the Lord with unveiled face, are re-formed into the same image, from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord. Accordingly the Jews and our own Judaizers think that Gog is the Scythian nations, savage and innumerable, which stretch beyond the Caucasus mountain and the Maeotic marsh and near the Caspian Sea as far as India — and that these are to be stirred up by the devil after the reign of a thousand years —, and that they are to come into the land of Israel to fight against the saints, with many nations gathered together with them: first Meshech, whom Josephus interprets as the Cappadocians; […]

38:4.t: What, then, is the threat against Gog? 'I will turn you about (or I will convert), and I will put a bridle in your jaws: first I will make you waver from your opinion and be converted, and I will put a bridle in your jaws — of which it is written: With bridle and bit bind fast the jaws of those who do not draw near to you —, so that the untamed horse, wanton and rushing headlong over precipices, may be subjected to the bridle of the Lord' — to whom the prophet says: You will mount upon your horses, and your riding is salvation, and to Job it is said through clouds and whirlwind: Did you surround the horse with strength? Such were the horses and horsemen whose multitude John saw in heaven —. So he says to Gog: I will lead out (or I will gather) you and all the army (or strength) of yours; he who is led out and gathered from dispersion is drawn back to salvation — according to what is promised in the law: If your dispersion be from the height of heaven to its height, from there I will gather you —.

Of his horses too, and horsemen clothed with breastplates — who imitate the armor of the Apostle and boast that they have the breastplates of righteousness — there is an excessive multitude, and all of them seize shield and sword against the Church, and they are most savage nations, hostile to Israel: Persians, Ethiopians and Libyans — whose wars against the people of God are related in the holy Scriptures —; Gomer too and the house of Togarmah, who come from the sides of the 'north' — which is a most cold wind and is called by the name 'dexter' [right-hand] —, and all the strength of Magog and all the peoples that are subject to him, will come with him to battle.

38:7.t: To him it is said by way of εἰρωνείαν [irony]: 'Prepare and equip yourself, and heap together to yourself all your multitude, which obeys your commands; but know that after many days you will be visited' — according to what is written: I will visit their iniquities with the rod and their sins with stripes —.

38:8.t: 'In the last', he says, 'of the years you will come'; whence John too says: My little children, it is the last hour, and the people of the Gentiles is hired at the eleventh hour to work in the vineyard; to whose land — that is, the land of the meek and the land of the saints, which brings forth fruit a hundredfold and sixtyfold and thirtyfold — Gog comes to storm it, the land which has turned back, or turned away, from the sword — for it knows that it is written: Scatter, O Lord, the nations that desire wars —, and abides in peace, and has been gathered from many peoples and nations so that, having despised the error of the nations, it might come to the mountains of Israel, that is, the patriarchs and prophets, who were once continually deserted, without the law and the precepts of God, to which it is afterwards said: More are the children of the deserted one than of her who has a husband; […]

38:9.t: And Gog, going up with all his army, will come like a storm and like a cloud, to cover the land of the believers — for which of the heretics, whose prince is the devil, does not come like a storm against the Church, and hasten to overwhelm and cover with the cloud of his words all the simple among the believers? —; whence it is said to him: 'As far as lies in you, you will cover all things, you and all your troops and many peoples with you'; and fittingly Gog, going up, has no willing rain, no early and late shower to gladden the parched fields, but storm and darkness, so as to confound all things with gloom and error.

38:10.t: Therefore the Lord God speaks these things to him: At that time, that is, in the last days, words will go up upon your heart, and you will think a most wicked thought — as Scripture says: If the spirit of one who has power should wish to go up upon you, do not abandon your place; but on the contrary God goes up into the heart of the holy man, of whom it is written: He has set ascents in his heart —; and Gog says: I will go up to the land without a wall (or cast forth) — that is, the land which is destitute of the help of God and not fortified by the argumentation of the dialecticians, I will come to those who are at rest, dwelling securely (or in peace) — for our king is peaceable, and his place is in peace —; all of them, he says, dwell without a wall, they have no bars and gates.

38:11.t: This the devil, the prince of the heretics, says: that the Church has no fortifications, nor the worldly wisdom which is foolishness with God, so that he may seize the spoils and fall upon the plunder of the Church, and lay his hand upon those who had been deserted when they did not have the knowledge of God and afterwards, restored through Christ, come to the Father — he says in the Gospel: Father, I have revealed your name to men —; and so that we may know that the people which had been deserted and afterwards restored signifies the Christian people, there follows: And upon the people which has been gathered out of the nations, which people has begun to possess the inheritance of Christ and to be the inhabitant of the navel of the earth — of which it is written: He has worked salvation in the midst of the earth. Truth, indeed, has sprung from the earth; which says in the Gospel: I am the way and the truth and the life —.

38:13.t: While he thinks and says these things and hastens to snatch the possession of the Church, the nations which had been converted from their former error to salvation: Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish — of Carthage or of the sea — who amid the waves of this world seek merchandise by good works, and all their villages or lions — or lions' whelps, as is contained in the Hebrew —, will say to him what follows — that the Seventy and Theodotion, however, put 'villages' in place of 'lions' whelps', which in Hebrew are called 'chaphir', is an evident error: for if you write it with the letter 'chi', it is called 'lion's whelp', but if with 'ce', which in Hebrew is called 'coph', it is called 'field' and 'village'; whence Capharnaum too is called 'most beautiful field' —. So Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish will say, and all the saints who are called lions' whelps, or at any rate the villages and dwellings of the believers: 'O Gog, is it for this that you come: to snatch the spoils of the Church? […]

38:14.t: 'Therefore, O prophet Ezekiel, who in the type of Christ are called son of man, speak to Gog and say to him: Thus says the Lord God: When, the error of the whole world having been taken away, my people Israel, which discerns God with the mind, dwells in the Church confidently or in peace, then you will know, or rise up and come from your place' — and what the place of heretical depravity is, the following word shows: From the sides of the north, which tries to chill all the warmth of the believers —.

38:15.t: And many peoples will come with him, all riders of horses — of whom it is written: The horse and the rider he has cast into the sea —, a great company and a mighty army; with whom: 'You will go up', he says, 'against my people Israel like a cloud and darkness, to cover my land — of which it was spoken above —. In the last days you will be, in the time of the preaching of the Gospel, and I will bring you upon my land — For there must also be heresies, so that those who are approved may be made manifest, and by the will of God the devil, the ἀνταγωνιστής [adversary], and all the dogmas of perversity have been left —, so that all the nations may know (and understand) me, when I am sanctified in you before their eyes, O Gog, that is, when through your punishments they have understood me as judge'.

38:17.t: And he makes an apostrophe to Gog himself: 'Are you not he of whom I spoke in ancient days, by the hands of my servants the prophets of Israel?': that is, of Moses — who says in the book of Numbers, at least according to the Seventy: A man shall come forth from his seed and shall rule over very many nations, and Gog his kingdom shall be lifted up, and his kingdom shall increase, but according to the Hebrew I found it written thus: His king shall be taken away because of Agag, and his kingdom shall be removed, because the kingdom of Israel was destroyed in Saul on account of Agag king of Amalek; and in another place: He will cleanse the land of his people —; Joel too describes the peoples to be gathered in the valley of 'Iosaphat', that is, 'of the judgment of God'; and Isaiah, and all the prophets, in whose hands and good works the word of the Lord comes about.

38:18.t: 'When therefore you come upon the land of Israel, my indignation will go up in my fury against you. And in my zeal for my people, in the fire of my wrath I have spoken, which is to consume all the timbers of your vices: At that', he says, 'time there will be a great commotion upon the land of Israel': for at the instigation of the devil frequent persecution will arise against the Church, and when it has been lulled to rest and overcome by the protection of God, then the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field, and every creeping thing that moves upon the earth, and all the men who are upon the face of the earth, will be moved before his face; […]

38:20.t: Then, from the face of the Lord and from the sight of his majesty, the mountains which raised themselves against the knowledge of God will be overturned, and the hedges or valleys will fall, which either have sunk to the depths through lowness of understanding or at any rate promise some fortification so as to imitate the Church of God — of whose hedges it is said: Whoever breaks down a hedge, a serpent will bite him —, and every wall will collapse to the ground: for when the strength of the Church's word appears, all the fortifications of the heretics will collapse.

38:21.t: 'And I will call together against him, that is, against Gog, the prince of the heretics, a sword on all my mountains, so that the princes of his army may be destroyed by the sword for the Lord'; then heresy will fight against heresy, and their fighting among themselves is our victory.

38:22.t: And I will judge, he says, him with death (or pestilence) and blood and violent rain and immense stones (or of hail): and Gog is judged by his own death, and by the blood which he shed, and by violent rain, the words of a learned and perfect man, and by immense stones which overwhelm him with the testimonies of the Scriptures, or of hail, which make his heat grow cold — All, indeed, who commit adultery, their hearts are like an oven —. Fire, he says, and sulphur I will rain upon him, by which the punishment of eternal judgment is shown; and not only upon him who was the author of perversity, but also upon all his army and multitude and upon the many peoples who are with him — for the heretics have many companions, or rather the devil, their prince, is surrounded by an infinite multitude —.

38:23.t: And when all error has been taken away and the princes of the heretics have been punished and destroyed, the Lord is magnified, and sanctified in the believers, and becomes known in the eyes of the many nations which have believed in his faith, and both from their own blessedness and from the punishments of the adversaries they will know and recognize that he himself is the Lord. These things we have interpreted as we were able, obeying that precept: You shall turn aside neither to the right nor to the left, but: You shall walk on the royal road; but if anyone finds fault with what is ours, let him either bring forward better things for us to follow, or, if he wishes to say nothing, let him leave perfect knowledge to God, provided only that he knows that it is by no means our powers, but our intention, that is to be judged.

39:1.t: Gog too has his own trinity, 'Ros' and 'Mosoch' and 'Thubal', that is, 'head' and 'madness' and 'all things', so that there is no vice that does not stand in Gog's possession.

But you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Gog, prince of the head (or Ros) of Meshech and Tubal; and I will turn you about (or gather you) and lead you astray (or lead you down), and make you go up from the sides (or from the uttermost parts) of the north, and bring you upon the mountains of Israel. And I will strike (or destroy) your bow in your left hand (or from your left hand), and your arrows from your right hand, and I will cast you down upon the mountains of Israel. And you will fall, you and all your troops, and the peoples (or nations) that are with you; to the wild beasts, to the birds and to every winged thing and to the beasts of the earth I have given you to be devoured: on the face of the field (or plain) you will fall, for I have spoken, says the Lord God. And I will send fire on Magog, and on those who dwell in the islands confidently (or and the islands will be inhabited in peace), and they will know that I am the Lord. […]

39:2.t: He will be led out, or turned about, and he will be stroked and coaxed so that, hoping for victory, he may be led to battle to be slain; and he will go up from the sides, or from the uttermost parts, of the north, from which evils blaze up over all the earth, and by that very one he will be brought upon the mountains of Israel, which we ought to understand as the apostles and apostolic men and men of the Church, so that, after he has been brought to the mountains of Israel, then the bow that is in his left hand may be struck, and the arrows that are held in the right hand: for he too imitates, in order to kill those whom he has deceived, the having of weapons on the left and on the right, through good report and bad — these are the arrows and these the darts of which the psalmist too speaks: For behold, sinners have bent the bow, they have made ready arrows in the quiver, to shoot in the dark at the upright of heart, which fiery darts of the devil are to be quenched with the shield of faith —.

39:4.t: And Gog, who had gone up upon the mountains of Israel, is cast down, or will fall, on those very mountains with all his army and all his troops; and he will be food for the wild beasts, the birds and every winged thing and the beasts of the earth, namely the adverse powers that ate the seed by the wayside, and the bloodthirsty beasts — for as it is written of the dragon: You gave him as food to the Ethiopian peoples, so all who are deceived by the heretics are the food of demons —: and Gog will fall either in the breadth of the plain or in that of the field which has been tilled by God's husbandmen; for it cannot be that the Lord's words should be void.

39:6.t: Then fire will be sent on Magog, namely on those who received Gog's teaching, and on those who, like islands, are beaten by the waves of the world and think that they ought to be secure — that fire of which the Lord speaks: I came to send fire upon the earth, and how I will that it burn —: 'that all may know and understand that I am the Lord'.

39:7.t: 'And let my holy name be made known in the midst of my people, which was by no means led astray by the authority of Gog, and let my name no longer be polluted among the heretics on the pretext of the knowledge falsely so called, and let the nations that are round about know that I am the Lord'.

39:8.t: But what follows, Behold, it comes, and it has been done, is said of the judgment of Christ, who coming will come and will not delay; and this is the day of punishments and vengeance of which the Lord has spoken through all the prophets.

39:9.t: And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go forth: the peoples of believers; and by the cities of Israel we understand the Church of right faith. And they will kindle and burn the weapons — of which it is written in another place too: He will crush the bow, he will shatter the weapons, and he will burn the shields with fire —, shields and spears, bow and arrows, hand staves — with which they celebrated a perverse Passover —, lances or pikes — with which they inflicted the broad and incurable wounds of their doctrines —, and shields, bows and arrows, of which it was said above. And what follows, And they will kindle them with fire seven years, is to be taken from Exodus and Leviticus, in which it is commanded by the law that in the seventh year, of release, when liberty is restored to Hebrew slaves and all debts are cancelled and the ancient possession returns to its owners, rest too is granted to the land and all the crops are given over to the poor; […]

39:11.t: On that day — in the clear light of preaching — I will give, he says, Gog a renowned place, a sepulcher in Israel, according to the Hebrew: the valley of the travelers east of the sea, which makes those who pass by stand aghast; the sense of this saying is this: The sepulcher of Gog will not be on the mountains but in low valleys and rugged places — which in Hebrew are called 'ge'; and the heretics, though they are situated in the west, pretend that these are places of the east —, in order to deceive the travelers, namely those who pass through this world and are not inhabitants but sojourners — saying that prophetic word: I am a stranger and a sojourner, as all my fathers were —. For which of those passing by — of whom it is written: And those who passed by did not say: The blessing of the Lord be upon you! — does not marvel and stand aghast when he sees the valley of the travelers, which to the travelers seems a valley, to the inhabitants a mountain? This is according to the Hebrew. […]

39:12.t: And as we said above that the weapons of the adversaries are kindled through seven years, so through seven months the land will be cleansed of the filth of the heretics; for from the first month — when we celebrate the Lord's Passover and escape the destroyer of Egypt by the blood of the lamb on our doorposts —, up to the end of the year — that is, up to the seventh month, when we pitch tabernacles and, among the other foliage, are sheltered also by branches of palms, so that a perfect victory over the enemies may be shown —, we fulfil all the festivals among the peoples; and not only the teachers but the whole people too will do this eagerly, to bury Gog, and cover him with earth, and by no means allow him to take in the free air.

39:14.t: After the peace, however, and the slaying, or the burial, of Gog, men of the Church will be chosen who have this as their concern: that nothing of the former filth remain in the land of Israel, nothing of carrion; men to go through the land and search out the dead and bury them, so that, namely, the land of the Church may be cleansed. But if after seven months, when all things ought to have been purged, those who traverse and go round the land see that in anyone a man's bone — that is, the hardness of heretical depravity — or something of the carrion of the former doctrine has remained, they will set up, or build, a marker beside it, so that, after those who are of this kind have been marked, they may then either be corrected or be buried with Gog and thrust away into the throng of his burial.

39:16.t: And the name of the city where the victory of the servants of the Lord is, and where the adversaries lie and the whole multitude of his enemies has been laid low, will be called 'Amona' or Πολυάνδριον, so that the end of all things may be the restoration of purity. Finally there follows: And they will cleanse the land, doubtless those of whom it is written above: They will begin to search, and will go round traversing the land.

39:17.t: But we, following the tropology we have begun, say this: that the Lord calls together all the birds and all the beasts, to hand over to them the princes of the heretics to be devoured as the fattest offerings — and those to whom the adversaries are handed over are called birds and beasts either for their swiftness in running about into all things or for their savagery and cruelty: For the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved, and that they may learn not to blaspheme —; and they will eat a great and very fat victim: not elsewhere, but upon the mountains of Israel, which we ought to understand as the prophets and apostles and holy men — for upon them the teachers of contrary dogmas fall in ruin, and by them they perish wounded —, upon whom the Church is built, and, to speak more truly, upon the mountain of mountains — of which Isaiah speaks, and Micah: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will announce to us his way —. […]

Therefore you, son of man, thus says the Lord God: Say to every bird and to all the fowl and to all the beasts of the field (or plain): Assemble and hasten, run together from every side (or round about) to my victim, which I have sacrificed for you, a great victim upon the mountains of Israel, that you may eat flesh and drink blood. You will eat the flesh of the mighty (or of giants), and you will drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs and of he-goats, and of fatted bulls and of all fat things; and you will eat fat to the full, and drink blood to drunkenness from the victim which I have sacrificed for you. And you will be filled at my table with horse and with mighty horseman (or giant), and with all men of war, says the Lord God. And I will set (or give) my glory among the nations (or among you), and all the nations will see my judgment which I have done, and my hand which I have laid (or brought) upon them; […]

39:18.t: The flesh of the mighty, or of giants, who rebelled against the knowledge of God, and the blood of the princes, not of heaven but of the earth, who savored all earthly things, they will drink: the blood of rams, of lambs and of he-goats, or, according to the Seventy, of rams, of calves and of he-goats, so that it signifies three living creatures that are sacrificed among the victims of God: for the heretics too imitate the gentleness of the Church, but their oblation serves not for the worship of God but for the food of demons, and this is their fattest offering; and they are sated as if with fat, and they drink the blood of the deceived to drunkenness; but God sacrifices this victim through the men of the Church, so that the most wicked guests may be sated with the multitude of the deceived, and drink to vomiting and drunkenness.

39:20.t: When you see holy men, learned in the divine Scriptures, cutting down the horses of the heretics and their riders — of which it is written: The horse and the rider he has cast into the sea —, and hewing down all the rebels and giants with their own blade, and shedding the blood of all the warriors of the knowledge falsely so called, then know that the table of the Lord has been prepared, that he may set his glory among all the nations that believe in his name.

39:21.t: And the churches of the saints will understand his judgment which he has executed upon the adversaries, and the strong hand with which he struck them; and let the house of Israel know and recognize that he is the Lord their God — who said: I am the Lord your God — from the day of the Lord's victory for ever, and let them reflect that the house of Israel was once taken captive by the heretics and scattered through the whole world of perverse dogmas for this reason: that they forsook him who for a little while hid, or turned away, his face from them and delivered them into the hand of the heretics, and they fell, pierced through by their blade, because of their uncleannesses and iniquities; and this was the cause of his hiding and turning away his face from them.

39:25.t: And having set forth the reasons — according to that which is written: There must also be heresies, so that those who are approved may be made manifest — for the captivity of Israel, that is, of the Church, in which those dwell who see God, he now promises that he will bring back into the Church the captivity of Jacob, who had supplanted the Jewish people and afterward was himself supplanted by the frauds of the heretics; and that he will have mercy on the whole house of Israel, not according to the flesh but according to the spirit. And I will take up, he says, my zeal for my holy name, which was blasphemed among the nations because of the heretics, so that, after he has set them free, they may blush and be confounded because, having abandoned the faith of the Church, they transgressed against me. Let them be confounded, then, and blush very swiftly, when they dwell in their own land, the land of the meek and the land of the saints, and dwell confidently, or in peace, by no means fearing the snares of the heretics.

39:27.t: Then they will be brought back from the peoples, and gathered from the lands of their enemies into their own land, and the Lord will be sanctified in them in the sight of very many nations, which themselves too are going to believe in the Lord; and let this be the end of blessedness: to know and recognize that he is the Lord their God, because he appeared to them among the nations, or carried them over from the nations, and gathered them upon their own land, the land of Judea, the land of confession, the land of the meek and the land of the living, and left not even one to heretical depravity.
