And he measured toward the north wind five hundred reeds by the reed of measure all around. And toward the south wind he measured five hundred reeds by the reed of measure round about. And toward the west wind he measured five hundred reeds by the reed of measure. By the four winds he measured its wall on every side round about, the length of five hundred cubits, and the breadth of five hundred cubits, dividing between the sanctuary and the place of the common people. […]

42:16.t: Now the man who had led the prophet out, by no means into the outer court but by the way of the gate which looked toward the eastern way, measured first toward the east wind — that is, toward the eastern quarter — five hundred reeds all around, second toward the north, third toward the south, fourth toward the sea — that is, toward the west —: by the four winds, namely, the wall round about, as much in length as in breadth, that is, in a square: which wall had in all two thousand reeds: but if the reed was of six cubits and one παλαιστῇ [handbreadth] — which παλαιστής is the sixth part of a cubit —, it is clear that the outer wall had round about two thousand reeds: which make twelve thousand three hundred and thirty-three cubits and a third, out of the two thousand — let the prudent and diligent reader read the book of Joshua son of Nun, and he will find how this measure is kept in the suburbs; […]

43:1.t: And he brought me to the gate that looked toward the eastern way, and behold, the glory of the God of Israel was entering by the eastern way, and its voice was like the voice of many waters, and the earth shone from his majesty. And I saw a vision according to the appearance that I had seen when he came to destroy the city, and the appearance according to the aspect that I had seen beside the river Chebar, and I fell upon my face. And the majesty of the Lord entered the temple by the way of the gate that looked toward the east. And the spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court; and behold, the house was filled with the glory of the Lord. And I heard one speaking to me from the house, and the man who was standing beside me said to me: Son of man, the place of my throne and the place of the footprints of my feet, where I dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel forever; […]

43:4.t: 'And when', he says, 'I had fallen down, the majesty of the Lord entered the temple by the way of the gate that looked toward the east; and at once the spirit lifted me up — for lying down I was not able to go on — and brought me into the inner court — for I had fallen outside —; and behold, I who had earlier beheld the glory of the God of Israel coming by the eastern way saw his house filled with the glory of the Lord, and I heard the voice of one speaking to me from the inner house' — what it said, Scripture does not relate, unless perhaps that saying of the apostle: And I heard unspeakable words which it is not lawful for men to speak —.

43:6.t: But that man, he says, who was standing beside the prophet spoke to him; and we plainly understand him to be the Lord: for to whom could what follows apply, Son of man, the place of my throne and the place of the footprints of my feet, where I dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel forever, except to him who dwells in the Church in the midst of the sons of Israel who see God? — and 'he dwells forever', not as in the temple of Solomon, for a time; and 'his place' is that of which it is written: And his place was made in peace, which surpasses all understanding; and 'the place of the footprints of his feet', as the apostles say: Let us worship in the place where his feet stood, and he said 'stood' beautifully: for in the Church the feet of the Lord stand, in the Synagogue they walk and pass by —; and so that we may know that this is said of the Church, there is joined: And the house of Israel shall no more pollute my holy name, which properly pertains to those who, being of holy life, abide in the Church; […]

43:8.t: Let the silly women laden with sins, who are carried about by every wind of doctrine, always learning and never arriving at the knowledge of the truth, hear these things according to the letter: that it is a mind joined to God, not nearness to the churches and a dwelling close to God, that calls forth clemency upon itself, and that rather the indignation of the Lord is stirred up when there is an unworthy inhabitant in consecrated places. They built, he says, their threshold beside my threshold, so that there was no difference between sacred and profane, and their posts beside my posts, so that there was one entrance for laity and priests — whence the apostle too says: But let a man prove himself, and so approach the body and blood of the Lord —; and to make what he was saying weightier, he joins in the following verse: And there was a wall between me and them, so that a very short wall divided the priestly sacrifices and the places of the sacraments of the body and blood of Christ. […]

43:9.t: And yet the merciful Lord again commands the prophet to bid them remove their former fornications far from themselves, and to abandon the ruins of their kings and princes and drive them away, not so much from themselves as from God; and he at once promises the rewards of good work, saying: And I will dwell in the midst of them — of whom it is said in the Gospel: There stands in the midst of you one whom you do not know —; and he will dwell not for a short time, as in the Synagogue, but forever, which is borne out in the Church of Christ.

43:10.t: But you, son of man, show the house of Israel the temple, and let them be confounded by their iniquities, and let them measure the structure, and let them blush for all that they have done. The figure of the house and of its structure, its exits and entrances, and its whole design, and all its precepts, and its whole order and all its laws, show them; and you shall write it in their sight, that they may keep all its distributions and its precepts and do them. This is the law of the house on the summit of the mountain: all its bounds round about are the Holy of Holies; this therefore is the law of the house. (LXX: "And you, son of man, show the house of Israel the house, and they shall cease from their sins, and its vision and its arrangement, and they themselves shall bear their torment for all that they have done. And you shall describe the house and its preparation, and its exits and its entrances, and its substance, and all its precepts, and all its ordinances and all its laws you shall show them; […]

43:11.t: There follows: Its exits and entrances, 'of the house' being understood — the exits, that is, of those who go out to those who are outside, and the entrances of those who through the discipline of teachers penetrate to the inner parts —. 'And all', he says, 'its design (or substance, as the Seventy translated: which pertains not so much to the nature of the house as to its furnishings and riches), and all the precepts, and the whole order and all the laws of the temple you shall show them, who have borne the torment of their iniquities and have ceased, or been confounded, over the things they had done before; and for this reason you shall show them, that they may keep all that has been commanded: for it profits nothing to know the design of the house and all its distributions — of which it is written: Many mansions with the Father, and again: He set the bounds of the nations according to the number of the sons of Israel (or of the angels of God) — unless you do what has been commanded'.

43:12.t: But the house, and the law of all the precepts of God, and the city which is established on the summit of the mountain, must be believed to be that one of which it is written: A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden, and: The rush of the river gladdens the city of God: which plainly refers to the Church of God, and it is situated on that mountain which is at the peak of all mountains and by which the prince of Tyre was wounded; and all the bounds and boundaries of this house are the Holy of Holies — in that house, that is, in the tabernacle that was made by Moses and in the temple that was built by Solomon, only the inner parts, where the Cherubim were and the mercy seat and the ark of the covenant and the table of incense, were called the Holy of Holies; but in this house, which is shown to Ezekiel and which is established on the summit of the mountain, all its boundaries are reckoned among the Holy of Holies —; […]

43:13.t: And these are the measures of the altar in the truest cubit, which had a cubit and a handbreadth (or palaesten [handbreadth]): in its bosom was a cubit, and a cubit in breadth, and the delimitation up to its lip, and round about one handbreadth: this also was the trench of the altar. And from the bosom of the earth to the lowest ledge two cubits, and the breadth of one cubit; and from the lesser ledge to the greater ledge four cubits, and the breadth of one cubit. And the 'ariel' itself of four cubits, and from the 'ariel' upward four horns. And the 'ariel' twelve cubits in length by twelve cubits of breadth, squared with equal sides. And the ledge fourteen cubits of length by fourteen of breadth in its four corners; and the crown round about it of half a cubit, and its bosom of one cubit round about; and its steps turned toward the east. […]

43:14.t: But the 'pit' of the altar, or 'depth' and 'height', for which in the Hebrew 'gab' is set down, was of two cubits from the bosom of the earth up to the lowest ledge, or up to the greatest mercy seat, and its breadth of one cubit: for the lower parts, deep and clinging to the earth, are contained in the dual number — which was also set down for the unclean animals —, but the upper parts, reaching to the ledge or mercy seat — which Theodotion called by the Hebrew name itself, 'azara' [ledge, enclosure] — have a breadth of one cubit, so that the dual number passes over to the single, and the good of marriage, which is lower, attains to the blessedness of unity. […]

43:15.t: And the 'ariel' itself was of four cubits, and from the 'ariel' upward four horns (or, as is said in the Seventy, and from the 'ariel' up to the upper parts of the horns one cubit): 'ariel', as most suppose, means 'my light is God' — about which we have spoken more fully in the prophet Isaiah too, where it is written: Woe to you, city 'ariel', which David stormed (or surrounded) —, but, as I think, 'lion' or 'strong one of God' — a name which refers properly to the altar, in which there is either the illumination of God, or the lion and his strength, as Jacob says to Judah: A lion's whelp, my son, Judah; to the prey, son, you have gone up. Resting you lay down as a lion, and as a lioness: who will rouse him? —; […]

43:16.t: And so that the obscurity of the present passage may little by little become clearer, there follows: And the 'ariel' twelve cubits in length by twelve cubits of breadth, square with equal sides, which no one doubts pertains to the twelve tribes which are written in the Revelation of John, and to the number of the apostles, about whose mystery I remember having spoken above; along the four sides — the sides of the world — twelve cubits each together make forty-eight cubits — of the priestly cities —, so that, with these as it were foundations distributed through the whole world, the strength of the Church may be made firm.

43:17.t: Furthermore: The ledge (for which the Seventy translated mercy seat, Theodotion, as above, 'azara', Symmachus περίβολον, that is, 'circuit') was of fourteen cubits of length by fourteen of breadth, in its four corners; and the 'crown' round about it of half a cubit (for which again the Seventy translated 'gison'), and the bosom (or, according to Symmachus, 'consummation') of it (and 'perfection') of one cubit round about: this covertly shows that our Lord, who is truly called the mercy seat, not only for our sins but for the whole world, came through fourteen generations from Abraham to David, and again through another fourteen to the captivity of Jeconiah, and by the mystery of the same number descended to earthly things, so that in the third tesseriscedecade [set of fourteen], and by the mystery of the divine number, he might save the four corners of the world — of which it is written: Many will come from the east and from the west and from the north and the south, and will recline with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in […]

43:18.t: And he said to me: Son of man, thus says the Lord God: These are the rites of the altar on whatever day it shall have been built, that a holocaust may be offered upon it and blood poured out. And you shall give to the priests and Levites who are of the seed of Zadok, who approach me, says the Lord God, that they may offer me a calf of the herd for sin. And taking some of its blood, you shall put it upon the four horns, and upon the four corners of the ledge, and upon the crown round about, and you shall cleanse it and expiate it. And you shall take the calf that has been offered for sin, and you shall burn it in a separate place of the house outside the sanctuary. And on the second day you shall offer a he-goat of the goats without blemish for sin, and they shall expiate the altar as they expiated it with the calf. […]

43:19.t: And first a victim is offered, and it is given to the priests of the race of Levi who are of the seed of 'Sadoc' — why the Seventy name him 'Saddoch' I am not able to know. And 'Sadoc' means 'righteous' —. And there is offered, according to the Seventy and Theodotion, a 'calf', according to Symmachus a 'bull', which in Hebrew is called 'phar' — and many passages of the Scriptures, and especially the epistle of Barnabas, which is held among the apocryphal scriptures, name him who was sacrificed for us a 'calf' —; and a he-goat of the goats is offered on the second day: whence also those who are to keep the Passover take from the flock a lamb and a kid, and those who could not keep the first Passover keep it in the second month: of which the one pertains to the righteous, the other to the penitent. […]

43:23.t: And when you have finished expiating it, you shall offer a calf of the herd without blemish, and a ram of the flock without blemish; and you shall offer them in the sight of the Lord, and the priests shall cast salt upon them, and shall offer them as a holocaust to the Lord. For seven days you shall make a he-goat for sin daily, and a calf of the herd and a ram of the flocks without blemish they shall offer. For seven days they shall expiate the altar and cleanse it, and they shall fill its hand; and when the days are completed, on the eighth day and onward the priests shall make your holocausts upon the altar, and those which they offer for peace; and I will be appeased toward you, says the Lord God. (LXX: "And when you have completed the expiation, they shall offer a calf of the oxen without blemish, and a ram of the sheep without blemish; and you shall offer them before the Lord, and the priests shall sprinkle salt upon them, and shall offer them as holocausts to the Lord. […]

43:25.t: And when the altar has been expiated, for seven days a he-goat or kid is offered for sin daily, and a calf of the herd and a ram of the flocks without blemish, so that through these sacrifices over seven days the altar may be expiated to perfection: in the seven days is shown the sabbath rest which, according to the apostle, is reserved for the people of the Lord, in which we hope for eternal and true rest and may by no means do the servile work of sins; and in the he-goat and the calf and the ram are shown three general offenses to which the whole race of mortals is subject: for we sin either in thoughts or in speech or in deed — thought is referred to the ram, which is the first of all sins and from which the other two sins are born; and the kid, or he-goat, to utterance and speech, which always disputes about loftier things; but deeds are properly assigned to the calf, which is bound over to the plowshare and to labor and to earthly works —. […]

43:26.t: And what is added, And they shall cleanse it, and shall fill its hand, as both the Hebrew and the other translators rendered it, signifies this: that the gifts of the altar itself too, for whose expiation the sacrifice is offered, must be filled up, just as it is offered for the priests and the people and the high priest, lest anything should seem to have stood empty in the sight of the Lord; for which the Seventy put: And they shall cleanse it, and shall fill their own hands, so that 'the priests' is understood, who, when they have been full of good works — for this is what full hands signify —, once the sabbath is past, may come to the eighth day of the resurrection — and say with the apostle: We have risen with Christ —, and beyond the eighth may tend toward heavenly things, and offer for us holocausts, or those offerings which are for the peace of our sins and for our salvation, so that, through the fire of the Holy Spirit, all that we think, speak and do may be converted into spiritual substance, and the Lord, […]

44:1.t: And he turned me back to the way of the gate of the outer sanctuary which looked toward the east, and it was shut; and the Lord said to me: This gate shall be shut, and it shall not be opened, and no man shall pass through it, because the Lord God of Israel has entered (or will enter) by it, and it shall be shut for the prince: the prince himself shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord; he shall enter by the way of the vestibule (that is, 'aelam') of the gate, and by its way he shall go out. (Where it is written in the Hebrew: It shall be shut for the prince, the Seventy translated: And it shall be shut, because the leader himself shall sit in it.) There are many gates which Scripture mentions in the description of Ezekiel's temple, both within and without; the preceding discourse also ran through the shape of the altar, its consecration and its sacrifices. That being finished, he comes to the gate of the outer sanctuary which looked toward the east, and it was shut; […]

Do you wish that I should meanwhile show you that the seventh and the eighth number contain very many mysteries? Let us read Ezekiel, and at one gate it is said: "And let him enter," it says, "through the gate of the east into the temple that is being built." In Ezekiel, in the last part. "And the high priest shall go up," it says, "by seven and eight steps." And could it be that at that gate there were both seven steps, and eight? But see what he says. The eastern gate, from which the light comes. Our Lord and Savior. There is indeed one gate, and no one enters through it except the high priest. And what is said there? "This gate shall always be shut." And it is not opened except to the priest. So therefore both the new and the old testament was always shut: it was not opened except to the Savior. For he is the one "who holds the key, who opens and no one shuts, who shuts and no one opens." So one gate has both seven and eight steps. […]

44:2.t: What, then, is this gate which is always shut, and by which the Lord God of Israel alone will enter? Surely it is the one of which the Savior speaks in the Gospel: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, and: Woe to you, doctors of the law, woe, who take away the key of knowledge: you yourselves do not enter, and those who are entering you hinder — of this, under the name of a book, Isaiah writes: The words of this book shall be like sealed words; when you give it to a man who does not know letters, and say to him: Read; he will answer you: I do not know letters. And they will give it to a man who knows letters, saying: Read; […]

— That the eastern gate beyond the bounds of the world is always shut and by no means lies open to human sight, the Gospel of John proves — when it says: No one has ever seen God except the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father; he has made him known, as if he had said in other words: And it shall be shut for the prince: the prince alone shall sit in it to eat the bread 'of perfect and consummate knowledge': for No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son, and he to whom the Son wills to reveal him —. Some fittingly understand the shut gate, through which the Lord God of Israel alone enters, and the leader for whom the gate is shut, as the Virgin Mary, who remained a virgin both before giving birth and after giving birth — for both at the time when the angel was saying: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; […]

What means this closed gate in the House of the Lord, except that Mary is to be ever inviolate? What does it mean that 'no man shall pass through it,' save that Joseph shall not know her? And what is this - 'The Lord alone enters in and goeth out by it' - except that the Holy Ghost shall impregnate her, and that the Lord of angels shall be born of her? And what means this—'it shall be shut for evermore' - but that Mary is a virgin before His Birth, a virgin in His Birth, and a virgin after His Birth?
44:2.s: De Annunt. Dom. iii (as quoted by Aquinas, AD 1274)

44:2.t: But in answer to those who argue that, if He were brought forth in the flesh, the Virgin was corrupted: and if she were not corrupted, that He was brought forth only in appearance, we say; the prophet declares, "the Lord, the God of Israel, hath entered in and gone out, and the gate remaineth closed." If, moreover, the Word was made flesh without sexual intercourse, being conceived altogether without seed, then was He born without injury to her virginity.
44:2.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

44:2.t: But just as He who was conceived kept her who conceived still virgin, in like manner also He who was born preserved her virginity intact, only passing through her and keeping her closed. The conception, indeed, was through the sense of hearing, but the birth through the usual path by which children come, although some tell tales of His birth through the side of the Mother of God. For it was not impossible for Him to have come by this gate, without injuring her seal in any way.
44:2.s: An Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith, Book 4, Chapter 14

44:2.t: In Ezekiel (Ezek. 46:1 and so on) it is written that the temple shown to him had three gates: the eastern, the southern, and the northern. God commands that the eastern gate always remain shut, with only the Prince entering and leaving through it. The eastern gate represents the blessed and glorious Virgin Mary, who remained shut before the Prince, that is, Christ, entered, and remained shut forever after he left.

44:3.t: This gate, then, which is shut to all — for No man shall pass through it —: It shall be shut for the prince (or for the leader), and will be reserved for his coming: who shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord — of which he himself declares in the Gospel, saying: My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to accomplish his work —; he himself is prince and high priest according to the order of Melchizedek, both victim and priest, who in the sight of the Father eats the heavenly bread with us and drinks the wine — of which he speaks in the Gospel: I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until I drink it new in the kingdom of my Father: namely in that kingdom of which the Apostle also writes: The kingdom of God is within you —; and the gate will be shut: for no one can know the mysteries of the Lord's passion and of his body and blood as the majesty of the thing deserves; […]

44:4.t: And he brought me by the way of the north gate in front of the house; and I looked, and behold, the glory of the Lord had filled the house of the Lord, and I fell on my face. And the Lord said to me: Son of man, set your heart, and see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I say to you concerning all the ceremonies of the house of the Lord, and concerning all its laws; and you shall set your heart on the ways of the temple, through all the exits of the sanctuary. The man who is the prophet's guide, and through whose showing he learns everything in the temple, after he had shown him the gate shut, never to be unbarred and yet open to him who entered through shut doors, leads the prophet to the way of the north gate, which itself too was in front of the house: no doubt this signifies the temple; […]

Therefore, because he had been cast down in humility, it is no longer the man but the Lord who says to him: Son of man, set your heart, and the rest: at the completion of the tabernacle and at the building of the temple which was erected by Solomon the glory of the Lord appeared, which afterward was done away by comparison with the glory of the Gospel — as the Apostle says: For what was glorified has not been glorified in this respect, because of the surpassing glory. For if what is done away was through glory, much more what remains is in glory —; and we must beware of thinking the doing away of the former glory to be its abolition, but must understand it thus: After that which is perfect has come, that which was in part will be done away — as if you were to compare a torch to the rays of the sun, or the light of a torch to a little lamp; for which reason it is also said of John the Baptist: He was a lamp shining in the house; […]

44:6.t: And you shall say to the house of Israel that provokes me: Thus says the Lord God: Let all your crimes suffice you, house of Israel, in that you bring in alien sons (or foreigners) uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary and to pollute my house; and you offer my loaves, the fat and the blood, and you dissolve my covenant (or you pass over my precept) in all your crimes. And you have not kept the precepts of my sanctuary, and you have set keepers of my observances in my sanctuary for yourselves. When he says: Let all your crimes suffice you (or your iniquities), he exhorts to repentance for former sins, lest we add sins to sins and prepare fuel for the fire to come — but let us hear what Isaiah says: Woe to those who draw sins as with a long cord, and iniquities as with the yoke-strap of a calf —.

44:7.t: And the first sin is that they bring in alien sons — or foreigners — uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in the sanctuary of God and to pollute the house of the Lord — for A little leaven corrupts the whole lump, and in some copies of Proverbs there is found: Do not bring the wicked man into the tents of the righteous —. At this place the Jews and the Ebionites — who accept circumcision of the flesh — press us as to how we can explain the present passage: uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, meaning, that is, that after the spiritual understanding we ought also to undergo circumcision of the flesh; but — we who read Paul saying: And I testify to every man who is circumcised that, if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing, and that word of Jeremiah: Behold, your ears are uncircumcised, and you would not hear, and in Exodus: Moses spoke before the Lord, saying: Behold, the sons of Israel have not listened, and how will Pharaoh listen to me? […]

And it must be read thus, and the order of the reading rendered so: 'Since you bring alien sons, uncircumcised in heart and in body, into my sanctuary and pollute my house, you dare to offer loaves and fat and blood — the mystic sacraments — and you do not understand what you have dissolved, and that you have transgressed my covenant in all your crimes and impieties; and that you have not kept the precepts of my sanctuary nor set keepers of my ceremonies in my sanctuary' — and the whole threat is against those who have not heeded the Apostle warning beforehand: Lay hands hastily on no one, and do not share in other men's sins —; […]

44:9.t: But also he who holds heretical thoughts in his mind and arranges blasphemous assertions against the knowledge of Christ in his heart, this man is "uncircumcised" in "heart." But he who guards a pure faith in the sincerity of conscience, he is circumcised in heart; of whom it can be said: "blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see God."

Thus says the Lord God: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh shall enter my sanctuary, no alien son who is in the midst of the sons of Israel. But also the Levites who went far away from me in the straying of the sons of Israel, and strayed from me after their idols, shall bear their iniquity, who were in my sanctuary temple-keepers and doorkeepers of the gates of the house and ministers of the house: and they slaughtered the holocausts and the victims of the people, and they stood before them to minister to them. Because, then, they ministered to them in the sight of their idols and became to the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity, therefore I have lifted up my hand against them, says the Lord God, and they have borne their iniquity. And they shall not draw near to me to exercise the priesthood for me, nor shall they approach any of my sanctuary next to the Holy of Holies, but they shall bear their shame and their crimes which they committed. […]

44:10.t: How is it that in the book of Ezekiel, where a description is given of the future church and of the heavenly Jerusalem, the priests who have sinned are degraded to the rank of sacristans and doorkeepers, and although they are in the temple of God, that is, on the right hand, they are not among the rams but among the poorest of the sheep?

44:12.t: For certainly no one does more harm in the Church than one who has the name and rank of sanctity, while he acts perversely. For him, when he transgresses, no one presumes to take to task; and the offence spreads forcibly for example, when out of reverence to his rank the sinner is honoured.

44:14.t: Where we have put: And I will make them doorkeepers of the house in all its service and in all that is done in it, them, namely, of the Levites who went far away from God in the straying of the sons of Israel and followed idols to which they sacrificed victims, Symmachus, considering the order of the reading and its sense, translated more correctly, saying: For I had made them keepers of the doors of the house, of all its service and of all that is done in it, so that it does not refer to those who are to be in the temple, but to those who were.

44:17.t: And when they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed with garments (or robes) of linen, and nothing woollen shall come upon them (or and they shall not be clothed with woollens) while they minister in the gates (or from the gates) of the inner court and within. Linen fillets shall be on their heads (or they shall have linen turbans upon their heads), and linen breeches shall be on their loins, and they shall not be girded in sweat (or violently). And when they go out to the outer court to the people, they shall put off their garments (or robes) in which they had ministered, and they shall lay them (or them) up in the chambers (or exedras) of the sanctuary (or of the holy places), and they shall clothe themselves in other garments (or robes), and they shall not sanctify the people in their garments (or robes). But they shall not shave their head, nor let their hair grow long, but clipping they shall clip their heads (or: They shall not shave their heads, and they shall not crop their hair close; […]

What all these things indicate according to the spiritual sense, what follows will show. That there are holy and spiritual garments the Apostle teaches, saying: Put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and in another place: Put on the bowels of mercy, goodness, humility, meekness and patience, and again: Strip off the old man with his works, and put on the new, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of the Creator; and I think this too signifies the same: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality. And when this corruptible has put on incorruption — and this mortal immortality —, then shall come to pass the word that is written, and the rest — concerning the priestly garments it is written more fully in Exodus, and we once published a book to whose interpretation the diligent reader must be sent: for we cannot comprehend a broad subject in a brief discourse —; […]

The priests of Egypt use linen garments not only within but without — but the divine religion has one dress for the ministry, another for common use —; and the fillets and breeches are rightly put on, so that seemliness and decorum may be preserved — namely, lest in climbing the steps of the altar and running about at the ministries they uncover their shame —; shaven heads belong to the superstition of the Gentiles; but from wine, as far as my knowledge goes, I do not think any of the Gentiles abstains.

44:18.t: As for what follows: Linen fillets (or turbans) shall be on their heads, I think it shows the crown of grace of which it is written: For your head shall receive a crown of graces; nor let that which the Apostle says about the uncovered and bared head raise a question for us: A woman ought to have authority over her head because of the angels. For if a woman is not veiled, let her be shorn; but if it is shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered. For a man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of the man: for if it belongs to men not to cover the head, it seems contradictory how the priests are now ordered to cover their heads with linen fillets or a turban; […]

44:19.t: And because he had once commanded what garments the priests ought to use when they are within at their ministries, he orders again that, going out into the chambers — or exedras — of the holy places, they put off their former garments and put on others, lest, if they have the holy garments, they sanctify the people placed outside, who have not yet been sanctified nor prepared themselves for the sanctification of the temple, so as to be a Nazirite of the Lord; by which we learn that we ought not to enter the Holy of Holies in everyday garments, any whatever, polluted by the use of common life, but to hold the sacraments of the Lord with a clean conscience and clean garments.

Further, when he goes outside and mingles with the people, he lays aside the priestly garments in the chamber in which the riches of the Lord are kept, and the priests use other garments and other teaching for the common crowd, lest the people be sanctified in their robes: for it is a grave thing to take up the burden of the multitude beyond one's strength, as Solomon says: It is a snare to a man to sanctify hastily anything of his own: for when he has made a vow, repentance steals upon him. — Further, the Nazirites too offer themselves of their own accord; and whoever has vowed anything and has not fulfilled it is guilty of the vow; hence it is also said of widows: When they have grown wanton in Christ, they wish to marry, having condemnation because they have made void their first faith — for It is better not to promise than to promise and not to perform —: Hannah offered Samuel, who remained in perpetual holiness; […]

44:20.t: As for what follows: But they shall not shave their head, nor let their hair grow long, but clipping they shall clip their heads, it is clearly shown that we ought neither to have shaven heads like the priests and worshipers of Isis and Serapis, nor again to let our hair hang down, which is properly the mark of the luxurious and of barbarians and soldiers, but that the seemly bearing of priests should be shown at first sight; as for what the Seventy said: They shall not shave their heads, and they shall not crop their hair close, but covering they shall cover their heads, according to them we learn that baldness is not to be made with the razor, nor is the head to be cropped so close that it seems like those of the shaven, but the hair is to be let grow only so far that the skin is covered — or certainly that the priests are always to cover their heads, according to that line of Vergil: Covered, to veil his locks with a purple mantle; but this is a forced interpretation —.

And the Lord wills his priests to have perpetual hair of consecration and to cover their heads, not with any veil from outside but with their own natural hair, not for ornament and luxury but for seemliness — hence the hairs of the head of the apostles too are numbered, as the Savior says: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered: of that head of which it is also written in Ecclesiastes: The eyes of the wise man are in his head. And the head of the man is Christ, which the sinner tramples and despises and, so to speak, shaves with a razor and takes away its beauty: which the Ammonites also did to those whom David had sent as envoys —; but if transgression of the law dishonors God, it follows that he who keeps the precepts of the law honors him — that what is written may be fulfilled: That all may honor the Son, as they honor the Father —.

44:21.t: And wine the priests and Levites shall not drink, not only for their ministry, but indeed when they are about to enter the Holy of Holies, lest the mind be weighed down and the understanding become duller — hence the Apostle too says: It is good, he says, not to drink wine and not to eat meat, and in another place: And wine, in which is debauchery — for The people ate and drank, and rose up to play —; and what he grants Timothy, to drink a little wine, he clearly shows why he granted it: For your stomach, he says, and your frequent infirmities —.

Further, as for what follows, that: No priest, when he is about to enter the inner court, shall drink wine, it is clear that by drunkenness and strong drink the state of the mind is overturned, and that we are not fully wise when the mind is taken up with wine and satiety; but drunkenness is shown not only in the drinking of wine but in all things by which, both in contracts and in the business of the world, in losses and gains, in love and hatred, the mind is made drunk and wavers and cannot keep its state; and because we are encompassed by frail flesh and are compelled — for food and clothing and the necessities which pertain to the body — to do some things which we ought not to do, at least this is required of us: that — when we return into ourselves and know why we were born and enter the inner parts and shrines of the temple — we withdraw from the vices of the world and commit not even the least sins; […]

44:22.t: A widow and a divorced woman (or a woman cast out) they shall not take as wives, but a virgin of the seed of the house of Israel; but also a widow who has been the widow of a priest they may take. And they shall teach my people; what the difference is between holy and polluted, between clean and unclean, they shall show them. And when there is a controversy (as is added in the Seventy, of blood), they shall stand in my judgments, and they shall judge; my laws and my precepts they shall keep in all my solemn feasts, and they shall sanctify my sabbaths. And they shall not go in to a dead man, lest they be polluted, except to father and mother, son and daughter, brother and sister who has not had another man: in these they shall be defiled. And after he has been cleansed, seven days shall be counted to him, and on the day of his entry into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister to me in the sanctuary, he shall offer for his sin, says the Lord God. But they shall have no inheritance; […]

44:23.t: It is the office of the priest too to teach the people: What the difference is between holy and polluted, between clean and unclean, so that we refer the first to doctrines, the second to the works which are performed through the flesh — for who understands transgressions? —.

44:24.t: And when there is a controversy 'about any matter' or, as the Seventy translated, 'of blood', that is, what pertains to a mortal crime: The priests shall stand in my judgments, so that they do not judge according to rank nor accept the person of poor or rich in judgment, but stand in the judgments of God — and remember that psalm: God has stood in the synagogue of gods, and in the midst he judges gods, calling 'gods' those who have the power of judging men —: for with what judgment they have judged, they themselves will be judged. My laws, he says, and my precepts they shall keep in all my solemn feasts, so that they may know how Christ our Passover was sacrificed, how we ought to fulfill seven weeks of joy and gladness, and humble our souls in fasting and in the sound of trumpets, and understand also spiritual feasts of Tabernacles — in which we say: I am a sojourner and a stranger, as all my fathers were —; […]

44:25.t: As for what follows: And they shall not go in to a dead man, lest they be polluted: it belongs properly to the priestly office not to touch dead things, so that he who prays for the vices of others may himself approach the altar clean — of which dead the Savior too speaks in the Gospel: Leave the dead to bury their own dead —; these are defiled in a dead father when they forsake their Creator, and in a dead mother, departing from the Church, in a son also and a daughter, in that the one pertains to thoughts, the other to works — which is said more expressively in Greek, νοητὰ καὶ αἰσθητὰ [things of the mind and things of the senses] —; in brother also and sister: he who, reborn of the same spirit, if he has reckoned him dead, is defiled in him, only on this condition, if the sister has remained a virgin and not been stained by the embrace of any man — from which we understand the virginal privilege, that the contact of any man whatever takes away perfect purity; […]

44:26.t: And after the priest has been cleansed by the order of purification which is written in the Mosaic law: Seven days shall be counted to him — either the perfect number of penitence, or after the consummation of the world, when we have passed over to the true ogdoad —, that he may enter the Holy of Holies — for this is the inner court — and be able to minister in the sanctuary and always to offer a victim for the sin of conscience; and let there be no time in which he does not remember that he was stained over father and mother, son and daughter, brother and sister: for we are compelled to do many things, set as we are in the straits of this world, either by the condition of the flesh or by the frailty of nature.

44:28.t: But he who shows himself such as to minister in the sanctuary and enter the inner court and always offer sacrifice to the Lord — so that, a true priest, he may be true, or rather an imitator of him of whom it is written: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek —, he shall have no inheritance except God, who is his inheritance, nor shall he receive a possession in Israel — that is, among the common crowd —, but a priestly one, so that the Lord may say of him: I am the inheritance and: I am their possession — whom, when they have found him, they will speak and say: I will hold him and will not let him go, and they will sing with the prophet: The Lord is my portion —.

44:29.t: The victim both for sin and for trespass (or for ignorance) they shall eat, and every vow (or separation) in Israel shall be theirs; and the first portions of all the firstborn, and all the libations of all that are offered, shall be the priests'; and the first portions of your foods you shall give to the priest, that he may lay up a blessing for his house (or that he may put blessings upon your houses). For 'victim' and sacrifice, which in Hebrew is called 'manaa', Aquila and Symmachus translated 'gift'; again, for 'vow', which the Seventy translated ἀφόρισμα, that is, 'separation', Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion translated ἀνάθημα [a thing devoted], which in Hebrew is called 'herem'; and it must be considered that all the things which the Lord now speaks through the prophet he had already said before through Moses; […]

44:30.t: The first portions, according to the letter, are those of living and lifeless things which are born first and which the earth first brings forth; the firstfruits of our foods too are offered to the priests, so that we taste nothing of the new crops unless the priest has tasted it first; and we do this so that the priest may lay up our blessing and offering in his house, or so that at his prayer the Lord may bless our houses: great is the dignity of priests, but great the ruin if they sin; we rejoice at the ascent, but let us fear the fall: it is not so great a joy to have held the heights as it is a grief to have fallen from the loftier places — for we shall render account not only for our own transgressions but for those of all whose gifts we abuse; and we are by no means anxious for their salvation —.

44:31.t: Anything that has died of itself or been caught by a beast, of birds or of cattle, the priests shall not eat; and according to the letter these precepts befit every chosen race, royal and priestly — which refers properly to Christians, who have been anointed with the spiritual oil of which it is written: God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows —: that he not eat 'what has died of itself', whether of birds or of cattle, whose blood has not been shed — which in the Acts of the Apostles is called 'strangled', and that these things must necessarily be observed the letter of the apostles from Jerusalem warns — and what has been caught by a beast, because that too is likewise strangled: and it condemns priests who, out of the greed of the gullet, do not keep these things in the case of thrushes, figpeckers, dormice and other things of this kind. […]

45:1.t: And when you begin to divide the land as a possession, set apart firstfruits to the Lord, a sanctified portion of the land, twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in breadth; it shall be sanctified in all its border round about. And of this there shall be a sanctified portion five hundred by five hundred, four-square round about, and fifty cubits for its suburbs all around. And from this measure you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand, and in it shall be the temple (or the sanctification) and the Holy of Holies. The sanctified portion of the land shall be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who approach to the ministry of the Lord; and it shall be a place for them for houses and for a sanctuary of holiness: twenty-five thousand of length and ten thousand of breadth. But the Levites who minister to the house, they shall possess twenty chambers (for which the Seventy translated: they shall hold a city to dwell in). […]

But if we wish to compare spiritual things with spiritual and, following certain interpreters, to climb to higher things — they assert that the present things are a figure of things to come, and that all that is said pertains to the heavenly Jerusalem, which is the mother of us all, and to the Church of the firstborn —, it will not indeed be difficult to say what has been said by others, but we fear that the prudent reader may by no means accept an exposition of this kind; hence all things are to be referred both to the present time and to the Church, which now labors in the world and hastens to go to heavenly things: so that out of the whole world some are chosen as a possession of God to possess the holy place, and others, who have advanced to greater things, to hold the Holy of Holies; […]

45:3.t: When this description is finished, another measure, of a sanctification to be set apart, is prescribed afresh: that after the former measure another land be measured, of twenty-five thousand reeds in length and ten thousand in breadth, in which there is by no means the temple, that is, the holy place, but the Holy of Holies.

45:4.t: And in it let the priests dwell who approach to the ministry of the Lord; and let them dwell there at the time when they discharge the priestly office: and let this possession be, as we have said, of twenty-five thousand reeds in length and ten thousand in breadth.

45:5.t: Further, the Levites, who serve the priests and have ministries of their own, will receive a place for building twenty 'chambers' — according to Aquila; 'exedras' according to Symmachus; 'cells' according to Theodotion; or, as the Seventy translated, 'a city', by which we understand that a certain separate place for the dwelling of the Levites is called by the name of a city —, a place which is to have five thousand reeds in breadth and twenty-five thousand in length. All these things, that is, the sanctuary and the second sanctuary, and the Holy of Holies, and the dwellings of the priests and the houses of the Levites who minister to the priests, are called places separated and consecrated for ministry and for sanctification for the house of Israel.

45:7.t: After the fourfold description of the holy land a fifth division is set down: that the prince or leader of the people should receive on this side and on that, that is, on either side of the sanctuary, for his possession, and should dwell in the city, and that his possession should face the place set apart for the temple and the face of the city, and should be from the side of the sea, that is, from the west, as far as the other side of the sea, having the breadth which the prophet describes below in the description of the individual tribes. Then follows: But in length along each part — which the individual tribes receive — from the western border — that is, of the sea — as far as the eastern border — where this ends we learn in the description of the tribes —; and this will be the possession of the leader or prince in the land of Israel. These things have been said for the present so that the plain account of the history may be known.

45:9.t: Thus says the Lord God: Let it suffice you, princes in Israel; leave off iniquity and plunder, and do judgment and righteousness: separate your borders from my people, says the Lord God. For 'plunder' the Seventy translated 'misery'; for 'borders', 'oppression'. And the sense is: 'Since you have received your portion, O princes — as Scripture says: To the prince also on this side and on that, in the separation of the sanctuary, in the possession of the city (understand: you shall give) —, and your power is so great that your possession has received the portion of one tribe: therefore I command and admonish you that it suffice to have committed iniquity and plunder up to now, while you invade and snatch away what belongs to others; […]

45:10.t: A just balance and a just 'oephi' and a just batus you shall have; the 'oephi' and the batus shall be equal and of one measure, so that the batus holds a tenth part, and the 'oephi' a tenth part: according to the measure of the 'corus' shall be their equal balancing. And the shekel has twenty obols; moreover, twenty shekels and twenty-five shekels and fifteen shekels make a mina. (LXX: "A just balance and a just measure and a just choenix you shall have for measure, and likewise there shall be one choenix for receiving: the tenth part of the gomer the choenix, and the tenth part of the gomer the 'oephi'; in relation to the gomer it shall be equal, and for weight twenty obols: twenty shekels, five and twenty shekels and fifteen shekels shall be your mina.") […]

45:13.t: And these are the firstfruits which you shall take: the sixth part of an 'oephi' from a 'corus' of grain, and the sixth part of an 'oephi' from a 'corus' of barley. The measure of oil also, a batus of oil, is the tenth part of a 'corus'; and ten bati make a 'corus', because ten bati fill a 'corus'. (LXX: "And these are the firstfruits which you shall set apart: the sixth part of a measure from a gomor of wheat and the sixth part of an 'oephi' from a 'corus' of barley. And the ordinance of the oil: a cotyle — that is, a cyathus — of oil from ten cotylae, because ten cotylae are a gomor.") Here too, the names of the measures having been changed, everything in the edition of the Seventy is confused, so that what is said cannot be understood: for they who above had said 'measure' for 'oephi', and 'choenix' for 'batus', and 'gomor' for 'corus', 'weight' for 'siclus', here too say 'measure' for 'oephi', for 'corus' now 'gomer', now 'corus' itself, and in the measure of oil 'cotyle', that is, 'cyathus', for 'batus'. […]

45:15.t: And one ram from a flock of two hundred, from those which they nourish in Israel, for a sacrifice and for a holocaust and for peace offerings, to make expiation for them, says the Lord God. All the people of the land shall be bound to these firstfruits for the prince of Israel; and upon the prince shall be the holocausts and the sacrifice and the libations, at the solemnities and at the calends and at the sabbaths: at all the solemnities of the house of Israel: he shall make the sacrifice for sin and the holocaust and the peace offerings, to make expiation for the house of Israel. Above he said what portion of the things that are weighed, and of the measures too, both of dry kinds and of liquids, ought to be offered to the prince; now he keeps the same order of firstfruits in living creatures, and commands Israel to offer one out of a flock of two hundred rams: Which Israel nourishes, for a sacrifice and for a holocaust and for peace offerings, to make expiation for the people of Israel, says the Lord God. […]

And as in the preceding we read that the sixtieth part of the things that are weighed and that are subject to measure ought to be offered to the prince, so now the two-hundredth part of the living creatures is commanded to be offered, and the whole people is subject to the precept of this law and of this command: that it offer to the leader or prince, because, of course, through him holocausts and sacrifices and libations are offered for the people at each solemnity, and the house of God is expiated; from which it is to be noticed that, as the people is debtor to offer firstfruits to the prince, so the prince is debtor to the people to offer victims for it; and him, according to tropology, we can understand as none other than God the Savior. […]

45:18.t: If then we have learned spiritual solemnities, we shall consequently be taught spiritual victims too: a calf is taken from the herd — or a bull, as Symmachus translated —, free and pressed by no yoke, that is, by the burden of sins, and without blemish: Who did no sin, nor was guile found in his mouth, a young calf putting forth horns and hoofs: so that in him the sanctuary may be cleansed and expiated.

Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first of the month, you shall take a calf from the herd without blemish, and you shall expiate the sanctuary. And the priest shall take of the blood of what will be for sin, and shall put it on the doorposts of the house and on the four corners of the ledge of the altar and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court. And thus you shall do on the seventh of the month for each one who was ignorant and was deceived by error, and you shall make expiation for the house. In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a solemnity; for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten. And the prince shall make on that day, for himself and for all the people of the land, a calf for sin; and in the solemnity of seven days he shall make as a holocaust to the Lord seven calves and seven rams without blemish daily for seven days, and for sin a he-goat of the goats daily; […]

45:19.t: And the priest, he says, shall take of its blood which will be for the sin of all, who in other words is called a lamb in Exodus, and in the Gospel, as John the Baptist says: Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world; and the blood itself is precious, in which we are redeemed in the passion of the Lord Savior, by whose flesh we are fed and with whose blood we are given drink, by which are touched the four corners of the ledge of the 'altar' — for which Theodotion put the Hebrew word itself, 'azara' [ledge, court], or of the 'temple', as the Seventy translated —, so that the house and the altar may be sanctified — for all the elements of the world are sanctified by this blood — so that, when someone has been expiated and cleansed, he may enter the gate of the inner court and be able to know the secrets of the Lord, and consequently come to the seventh day of the first month and attain rest and offer sacrifice to the Lord: both for ignorance — of which David speaks: The sins of my youth and of my […]

45:21.t: And when the two solemnities of the first month have been completed, that is, of the first day and of its seventh, he comes to the fourteenth day of the month, on which is the solemnity of the Passover, of which it is written: For our Passover has been sacrificed, Christ; then we eat unleavened bread for seven days in rest and security of all things, when, destroying the leaven of malice and wickedness, we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, while our prince offers all these things for us: and first 'for himself' — for he took up a human body and for sin destroyed sin, he who grieves for us and bears our infirmities —, then 'for his house' — which is written in the Seventy but is not found in the Hebrew — that is, for the Church, and for all the people of the land, namely the whole human race: He is the Savior, indeed, of all men and especially of the faithful; and he himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not only for us, but for the whole world.

45:23.t: And when the calf has been offered for all the people of the land, on the seven remaining days of the Lord's passion seven calves and seven rams without blemish are offered daily, so that they may be burned up as a holocaust and by the Lord's fire: and the seven calves and seven rams are those who are conformed to the Lord's passion, so that they may imitate the true calf and the true ram, and by the blood of the martyrs through seven days the sins of the whole world may be cleansed; a he-goat of the goats too is offered for sin daily, namely for seven days.

45:24.t: And it must be noted more carefully that in the sacrifice an 'oephi' for each calf and an 'oephi' for each ram and a 'hin' of oil are offered, which are commanded by the law, but in the offering of the he-goat neither an 'oephi' nor, as the Seventy translated, a 'cooking' is set down — they who for 'oephi' translated πέμμα, that is, 'cooking' —; but the 'hin', which is a fixed measure of oil, of which we have already spoken before, is taken up in the sacrifice of the calf and of the ram, so that we may receive the fuel of everlasting light, and rest from labor, and healing from weariness after the appeasement of sins.

45:25.t: In the seventh month too, on the fifteenth day of the month, that is, of the Scenopegia, the same order of oblation and sacrifices is to be kept: Both for sin and for the holocaust and in sacrifice and in oil, so that, darkness having been put to flight and the light of the oil having risen, we may attain the festival of the Lord, and may have brighter solemnities, in which all our sins are forgiven us.

46:1.t: And meanwhile, before we discuss what these things signify, the very words of Scripture must be laid open παραφραστικῶς [by way of paraphrase]. The gate, he says, of the inner court on six days — of which it is written: Six days you shall labor and do all your works — shall be shut, and not just any gate, but the one that faces toward the east, whence the sun of righteousness rises; further, on the sabbath day, that is, the seventh, on which there is rest, it will be opened every week, and again, when thirty days are completed, when there is the end of one month and the beginning of another, on the new moon, namely the day of the kalends, it will be opened, so that the privilege the seventh day has in the week, the beginning of the month may have as its privilege too.

Let these things be set down for the sake of clarity; now, the Lord granting, let us unfold the spiritual sense. During the six days on which we work in the world, the eastern gate of the inner court is shut to us; but after we have come to the seventh day, that is, to the sabbath day on which there is eternal rest, or to the day of the kalends, when after blind night and dreadful darkness there is the beginning of light, the eastern gate is opened to us; and if any of us, through the merits of the virtues, has attained the name and dignity of a leader, he will enter by the way of the vestibule of the gate from outside, that is, through the labors of this world, and through the gate of the Church, which is still set within earthly bounds, not into the inner court — for this is what is written in the present passage — but to the threshold of the inner gate: and he will stand in it; […]

46:2.t: But why the gate of the inner court that faces toward the east is opened on the seventh day and on the day of the kalends, the following discourse will show: And the prince shall enter, he says, by the way of the gate from outside — namely of the outer court —, and shall stand on the threshold of the gate — of the inner court, which faces the east —, and he shall not enter the inner court, but, while he stands, other priests are to make for him the 'holocaust' — which Symmachus translated 'offering' —, and the peace offerings — or those which pertain to salvation —, so that, after the prince's victim has been burned up by the sacred fire and the leader has been reconciled to God, he may then worship upon the threshold of the gate of the inner court on which he has stood, and go out. What then? After the prince's going out will the gate be shut at once? […]

46:4.t: And since he had said above: The priests shall make his holocaust and his peace offerings, and had not indicated the number of the holocaust, he now adds: And this holocaust the prince shall offer to the Lord on the sabbath day — he will offer it, however, not by himself, but through the priests, of whom it is written: And the priests shall make his holocaust and his peace offerings —: six, he says, lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish, so that the sacrifice of the ram is the measure of an 'oephi' — which in Hebrew is called 'epha' —, while for the six lambs the sacrifice is what the hand of the one who offers was able to offer, and for each 'oephi' there will be the measure of oil that is called 'hin'; […]

And this very holocaust, which the prince offers through the priests on the sabbath day, is bounded by the number of six lambs without blemish — namely after the six days on which we work in the world — and a ram without blemish, which is the prince of the flock, so that for each ram an 'oephi' is offered in sacrifice, that is, the tenth part of a 'corus'; but in the sacrifice of the six lambs no fixed measure is laid down, but as much as the hand of the one who offers shall give, that is, according to the quality and measure of his works; and he will offer a 'hin' of oil for each 'oephi' — that is, the oil which the five virgins prepared for themselves —, to anoint the fine flour or mix it, so that every offering to God may be full of the light of truth, and the face of the one who offers may be made glad with oil; […]

46:5.t: Thus says the Lord God: The gate of the inner court that faces toward the east shall be shut on the six days on which work is done; but on the sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the kalends also it shall be opened, and the prince shall enter by the way of the vestibule of the gate from outside, and shall stand on the threshold of the gate, and the priests shall make his holocaust and his peace offerings, and he shall worship upon the threshold of the gate, and shall go out; but the gate shall not be shut until evening. And the people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate on the sabbaths and kalends before the Lord. And this holocaust the prince shall offer to the Lord on the sabbath day: six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish, and a sacrifice of an 'oephi' for the ram, but for the lambs a sacrifice such as his hand shall give, and a 'hin' of oil for each 'oephi'; […]

46:8.t: And when the prince enters, let him enter by the way of the vestibule of the gate, and let him go out by the same way. And when the people of the land enter in the sight of the Lord on the solemn feasts, he who enters by the gate of the north to worship, let him go out by the way of the southern gate; and he who enters by the way of the southern gate, let him go out by the way of the gate of the north: he shall not return by the way of the gate by which he entered, but shall go out opposite it. But the prince in their midst shall enter with those who enter and shall go out with those who go out. And on market days and on solemn feasts the sacrifice shall be an 'oephi' for the calf and an 'oephi' for the ram, but for the lambs the sacrifice shall be as his hand shall find, and a 'hin' of oil for each 'oephi'. […]

46:9.t: Then too, he does not seek market days or solemn feasts, nor does he observe any difference of days, because every time is a festival as well; but the people enter and go out only on market days and on solemn feasts, and not by the same way, but by one way and then another: for it is written: And when the people of the land enter in the sight of the Lord on the solemn feasts, he who enters by the gate of the north to worship, let him go out by the way of the southern gate; and he who enters by the way of the southern gate, let him go out by the way of the gate of the north: he shall not return by the way of the gate by which he entered, but shall go out opposite it — which is commanded not only to those who go out of Sodom, and to whom it is said: Do not look back, nor only to those who put their hand to the plow, that they not look back at the things that are behind their back, but those too who are set in the house of the Lord are commanded not to look behind their backs and return to the weak and beggarly […]

The southern gate represents the Old Testament, while the northern gate represents the New. Those said to come from the south represent the Jews; those from the north represent the Gentiles. The Jews, then, who knew God and to whom the Law had been given from the direction of the sun, that is, from the south, where the sun burns more fiercely, are rightly said to come to the Church. They entered through the southern gate because, recognizing that Christ had been prophesied in many ways and prefigured in various forms in the Old Testament, they were drawn by their own Scriptures to embrace faith in Christ. The Gentiles, however, abandoning idolatry and renouncing the one who said, “I will sit on the mountain of the covenant, on the sides of the north; I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High” (Isa. 14:13), are fittingly said to come from the north. […]

46:10.t: But the prince, he says, in their midst will be, namely in the midst of those entering and going out, according to what is written: In the midst among you stands one whom you do not know, and the Apostle: Or do you not know that Christ is in you? — but if it is said to those who do not know that Christ stands in their midst, how much more to those who know; but when Christ has stood among those who know, then the body will become dead because of sin and the spirit living because of righteousness! —; and the prince enters with those who enter, and goes out with those who go out, standing by as witness of both, of virtue and of sin.

46:11.t: Therefore on market days and on solemn feasts — namely of the sabbaths and kalends and of every festival, of which we have spoken earlier — both with the calf and with the ram a single 'oephi' will be offered in sacrifice; but with the lambs there will be no fixed number, nor is the choice left to the will, but one will use his strength and the good of his conscience, so as to offer as much as he can, not as much as he wishes; and over all, a 'hin' of oil for each 'oephi', so that the fine flour may be anointed and the lamp lit in the sight of the Lord, and those who use it may be able to say: But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord.

46:12.t: But when the prince makes a spontaneous holocaust or voluntary peace offerings to the Lord, the gate that faces toward the east shall be opened for him, and he shall make his holocaust and his peace offerings as is usually done on the sabbath day, and he shall go out, and the gate shall be shut after he has gone out. And a yearling lamb without blemish he shall make as a holocaust daily to the Lord; morning by morning he shall make it. And a sacrifice (or manaa) he shall make with it morning by morning, a sixth part of an 'oephi' (or of a measure), and of oil a third part of a 'hin', to be mixed (or according to Symmachus sprinkled) with the fine flour; a sacrifice (or manaa) to the Lord, lawful, continual and perpetual. You shall make the lamb and the sacrifice and the oil morning by morning, an everlasting holocaust. Where we read 'without blemish' and in the Hebrew is written 'thamim', Aquila translates 'perfect'; and where the Seventy have 'manaa', Theodotion translated 'sacrifice', Aquila and Symmachus 'gift'; […]

46:13.t: And since he had said in general: A spontaneous holocaust or voluntary peace offerings to the Lord, and had not added bull or calf, ram or sheep, and a he-goat for sin, he teaches what this holocaust is: A yearling lamb, he says, without blemish he shall make as a holocaust; and not on fixed days, but: daily; nor at any other hour, but: morning by morning he shall make it: namely each 'morning', when, the sun having risen, there is the beginning of light — of which 'morning' David speaks in a psalm: In the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will stand before you, and will see, and in another place: In the evening weeping will linger, and in the morning gladness, and again: O God, my God, to you I keep watch from the morning. […]

46:14.t: And so in the holocaust of this lamb, without blemish and a yearling, which is always offered in the morning: the prince himself shall make a sacrifice (or 'manaa', and fine flour or gift) morning by morning, a sixth part of an 'oephi', of fine flour being understood — and a sixth part of an 'oephi' is half a modius; for if an 'oephi' is the tenth part of a 'corus', that is, three modii, no one doubts that the sixth part of an 'oephi' makes half a modius —. Of the oil also, a third part of the measure 'hin' is offered, to be mixed (or sprinkled) with the fine flour; a sacrifice to the Lord, lawful, continual and perpetual, which is interrupted on no day but at every time, when the sun has risen, is always offered, so that what is set at the end of this chapter may be fulfilled: He shall make the lamb for a sacrifice, and the oil, morning by morning, an everlasting holocaust.

46:16.t: Thus says the Lord God: If the prince (or leader) gives a gift to any of his sons, his inheritance shall belong to his sons; they shall possess it by inheritance. But if he gives a legacy from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of remission (for which Theodotion set down the Hebrew word itself, deror), but it shall return to the prince; but his inheritance shall belong to his sons. And the prince shall not take from the inheritance of the people by violence and from their possession, but from his own possession he shall give an inheritance to his sons, so that my people be not scattered, each one from his possession. Thus far the discourse about the prince; now precepts are given about his heirs, or rather about gifts, inheritance and legacies: to whom he ought to give, and whose the possession is, whether for a time or everlasting. […]

46:18.t: But what follows: And the prince shall not take from the inheritance of the people by violence (or, as the Seventy translated, so as to oppress them, or, as Aquila and Symmachus, afflict them and sadden them), but from his own possession he shall give an inheritance to his sons, censures not only the priests and princes of that time but also those of ours, who grow richer through the dignity of the priesthood and, beyond what is owed them by the Lord's ordinance, take from the poor by violence, or despoil the rich under the name of honor, so that even to their own sons, to whom the paternal inheritance is owed, they ought to leave nothing except what was left to them by their parents; […]

46:19.t: And he brought me in by the entrance that was at the side (or behind the back) of the gate into the chambers of the sanctuary for the priests (or exedras, and cells) that faced toward the north, and behold, there was a place sloping toward the west (or toward the sea, and, as the Seventy translated, separated); and he said to me: This is the place where the priests will cook for trespass and for sin (or for ignorance and for sin), where they will cook the sacrifice (or manaa, and gift), so that they do not carry it out into the outer court and the people be sanctified. And he brought me out into the outer court and led me around through the four corners of the court, and behold, there was a little court in a corner of the court, a little court in each corner of the court. In the four corners of the court little courts were laid out, of forty cubits in length and thirty in breadth: the four were of one measure. […]

46:20.t: But what follows: 'So that they do not carry it out into the outer court and the people be sanctified, the people who had not been prepared for sanctification', signifies this: that we should not readily give holy things to the unsanctified; that we should not, according to the Gospel, cast pearls before swine nor give what is holy to dogs — indeed Moses wishes the people to be sanctified for three days from all uncleanness and from the embrace of wives, so that they may approach Mount Sinai and, sanctified, receive holy things. But if those about to approach to hear and receive the words of God are commanded to be sanctified from their wives, it is manifest that that apostolic saying too is contained in the law: Do not defraud one another, except perhaps by consent for a time, that you may be free for prayer; and that by consent one must abstain from wives, that we may be free for prayer —.

46:21.t: After this it is written: And he brought me out into the outer court and led me around through the four corners of the court, and behold, there was a little court in a corner of the court, a little court in each corner of the court; in the four little courts of the corner, little courts laid out; that man whom he often mentions brought him out of the place of the priests which sloped toward the north, or which was separated, where the priests cook for trespass and for sin or ignorance; and he brought him out into the outer court: from which we understand that the court from which he went out was the inner one, and that there are many courts in the holy Scriptures — of which we read: You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God, and in John: And other sheep I have, which are not 'of this court'; […]

46:22.t: And that the four little courts which occupied the corners of the greater court were of one measure signifies the four quarters of the world: that we eat bread in the sweat of our face and all our labor profits the belly and the dung.

46:23.t: And these four little courts one wall also encircled: And kitchens were built beneath the porticoes all around, or they had couches nearby, so that where the food was, there was also the preparing of the tables.

46:24.t: And lest the prophet perhaps not know what he was seeing, he said to him: This is the house of the kitchens, in which the ministers of the Lord will cook the victims of the people: victims of the people indeed, which are offered for trespass or for sin and ignorance, but nourishment and refreshment for the priests, so that they may remember that they ought to desire nothing else, since even in the temple refreshments for their flesh have been prepared.

47:1.t: Further, what says He? "And there was a river flowing on the right, and from it arose beautiful trees; and whosoever shall eat of them shall live for ever." This meaneth, that we indeed descend into the water full of sins and defilement, but come up, bearing fruit in our heart, having the fear [of God] and trust in Jesus in our spirit. "And whosoever shall eat of these shall live for ever," This meaneth: Whosoever, He declares, shall hear thee speaking, and believe, shall live for ever.
47:1.s: The Epistle of Barnabas, Chapter XI

47:1.t: When the world falls into sin, nothing but a flood of waters can cleanse it again.

And he turned me to the gate of the house, and behold, waters were going out beneath the threshold of the house toward the east; for the face of the house looked toward the east, and the waters were going down into the right side of the temple, to the south of the altar. And he led me out by the way of the gate of the north, and he turned me to the way outside, to the outer gate, the way that looked toward the east; and behold, waters overflowing from the right side. When the man who had a cord in his hand went out toward the east, he both measured a thousand cubits and led me across through the water up to the ankles (or he passed over in water, water of remission). And again he measured a thousand, and led me across through the water up to the knees (or and he passed over in water, water up to the thighs). And he measured a thousand, and led me across through the water up to the kidneys (or and he passed over the water up to the loins). […]

47:2.t: But what follows: And he led me out by the way of the gate of the north, and turned to the way outside, to the outer gate, the way that looked toward the east, secretly shows that we cannot come at once to the eastern gate unless we come to it by the way of the gate of the north, by a long circuit: for unless we overcome the coldest wind by the heat of faith and trample its regions — so that that apostolic saying may be fulfilled in us: But God will crush Satan under your feet swiftly —, we are not able to enter the gate through which the waters enter and are on the right side; and note that these waters, which go out through the gate of the east, flee the left-hand parts to such a degree that they are described as proceeding from the right of the altar toward the south.

47:3.t: 'But that man who had the cord in his hand, when he had led me through the gate of the north, outside, to the way that looked toward the east, and he himself too was in the same place, measured a thousand cubits of the same water'. And he led me across through the water up to the 'ankles' — which Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion translated ἀστραγάλους [anklebones] — (for which the Seventy translated: But he passed over in water, water of remission), which we can understand to signify the first sins of men, which are remitted to us as we enter the waters of the Lord, and they show the saving grace of baptism, and are the beginnings of progress; finally, they reach as far as the ankles, which are neighbors to the sole and the heel — which lies open to the bites of the snake, as the Lord says: You shall watch for his head, and he shall watch for your heel; […]
